# HCC hypothesis and Harbor experiment

Status: proposed design, not an executed study. This file records the Lead's scientific deliverable and the exact HCC bindings. The bounded counts below are feasibility diagnostics, not endpoint results.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important opening is the boundary between a transient post-embolization laboratory flare and a clinically meaningful loss of hepatic reserve after TACE. The strongest inspected evidence supports three narrower claims: baseline hepatic reserve is associated with post-locoregional-therapy decompensation [K1]; a baseline Child-Pugh/APRI/FIB-4 nomogram can predict an acute post-intervention hepatic-dysfunction label in a small internal-validation cohort [K2]; and liver-function measurements before and five days after TACE can distinguish acute injury patterns [K3]. None of those claims establishes that a within-patient, multianalyte trajectory observed during the first seven days after TACE improves prediction of a later clinical decompensation event beyond baseline reserve and treatment context.

Primary hypothesis: among adult HCC patients with a first recorded TACE in the observable HCC history and no documented decompensation before that TACE, a 0–7-day trajectory dominated by worsening synthetic/renal reserve (total bilirubin, albumin, INR/PT ratio, creatinine and sodium, with platelet count as a portal-hypertension proxy) predicts a new decompensation-coded admission after the index discharge and between days 8 and 90 better than a prespecified baseline-only model. A short-lived AST/ALT rise without synthetic/renal deterioration is the leading rival pattern: it may represent expected hepatocellular injury or measurement intensity rather than impending decompensation.

This is a predictive/descriptive hypothesis, not a causal claim that TACE caused the event or that changing a laboratory value would prevent it. If supported, the substantive advance is evidence that post-procedure surveillance should distinguish a reserve-loss trajectory from an enzyme-only flare and that a simple baseline risk estimate may be insufficient for post-TACE follow-up. It would justify expert review and prospective validation of a small early-warning rule; it would not by itself justify withholding TACE or changing treatment.

The closest relevant work actually inspected is [K1]–[K3]. The novelty claim is deliberately bounded: I did not perform an exhaustive literature review, and this is not a reproduction of any cited paper. The advance is the explicit incremental, held-out test of routine-care multiday trajectories against a baseline comparator and clinically later outcome, in a longitudinal HCC-only source where imaging pixels, exact external dates, assay units and adjudicated outcomes are unavailable.

## Leading explanation and rivals

The leading explanation is early post-TACE loss of effective hepatic reserve: coordinated bilirubin/albumin/coagulation/renal changes should precede decompensation-coded care more specifically than an isolated aminotransferase peak.

Rivals with different predictions are:

1. Baseline severity: patients with poor reserve already have higher event risk; the post-TACE trajectory will add little after baseline labs, diagnoses and prior utilization are included.
2. Surveillance/measurement intensity: patients who are about to deteriorate have more labs and encounters, so apparent trajectory value will disappear after lab-count/timing features and negative-control tests.
3. Treatment selection and technical intensity: procedure subtype, extent and patient selection drive both laboratory change and outcomes. The observational design cannot identify a treatment effect; include procedure-context covariates and do not interpret coefficients causally.
4. Expected transient injury: AST/ALT can rise after embolization without subsequent clinical decompensation. A model whose signal is limited to this pattern should not be described as a reserve-loss mechanism.

The data can separate baseline severity from early trajectory, and can partially test measurement intensity and enzyme-only alternatives. It cannot identify ischemia, embolic territory, drug dose, inflammatory mechanism, or causal treatment harm.

## Exact population, temporal boundaries and estimands

Use only the HCC dataset. The source encounter table observed dates from 2010-07-27 through 2026-01-01 in the bounded scan; therefore require a complete 90-day observable follow-up and exclude index TACE dates after 2025-10-03, unless Harbor computes a later administrative maximum from the same frozen source and applies the equivalent 90-day rule.

Index procedure: the first observed procedure per patient whose 手术 contains one of TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞, or 动脉化疗栓塞, with a parseable 开始时间 and a join to an encounters row. Require an HCC diagnosis before or on the index encounter using transparent exact/regex flags in diagnoses.诊断名称 (at minimum 肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤), and age >=18 from encounters.年龄 at index. A sensitivity analysis should restrict to procedure names containing explicit chemotherapy embolization/TACE and exclude bland embolization terms; record both cohorts.

Exclude patients with a pre-index decompensation flag at any prior or index encounter: explicit diagnoses containing 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎, or 黄疸, plus a separately reported broader 肝硬化失代偿 flag. The flag is a screening phenotype, not a validated diagnosis. Do not exclude a patient solely for missing labs; missingness is part of the feature report.

Time zero is the earliest matched TACE 手术.开始时间. Baseline is the closest usable lab in [-14 days, 0] before time zero, with a secondary baseline window [-30 days, 0]. The trajectory window is [0, 7 days] after time zero; retain the exact local timestamps and the number/timing of observations. To avoid label leakage, do not use data after day 7 in features. Start the primary outcome clock at the later of index encounter 出院时间 and time zero + 7 days; count only a new encounter admission after the index discharge. The primary estimand is the test-set difference in calibrated risk and discrimination between the baseline-only model and the dynamic model for a new decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90. A prespecified short-horizon secondary outcome uses days 8–30.

Primary outcome: a new post-discharge encounter containing a decompensation flag in diagnoses.诊断名称, using the high-specificity terms above, with a sensitivity definition requiring the same concept in clinical_documents.入院诊断, 出院诊断, 入院情况, 出院情况, or 诊疗经过. Report separate component outcomes (ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, jaundice) and the composite. A new admission is not automatically unplanned; the source does not provide a validated planned/unplanned field. Secondary outcomes are (a) any new admission in days 8–90, (b) repeat TACE-like procedure in days 8–90, and (c) a documented liver-reserve deterioration phenotype without a decompensation code. The latter is exploratory and cannot substitute for the primary clinical endpoint.

The bounded diagnostic found 17,944 patients with a first TACE-like procedure under a broader procedure regex, 6,002 with a later admission within 90 days, 171 with a later broad decompensation-coded encounter and 58 within 30 days. These figures include no final baseline exclusion, no adjudication and a broad lexical screen; Harbor must recompute them from the frozen data and report denominators.

vitals, transfers and front_page are not inputs: their schemas contain only 患者主索引 and 就诊号 and the catalog marks them identifier-only. pathology is not required for the primary model; it can support an adjudication sample using 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, but it has no timestamp. Do not join any MIMIC or eICU source and do not infer equivalence from matching identifiers.

Laboratory features must be assay-specific. The catalog states that numeric lab results have no separate unit column; therefore do not pool numeric thresholds across assays or compute a clinically valid ALBI/MELD unless an expert verifies units and the exact assay mappings. Candidate exact 检验 names observed in the bounded sample include 总胆红素, 直接胆红素, 白蛋白, 血小板计数, 凝血酶原时间, 凝血酶原时间比值, 肌酐, 钠, 丙氨酸氨基转移酶, 天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶/谷草转氨酶, and 甲胎蛋白. Harbor must freeze the exact name dictionary after a schema/value audit, parse only numeric 定量结果, retain qualitative values separately, and use within-assay standardized deltas or ranks when units are unresolved. Candidate lab names are not evidence that every patient has every assay.

Medication features are exposure proxies only: prior/around-index use of diuretics, lactulose, antibiotics, albumin and antiviral agents, plus count and route; do not infer adherence or indication. Orders and examinations can provide measurement intensity and imaging/report context. Narrative text is not automatically a diagnosis: the catalog says the local lexical detector is unvalidated and supports only limited explicit context flags for cirrhosis. All primary endpoint flags require transparent string rules plus a blinded clinician adjudication sample before clinical interpretation.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

### Simple baseline

Fit a patient-level, temporally split regularized logistic regression for the primary binary outcome using only information available at time zero: age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus and prior-decompensation flags, counts of prior encounters/procedures/medications/orders, TACE name/source, and the closest pre-index assay-specific lab levels plus missingness indicators. Add a fixed, prespecified baseline-only variant with the same variables but no labs to quantify laboratory contribution. Do not fit ALBI or Child-Pugh from unverified local units. Use standardized training-set transformations only.

### Mechanistic alternative

Fit a multivariate measurement-error state-space model on the same patients and same base covariates. The latent state is an unobserved hepatic reserve/injury state with a slow reserve component and a transient injury component; assay-specific observations from 0–7 days update the state, with irregular sampling and missingness explicitly modeled. The model must report posterior state trajectories and separate the contribution of (i) synthetic/renal reserve indicators (bilirubin, albumin, INR/PT, creatinine, sodium, platelets) from (ii) AST/ALT enzyme-flare indicators. The outcome head predicts the day-8-to-90 composite using only the posterior state at day 7 and the same baseline covariates. This is a mechanistic representation of competing explanations, not proof of a biological pathway.

The information the alternative may reveal that the baseline loses is whether coordinated reserve deterioration, rather than a single baseline level or isolated enzyme peak, precedes the event; its cost is stronger modeling assumptions and sensitivity to missing/unit ambiguity. A neural temporal transformer is explicitly deferred: it could encode event ordering, but the first scientific comparison is state separation and calibration, not a small predictive gain. It can be revisited only if the state-space model is inadequate and a larger, independently held-out study has sufficient outcome support.

### Split, fitting target and uncertainty

Use index-TACE calendar splits fixed before outcome inspection: train 2010-07-27 through 2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01 through 2021-12-31, and test 2022-01-01 through 2025-10-03, with all rows from a patient in one split. If any split lacks enough events, preserve the chronological order and report the predeclared merged split rather than resampling patients randomly. Select regularization and state-space complexity on train/validation only. Fit each index patient once; do not let repeated procedures of the same patient enter the primary analysis.

Report test-set PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope and calibration-in-the-large, sensitivity/specificity at a prespecified high-sensitivity threshold, and decision-curve net benefit over clinically stated threshold probabilities. Use patient-cluster bootstrap resampling of the test set for 95% intervals, with stratified resampling only as a sensitivity analysis. Report the number of eligible patients, missingness, assay coverage, outcome events and censoring before reporting model metrics. Compare dynamic versus baseline predictions with paired patient-level bootstrap intervals. Also report the coefficient/state loading pattern and a plot/table of the posterior reserve-loss versus enzyme-flare states.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted baseline and state-space models, frozen held-out predictions, calibration/uncertainty summaries, a component-outcome table, and negative-control results. Readiness or a successful import is not a scientific result.

Approximate future Harbor resources: preprocessing and the regularized baseline should fit on 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM, likely tens of minutes after chunked CSV parsing (unmeasured). The state-space fit and bootstrap should request 16 CPUs, 64–128 GB RAM and no GPU, with a 4–8 hour budget estimate (unmeasured). The run envelope permits 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB memory, 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds; GPU use is not necessary for this tabular state-space workload. Full laboratory parsing is the dominant I/O uncertainty: the interactive scan of the 2.2-GB lab file exceeded 120 seconds, so the solver must use a managed job and checkpointed selected-column parsing.

## Falsification and interpretation

Negative controls are mandatory. First, repeat the dynamic model after permuting each patient's post-TACE lab timestamps within the 0–7-day window while preserving values and observation count; improvement that survives indicates ordering/measurement artifact. Second, use an analogous pre-index pseudo-window (days -7 to 0, with a matched prediction horizon) to test whether a purported post-TACE effect exists before treatment. Third, include lab-count/timing and encounter-count features; if the dynamic signal disappears, measurement intensity is a leading explanation. Fourth, perform a restricted analysis of patients with at least one baseline and one day-3-to-7 measurement, and a missingness-stratified analysis.

Supportive result: on the untouched temporal test set, the dynamic model improves calibration/Brier and PR-AUC over the baseline with uncertainty excluding no meaningful improvement, the reserve-loss state—not merely AST/ALT—precedes events, and the timestamp/peri-index negative controls do not reproduce the effect. This supports an incremental prognostic trajectory claim and justifies prospective validation and clinician review.

Adverse result: baseline-only performs as well or better, the dynamic advantage disappears after measurement-intensity adjustment, or the signal is confined to the enzyme-flare state. This falsifies the stated incremental reserve-loss hypothesis in this dataset; it does not show that liver tests have no clinical value.

Inconclusive result: the primary event count is too small, assay coverage is too sparse, the temporal splits lack events, calibration intervals are wide, or a clinician cannot adjudicate code-based events. This should defer the direction to a larger linked cohort rather than be reported as a null. If findings are robust only for repeat procedure or any readmission, that is a different utilization association and cannot be relabeled as decompensation.

## Claims requiring additional evidence

Computationally checkable claims are: cohort construction under the stated rules; key integrity; timestamp ordering; assay-specific feature extraction; held-out predictions; calibration/discrimination; uncertainty; negative-control behavior; and whether the dynamic model adds prognostic information.

Clinical adjudication is required for whether an encounter represents new/worsening ascites, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome or post-TACE liver failure; whether it was planned; whether the code/document is temporally and clinically valid; and whether the event reflects TACE injury versus HCC progression or another illness. The dataset lacks exact released dates outside local timestamps, validated assay units, Child-Pugh components, INR/albumin unit mapping, bilirubin assay harmonization, viral loads, ECOG status, imaging pixels, tumor measurements, embolized territory, drug/dose, portal-pressure data, death linkage and external validation. The primary study therefore cannot establish mechanism, treatment causality, mortality benefit, or a safe clinical action threshold. Those stronger claims require expert adjudication, richer procedural/imaging data, and prospective or external validation.

## Inspectable evidence

The three distinct inspected hypothesis-specific works are [K1], [K2] and [K3], with abstract-only limits preserved in the attached excerpts and key-references.json.

[K1] Sanai FM et al. Predictors and outcomes of hepatic decompensation following transarterial locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma. Scientific Reports, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-54466-4. Supports the consequence of decompensation and baseline-reserve framing; it does not test this routine-lab trajectory.

[K2] Xu L et al. Development and validation of a nomogram model for predicting acute hepatic dysfunction post-intervention in primary hepatocellular carcinoma: a retrospective case-control study. World Journal of Surgical Oncology, 2025. DOI: 10.1186/s12957-025-04100-w. Provides the baseline-only comparator precedent; its abstract reports internal rather than external validation.

[K3] You R et al. Comparison of liver injury and inflammatory response following conventional and drug-eluting bead transcatheter chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma. Discover Oncology, 2025. DOI: 10.1007/s12672-025-02286-9. Supports a day-5 laboratory injury window; it does not establish later decompensation prediction.

Reference source excerpts are hcc_ref_K1_excerpt.txt, hcc_ref_K2_excerpt.txt, and hcc_ref_K3_excerpt.txt; each is <=1 MiB, UTF-8, and explicitly labeled abstract-only.

# MIMIC-IV proposal: discordant renal recovery at ICU discharge

Status: planned, not executed. This is a prognostic observational experiment, not a causal treatment study.

## Hypothesis and importance

Among adults discharged alive from a first ICU stay lasting at least 48 hours, creatinine improvement without concurrent urine-output recovery in the final 24 hours before ICU discharge identifies excess 48-hour risk of ICU readmission or in-hospital death beyond current severity and support.

This matters because step-down decisions are made while creatinine is changing, yet creatinine can fall through dilution or reduced production and urine output is influenced by treatment and documentation. [K1] supports creatinine and urine output as complementary AKI criteria but does not establish this discharge-risk phenotype. [K2] reports measured-clearance evidence that creatinine-based eGFR can overestimate function after ICU muscle loss. [K3] reports that dynamic renal assessment can aid risk stratification while incremental biomarker benefit is modest/inconsistent. The unresolved claim is incremental, short-horizon prognostic value and reproducibility of observable discordance, not measured GFR, renal mechanism, or benefit from delaying discharge.

Rivals are creatinine artifact, urine collection/diuretic/documentation artifact, residual severity and clinician discharge selection, chronic kidney disease/renal reserve, and survivor selection. A positive result is a risk marker only; a null result with a narrow interval argues it adds little beyond severity; an imprecise result is inconclusive.

## Population and time

Use MIMIC-IV 3.1 snapshot 5126591f768df4f9d981d97d94329fd65f78a1a0e1eb7cab0332454f888ab8b6. Join hosp/patients to hosp/admissions on subject_id, then icu/icustays on subject_id and hadm_id. Retain each subject's first ICU stay, anchor_age at least 18, valid intime<outtime, los at least 2 days, and outtime no later than dischtime. Retain patients alive at ICU discharge. Set t0 to icustays.outtime. Every feature is strictly in [t0-24 hours,t0); follow-up begins at t0.

Require two creatinine observations six hours apart, the last in the feature window, and at least one urine record. Exclude or sensitivity-test renal replacement therapy before t0. Define C_peak as maximum pre-t0 creatinine, C_last as the last value in the feature window, and improvement as C_peak minus C_last at least 0.3 mg/dL. Sum nonnegative Foley/Void/Condom-Cath urine; low output is less than 400 mL per 24 hours, explicitly an unweighted proxy. Compare improved/high output (reference), improved/low output (discordant), not-improved/high, and not-improved/low.

Primary outcome is first admissions.deathtime in (t0,t0+48h] or later icustays.intime for the same subject_id and hadm_id in that interval, censored at dischtime. Secondary outcomes are each component, 7-day events, and in-hospital death. The estimand is the standardized observational risk difference between discordant and concordant groups over measured pre-index covariates, not a treatment effect.

## Baseline, learned alternative, and evaluation

B0 is penalized logistic regression for the 48-hour outcome with age, ICU LOS, peak/last creatinine, urine output, sex, admission type, last-six-hour MAP, available lactate/platelets, support indicators, and missingness indicators. B1 adds the four-level discordance group. Report standardized risks, risk difference, risk ratio, 95% intervals, Brier score, log loss, discrimination, and calibration.

The substantive alternative is a three-state multivariate hidden Markov/state-space model on 6-hour bins from ICU admission to t0, using the same routine measurements, support indicators, and missingness indicators. Fit only on training subjects and estimate last state, occupancy, transitions, and time since transition. Do not call states mechanisms. Use a fixed subject-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test split and 200 patient bootstrap intervals. If the test set has fewer than 200 subjects or 30 events, defer HMM inference and report baseline-only feasibility. The alternative can distinguish repeated discordant occupancy from transient measurement noise and fixed-threshold timing loss; it is not selected for a small AUROC gain.

Falsification checks are exposure permutation within baseline-risk/LOS/admission strata; 12- and 48-hour windows; continuous creatinine slope; weight-indexed output only if verified; sparse-documentation and RRT exclusions; creatinine-only, output-only and interaction models; a pseudo-landmark 24 hours earlier; and charting-density/ICU-type strata. Support requires a stable adjusted signal and reproducible latent transitions. Adverse results are null, explained by B0, or reversed after measurement/RRT adjustment. Inconclusive results are sparse cases, low events, unstable item sets, wide intervals, or poor state separation. Computation cannot establish true GFR, CKD, tubular injury, complete diuretic exposure, discharge rationale, mechanism, causality, or generalizability; those require adjudication or another cohort.

## Alternatives and deliverable

The deliverable is a frozen item manifest, cohort/event flow, newly fitted B0/B1 models, held-out predictions and calibration, HMM emissions/transitions/occupancy, uncertainty intervals, and falsification outputs. CPU is selected for extraction and tabular/HMM fitting (estimated 4-8 CPUs and 16-32 GiB; unverified until readiness); GPU is not required. A transformer/LSTM was deferred because it adds opacity and compute without a distinct observable. A mechanistic filtration model was deferred because cystatin C, measured GFR, fluid composition, and complete medication exposure are unavailable.

The three demonstrations were considered: Delphi suggests a longitudinal EHR adaptation but its UKB/Danish/genetic context is unavailable and unnecessary here; Oncoformer requires unavailable imaging and full text, so lab-only adaptation would not add information; ALADYNOULLI motivates the bounded latent longitudinal alternative, while original genetic inputs and reproduction are unavailable. None is claimed reproduced.

Three distinct inspected works are attached as abstract-only UTF-8 snapshots with key-references.json. No unavailable full text, supplement, MIMIC rows, cohort prevalence, model fit, or clinical adjudication is claimed.

# Cumulative hypotension duration beyond nadir as a predictor of incident AKI in eICU

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no full study result has been computed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The expert seed asks whether, at the same minimum blood pressure, longer-lasting hypotension is followed by more acute kidney injury (AKI). Inspected evidence makes a narrower claim: temporal hypotension trajectories have been associated with postoperative complications [K1], and KDIGO supplies creatinine-based AKI criteria [K2]. A randomized-target evidence synthesis shows that prognostic hypotension information cannot be interpreted as proof that raising a BP target improves AKI [K3].

Hypothesis H1: among adult eICU ICU stays with adequate early blood-pressure and creatinine ascertainment, cumulative time below MAP 65 mmHg has incremental, transportable prognostic information for a new creatinine-defined AKI event 6–48 hours after the exposure window, beyond nadir MAP, baseline/current severity, hospital, and BP/lab observation coverage.

Strong rival R1: duration is a proxy for current severity, measurement density, or treatment response. Sicker patients may have lower nadirs, longer low-MAP periods, more BP and creatinine measurements, more vasopressor changes, and more AKI. A residual association is descriptive; it does not prove renal hypoperfusion, causality, or a treatment threshold.

Clinical importance: if H1 survives these challenges, duration could improve how hypotensive episodes are summarized and how future monitoring or BP trials stratify risk. If it fails, clinicians should not treat duration as a portable renal-risk signal beyond nadir and severity. Either result changes the next study decision.

## Population, time and outcomes

Use only eICU; never join identifiers to HCC or MIMIC. Select first ICU stay per eICU uniquepid to prevent recurrent-stay leakage, with patientunitstayid as the within-eICU join key. Adults are age >=18. Index is ICU admission (unitadmitoffset=0). The primary exposure window is minutes 0–360. Require at least 12 valid BP bins and >=240 minutes from first to last covered bin; report all exclusions and never code absent observations as normotension. Exclude pre-index AKI or dialysis only for the incident-risk primary analysis; retain them in sensitivity/competing-event analyses.

Exposure is duration below MAP 65 in covered 5-minute bins, with no interpolation across gaps >10 minutes, plus nadir MAP, low-MAP area, number of episodes, first-low offset, observation count, median gap, covered-minutes fraction and BP modality. Primary valid range is MAP 20–200 mmHg; sensitivity 30–180. Use systemicmean from vitalPeriodic preferentially when both modalities occupy a bin and retain a modality flag; otherwise use noninvasivemean from vitalAperiodic. Threshold sensitivities are 60 and 70 mmHg and common-density resampling.

Primary outcome is new creatinine-defined AKI from 6–48 hours after index: >=0.3 mg/dL increase from the last valid pre-index creatinine in -24–0 minutes. Deduplicate revised lab results at the same clinical offset using the latest labresultrevisedoffset. A flagged sensitivity uses a first 0–6-hour creatinine baseline; it is never mixed invisibly with the primary cohort. Secondary outcome is >=1.5 times baseline within 7 ICU days. Audit urine output before claiming a full KDIGO endpoint; use intakeOutput and valid admission weight only if labels, units and timing pass readiness. Death, discharge, transfer, and missing follow-up are competing/censoring events, not automatic non-AKI. Report ascertainment, censoring and competing-risk/IPCW sensitivity.

## Exact available data bindings

All source archives are ordinary gzip files under the eICU snapshot (snapshot SHA-256 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec; catalog SHA-256 802870bc57f60a7adfb12f5a59267b7cba5e1d61896adb7c6b74a58a1219f14e). The following source paths are read-only:

- patient.csv.gz, table patient, source SHA-256 2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b: patientunitstayid, uniquepid, age, gender, ethnicity, hospitalid, wardid, unitadmitoffset, unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus, unittype, unitvisitnumber, admissionweight.
- vitalPeriodic.csv.gz, table vitalPeriodic, SHA-256 329b522f97f7d3d0cb4541e4fc4afc32048eb8fd0f8c9b156907f845a992906c: patientunitstayid, observationoffset, systemicmean, systemicsystolic, systemicdiastolic, heartrate, respiration; observationoffset is minutes from ICU admission.
- vitalAperiodic.csv.gz, table vitalAperiodic, SHA-256 8b23e5a50f8aabc6cb62fc69e2dcdf755a2e5649b1439a7ca413a7c5b2d5a9a0: patientunitstayid, observationoffset, noninvasivemean, noninvasivesystolic, noninvasivediastolic.
- lab.csv.gz, table lab, SHA-256 91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a: patientunitstayid, labresultoffset, labname, labresult, labresulttext, labmeasurenamesystem, labmeasurenameinterface, labresultrevisedoffset.
- infusionDrug.csv.gz, table infusionDrug, SHA-256 f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b: patientunitstayid, infusionoffset, drugname, drugrate, infusionrate, drugamount, volumeoffluid, patientweight. Use norepinephrine, vasopressin, phenylephrine and other prespecified pressor names to measure treatment response.
- intakeOutput.csv.gz, table intakeOutput, SHA-256 f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121: patientunitstayid, intakeoutputoffset, outputtotal, dialysistotal, nettotal, intakeoutputentryoffset, cellpath, celllabel, cellvaluenumeric, cellvaluetext; urine semantics are unresolved until audited.
- carePlanEOL.csv.gz, table carePlanEOL, SHA-256 8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0: patientunitstayid, cpleolsaveoffset, cpleoldiscussionoffset, activeupondischarge, for EOL sensitivity.

- apacheApsVar.csv.gz, table apacheApsVar, SHA-256 4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4: patientunitstayid, meanbp, creatinine, urine, heartrate, wbc, temperature, dialysis, vent. It has no time field and is adjustment sensitivity only.

All longitudinal joins use patientunitstayid and their table-specific offset fields; no cross-dataset identity join is permitted.

## Analysis and method comparison

B0, the simple baseline, is a regularized logistic or discrete-time risk model with nadir MAP, initial MAP/HR, pre-index creatinine and missingness/source flags, age, sex, ethnicity, admission source/ICU type, hospital and prespecified process controls (BP coverage, count, median gap, modality). B0 excludes duration and all post-index variables.

B1 adds duration_low65, low-time fraction, number of episodes and first-low offset, using a restricted spline and fixed-nadir bands. The primary estimand is the held-out difference in log loss/Brier score and calibration between B1 and B0; AUROC/AUPRC are secondary. Use 60/20/20 hospital-level train/validation/test assignment with fixed seed, all stays for one uniquepid in one split, or repeated grouped-hospital cross-validation if hospital counts are inadequate. Bootstrap uncertainty is clustered by hospital and report leave-one-hospital-out heterogeneity.

Substantive learned alternative M uses the same 0–6-hour 5-minute sequence: MAP, HR, respiration, BP modality, pressor rates/indicators, fluid/output summaries only if semantics pass, and missingness/time-since-last-observation masks. Target is the same 6–48-hour AKI label, with 7-day AKI and competing events secondary. Fit a small GRU or temporal convolution (two layers, width 32–64, dropout, calibrated logistic head) on training hospitals with early stopping on validation hospitals. The information test is whether persistence, recovery slope, repeated episodes, oscillations or BP-treatment coupling reproducibly add signal after nadir is fixed—not whether a complex model wins by a tiny AUROC margin. GPU is optional; CPU tabular fits are expected, and one allocated A100 is reasonable only if the sequence fit materially benefits. Discovery probing has measured header-read time but not full compressed parsing; future resource estimates are unverified and must be measured by the solver.

Unchosen alternatives: latent trajectory classes are deferred because class count/shape can become exploratory; a renal state-space model is deferred because eICU lacks perfusion pressure, renal oxygenation, congestion imaging and adjudicated tubular biomarkers; a large transformer is deferred because it does not test a distinct scientific uncertainty. Revisit if M is robust but unstable in pattern attribution, or if those missing measurements are later supplied.

## Falsification and interpretation

Pre-register: within-hospital permutation of duration/trajectory within nadir bins; common-density thinning; BP modality strata; thresholds 60/65/70; pre-index negative-control creatinine-rise label; post-exposure observation/lab count as process controls; treatment-masked, treatment-only and vasopressor-adjusted ablations; and strict leakage audit excluding post-index labs, discharge, EOL and actual outcome fields.

Supportive: B1 improves held-out Brier/log loss and calibration over B0 with uncertainty excluding no improvement; duration-risk is monotone within fixed nadir bands; the result persists after process/treatment adjustment, common-density resampling and hospital holdout; M finds reproducible trajectory information. This supports a portable prognostic summary only.

Adverse: duration becomes null/non-monotone after adjustment, is confined to low-density/high-monitoring patients or one hospital, or disappears with treatment adjustment. This supports R1 and argues against duration as a robust renal-risk quantity.

Inconclusive: wide intervals, poor creatinine coverage, unstable hospital holdout or exposure-dependent censoring. This is not refutation; seek label adjudication/independent validation or defer to descriptive BP-process analysis.

## Required clinical limits and deliverable

The future solver must newly fit B0, B1 and M and emit cohort flow, label ascertainment, held-out predictions, coefficient/spline estimates, calibration and uncertainty tables, fixed-nadir duration curves, hospital heterogeneity and all falsification outputs. Readiness is not a solved result.

eICU lacks clinician-adjudicated AKI, reliable pre-ICU kidney function, complete fluid balance, arterial-line calibration, renal replacement indication, clinician intent, raw waveforms, staffing/bed context and independent external validation. It cannot establish causality, mechanism, a renal autoregulatory threshold, or that treating duration prevents AKI. Nephrology/critical-care review and a prospective or external validation study are required for those claims.

The ten imported eICU seeds were assessed repairable. Deferred alternatives are hospital vasopressor heterogeneity, testing-process transportability, hyperoxia, ventilatory burden, nighttime discharge, transfers, reduced testing, insulin/nutrition hypoglycemia and hospital recovery speed; each needs its own verified outcome/binding audit. This proposal is a narrowed adaptation of seed eicu-03, not a reproduction of any cited work.

# Episode 2: measurement and endpoint validity refinement for the HCC post-TACE trajectory

Status: concrete successor design; planned Harbor experiment, not an executed analysis.

## Disposition and advance over the parent

The parent candidate remains the scientific starting point and its primary question is frozen:

> Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does a 0–7-day post-TACE laboratory trajectory add prognostic information beyond baseline for a new decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 after index discharge?

This branch does not change the population, time-zero definition, feature window, outcome window, or baseline comparison. It makes the interpretation testable by requiring two validity separations before calling a trajectory clinically meaningful:

1. assay/measurement validity: an apparent change must be traceable to a stable assay-name definition and must retain information after observation count, timing, encounter density and missingness are modeled; and
2. endpoint validity: the event must be a new post-discharge admission with a high-specificity decompensation component, not merely a diagnosis string, any readmission, repeat procedure or increased care intensity.

The parent’s bounded counts (17,944 broad first TACE-like procedures, 6,002 later admissions, 171 broad decompensation-coded encounters and 58 by day 30) are feasibility diagnostics only. They are not results and must be recomputed after the final cohort and endpoint rules.

### Three demonstrations

[K1] Sanai et al., *Predictors and outcomes of hepatic decompensation following transarterial locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma* (Scientific Reports, 2026) is retained as the clinical anchor: it supports the importance of decompensation and baseline-reserve framing. Its inspected evidence does not establish that routine 0–7-day trajectories predict later coded admission, and it does not remove the need for adjudication.

[K2] Xu et al., *Development and validation of a nomogram model for predicting acute hepatic dysfunction post-intervention in primary hepatocellular carcinoma* (World Journal of Surgical Oncology, 2025) is retained as the closest baseline-comparator precedent. It motivates a baseline-only model but is not reproduced: its acute dysfunction label, internal validation and feature/unit context do not answer the later decompensation question in this HCC source.

[K3] You et al., *Comparison of liver injury and inflammatory response following conventional and drug-eluting bead transcatheter chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma* (Discover Oncology, 2025) is retained to motivate an early, approximately day-5 injury window and the AST/ALT-flare rival. It does not establish later decompensation prediction or distinguish biological injury from measurement intensity.

The inspected source material for all three works is abstract-only frozen evidence inherited unchanged from the parent. The parent’s key-references.json and three UTF-8 excerpts must be attached unchanged to the published child; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

## Scientific opening, rival explanations and exact claim

The strongest supported claim is narrower than the hypothesis: baseline reserve and acute post-intervention laboratory injury are clinically relevant in prior work, while their incremental relationship to later decompensation-coded care in this longitudinal source is unresolved.

Leading explanation: coordinated early deterioration in synthetic/renal reserve precedes clinically meaningful decompensation. The competing explanations are:

- baseline severity: the apparent trajectory is redundant with pre-TACE reserve and prior disease burden;
- observation/utilization: patients near an admission are measured more often, earlier and across more encounters, creating a trajectory artifact;
- assay representation: different local assays or qualitative/numeric mixtures create non-comparable changes;
- transient injury: AST/ALT rises are expected after embolization and do not imply later decompensation;
- endpoint ascertainment: diagnosis coding or documentation density makes a later “event” a utilization/recording artifact.

The experiment can test incremental prognostic/descriptive regularity and its robustness to these artifacts. It cannot establish that TACE caused decompensation, that the latent state is a biological mechanism, or that acting on a predicted risk improves outcomes.

## Exact population and temporal estimand

Use only HCC. The index is each patient's first observed procedure per patient whose \`手术\` contains one of the parent’s TACE-like terms (TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞, 动脉化疗栓塞), with parseable \`开始时间\` and a matching \`就诊号\` in encounters. Require age >=18 from encounters. Require an HCC diagnosis before or on the index encounter using transparent rules on \`诊断名称\` (at minimum 肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤). Report an explicit-chemotherapy/TACE sensitivity cohort excluding bland-embolization wording.

Exclude any prior or index encounter with the parent’s high-specificity decompensation screen: 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎 or 黄疸. Report, but do not silently use as exclusion, a broader 肝硬化失代偿 flag. Missing laboratory data never excludes a patient.

Time zero is the earliest matched index \`手术.开始时间\`. Baseline is the closest usable assay-specific laboratory result in [-14, 0] days before time zero; [-30, 0] is a prespecified sensitivity window. Features may use only [0, 7] days after time zero. The primary outcome clock is [8, 90] days after time zero and also must be after the index encounter’s \`出院时间\`; the eligible event is the first distinct post-discharge encounter with an admission time in that interval. If discharge is missing, report the case and do not silently treat an encounter-date string as discharge. Index and same-admission rows are not new admissions.

The estimand is the paired, temporal-test-set difference in calibrated prognostic performance between a baseline-only model and the dynamic model for the binary composite outcome. Secondary estimands are the same difference for days 8–30 and for each endpoint component. This is not a treatment effect.

## Exact source bindings, tables, joins and fields

All joins stay inside HCC and use the documented composite key (患者主索引, 就诊号). Verify duplicate-key rates before aggregation; aggregate observations to patient-index-TACE level only after preserving raw timestamps. No MIMIC/eICU joins and no identifier matching across datasets.

Required ordinary CSV inputs and exact fields:

- diagnoses: [private-path]/data_诊断_7504718184492840569.csv, SHA-256 7065658050118649870327351adfa9982d68718fe22246b981fec302d3302c7e. Use 患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称, 诊断类型.

- orders: [private-path]/data_医嘱(非药品)_2062526727266216118.csv, SHA-256 24a6356b5c259e0573e75163e27d3eea15592c7691ed68f8e0979ac3c358c3d1. Use 患者主索引, 就诊号, 医嘱(非药品), 开立时间, 开始时间, 结束时间, 医嘱期限, 医嘱状态, 频次.

vitals, transfers and front_page are not used because their available schemas are identifier-only. pathology is not required for modeling and has no timestamp; it may be used only in an explicitly labeled adjudication sample if its fields are available. The exact HCC README/catalog is the authority for these availability limits; no unavailable clinical measure is inferred.

## Assay-measurement validity protocol

The labs table has no separate unit column. Therefore the solver must not pool numeric thresholds across assays, compute a clinically valid ALBI/MELD/Child-Pugh score, or call a numeric change a physiologic reserve change without external assay verification.

Before fitting, freeze an assay dictionary from the observed \`检验\` values. Candidate parent names requiring audit include 总胆红素, 直接胆红素, 白蛋白, 血小板计数, 凝血酶原时间, 凝血酶原时间比值, 肌酐, 钠, 丙氨酸氨基转移酶, 天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶/谷草转氨酶 and 甲胎蛋白. The dictionary must record exact normalized name, raw-name variants, numeric-versus-qualitative coverage, specimen type, timestamp coverage, duplicate rate and whether an expert-confirmed unit mapping exists. The candidate list is not a claim that each assay is present for every patient.

Use only parseable numeric \`定量结果\` for numeric trajectory features; retain \`定性结果\` as a separate missing/qualitative indicator and never coerce it to a number. For an assay with no verified unit, use within-assay training-set standardized values and within-patient changes/ranks only; do not compare raw values across names, hospitals, periods or specimen types. If a clinically verified unit mapping becomes available, prespecify a unit-harmonized sensitivity analysis but retain the unit-agnostic primary analysis. Same-day duplicate results are retained for audit; the primary aggregation uses the result nearest a fixed daily grid (days 0, 1–2, 3–4, 5–7) with an explicit deterministic tie rule, while a sensitivity analysis uses all timestamped observations in the state-space model.

Report, before model metrics, assay coverage at baseline and in days 0–7, unit/qualitative ambiguity, missingness, number of unique assay names, duplicate observations, out-of-range/non-numeric exclusions and whether trajectory direction can be clinically named. If the audit cannot establish comparability for a proposed panel, the output may say only “assay-indexed trajectory”; it must not say “hepatic reserve loss.”

## Utilization and observation-process controls

Construct these from fields available before outcome ascertainment:

- baseline utilization: counts of encounters, admissions, distinct departments, procedures, medications, orders, examinations and laboratory observations in [-90,0) and [-30,0);
- early observation process: number of unique lab timestamps, number of distinct encounters with any lab, number of distinct lab assays, first post-TACE lab lag, last observed day, counts in days 0–2, 3–4 and 5–7, and number of encounters/clinical-document rows in each bin;
- index intensity/context: index admission length when both 入院时间 and 出院时间 parse, procedure source, procedure duration when available, department, and medication/order counts in [0,7].

These variables are controls and diagnostics, not evidence that utilization causes decompensation. Fit a measurement-only model using observation-process variables; add the same controls to the baseline and dynamic models; and report a common-support analysis requiring at least one baseline and one day-3–7 lab. Missingness indicators remain features. A sensitivity analysis stratifies by observation density and uses a pattern-mixture analysis; inverse observation weighting may be reported only if its weights are estimated in the training split and overlap is shown.

The key validity comparison is: trajectory increment without utilization controls, trajectory increment with controls, and the same comparison after restricting to common observation support. A trajectory signal that vanishes in the latter two comparisons is classified as utilization-compatible, not clinically meaningful.

## Endpoint validity protocol

Primary composite: a first distinct post-discharge encounter with admission time in days 8–90 and a high-specificity decompensation flag in diagnoses. Component flags are mutually reported, not silently collapsed: ascites (腹水), encephalopathy (肝性脑病), gastrointestinal/variceal bleeding (消化道出血 or 食管胃底静脉曲张 with bleeding context), renal/hepatic failure (肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭 or 肝功能衰竭), and jaundice (黄疸). Define the composite as any component, retain component-specific first dates, and report the number with one versus multiple components.

The primary lexical endpoint uses 诊断名称 only with transparent normalized exact/substring rules frozen before modeling. A sensitivity endpoint requires the same component in at least one of 入院诊断, 出院诊断, 入院情况, 出院情况 or 诊疗经过 in clinical_documents for the same (患者主索引, 就诊号). Report diagnosis-only positive, document-confirmed positive, discordant, and missing-document strata. A code/document string is a screening phenotype, not a validated diagnosis.

Do not label any admission unplanned: the source has no validated planned/unplanned field. Report repeat TACE-like procedure in days 8–90 separately, and report any admission separately. If the signal occurs only for any admission or repeat TACE, it is a utilization/treatment-pathway association, not evidence for decompensation.

The solver must produce an adjudication packet for a blinded clinician sample stratified by composite positive, component, diagnosis/document discordance and negative controls. Adjudication should determine new/worsening decompensation, planned status, temporal relation to TACE, competing illness/HCC progression and whether the text supports the component. The computational experiment cannot establish these clinical facts.

## Models, split and deliverables

Preserve the parent’s comparable alternatives:

- Baseline comparator: patient-level regularized logistic regression, chronological split by index date (train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31; validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31; test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, or equivalent later cutoff after checking the frozen source maximum). Inputs are time-zero age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, prior utilization, closest baseline assay-specific values and missingness. A no-lab baseline variant quantifies laboratory contribution.
- Learned/mechanistic alternative: the parent’s multivariate measurement-error state-space model with slow reserve and transient injury states, irregular timestamps and missingness. Its outcome head uses only the day-7 posterior and the same baseline covariates. It must separately expose reserve-panel versus AST/ALT-flare loadings. The representation is not proof of mechanism.
- Incremental measurement-validity models: baseline-only; baseline plus baseline labs; baseline plus utilization/observation controls; dynamic trajectory without controls; dynamic trajectory with controls; state-space dynamic model; and a measurement-only model. The primary comparison remains baseline-only versus dynamic-with-controls on the untouched temporal test set.

Fit patients once and keep all rows from a patient in one split. Choose regularization and state-space complexity using train/validation only. If event counts make a state-space fit unstable, preserve the question and report the predeclared penalized grouped-trajectory model as a feasibility fallback; do not substitute an easier endpoint or claim a null from a failed fit. The fallback must estimate assay-specific baseline-to-window changes, observation process and enzyme-only versus reserve-panel blocks with shrinkage.

Required outputs are: cohort flow and key-integrity audit; frozen assay dictionary and coverage/ambiguity table; endpoint component and diagnosis/document concordance table; held-out predictions for every model; PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope and calibration-in-the-large, sensitivity/specificity at a prespecified high-sensitivity threshold, decision-curve net benefit and paired patient-bootstrap 95% intervals; component-outcome results; utilization-adjusted versus unadjusted increments; common-support and missingness-stratified results; timestamp-permutation and pre-index pseudo-window results; and an adjudication packet. Readiness/import success is not a scientific result.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted baseline and dynamic models plus these validity audits and frozen held-out outputs. Approximate parent resource estimates are retained: preprocessing/baseline on 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM; state-space/bootstrap about 16 CPUs and 64–128 GB RAM for 4–8 hours, no GPU required. These estimates are unmeasured. The 2.2-GB lab file requires a managed, checkpointed selected-column parse under the configured 16 CPU/262,144 MiB/28,800-second envelope.

## Falsification and interpretation rules

Negative controls are diagnostics, not automatic proof of causality:

1. Within-patient permutation of post-TACE lab timestamps preserves values, counts and missingness but destroys temporal ordering. Dynamic improvement that survives is evidence for value/measurement intensity rather than ordered trajectory.
2. A pre-index pseudo-window (days -7 to 0) with a matched prediction horizon tests whether the same “post-TACE” signal exists before treatment. Similar performance weakens a post-TACE interpretation.
3. A measurement-only model and the unadjusted-versus-adjusted comparison test whether lab/visit density explains the increment.
4. Repeat TACE and any-admission outcomes test specificity. Stronger association only for these outcomes is not decompensation evidence.
5. AST/ALT-only versus reserve-panel-only blocks test the expected transient-injury rival. AST/ALT-only signal without reserve-panel or endpoint specificity should be classified as flare/utilization-compatible.

Supportive result: the reserve-panel trajectory improves held-out calibration/discrimination over the prespecified baseline comparator with uncertainty excluding a practically negligible increment; the increment persists after observation controls, common-support restriction, timestamp permutation does not reproduce it, the pre-index pseudo-window is weak, and document-confirmed/component patterns are directionally consistent. This supports an incremental prognostic regularity, not mechanism or treatment causality.

Adverse result: the increment disappears after assay audit, controls or common-support restriction; survives timestamp permutation; is reproduced in the pre-index pseudo-window; is driven only by AST/ALT; or predicts any admission/repeat TACE without component specificity. This supports measurement, selection, transient injury or utilization explanations and should revise or abandon a “reserve-loss” interpretation.

Inconclusive result: too few events, split imbalance, poor assay coverage, unstable endpoint concordance, wide paired intervals, or failed state-space convergence. Preserve the estimand and report uncertainty; defer clinical interpretation to adjudication or a linked/external cohort rather than calling it a null.

Computationally checkable claims are cohort rules, joins, timestamps, assay handling, model fitting, held-out metrics, uncertainty and negative-control behavior. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for true decompensation, planned status, causal TACE injury, biological reserve mechanism, mortality benefit, safe action thresholds and external validity. Missing evidence includes verified assay units, imaging/tumor burden, embolized territory and drug/dose, ECOG, portal pressure, death linkage, external validation and prospective adjudication.

## Unchosen alternatives and revisit criteria

A transformer/neural sequence model remains deferred because the immediate scientific uncertainty is whether the observed increment survives assay and utilization controls; its additional temporal capacity would not resolve that validity question. Revisit it only if the state-space/grouped model is adequate, outcome support is larger, assay names are harmonized, and an independent temporal or external test set is available. GPU use is not prohibited but is unnecessary for this tabular state-space workload. A simple baseline remains mandatory because it establishes whether complexity adds clinically interpretable information rather than a small predictive gain.

# Cumulative systemic hypotension duration beyond nadir as a predictor of incident creatinine-defined AKI in eICU

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no full study result has been computed. This is an episode-2 substantive child of candidate-cf876a27c00e81f2d6d28ddb.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The expert seed eicu-03 asks whether, at the same minimum blood pressure, longer-lasting hypotension precedes more AKI. Inspected prior evidence supports only narrower premises: temporal hypotension trajectories have been associated with postoperative complications [K1]; KDIGO provides creatinine-based AKI criteria [K2]; and randomized BP-target evidence warns that prognostic hypotension associations do not establish that raising a BP target improves AKI [K3]. The unresolved claim is incremental, transportable prognostic information, not a causal treatment effect.

H1: among adult eICU ICU stays with adequate early BP and creatinine ascertainment, cumulative covered time with systemic mean arterial pressure (MAP) below 65 mmHg during ICU minutes 0-360 predicts a new creatinine-defined AKI event during minutes 360-2880 beyond nadir systemic MAP, baseline/current severity and observation coverage, and retains information under hospital-held-out evaluation.

Strong rival R1: duration is a proxy for current severity, measurement density, treatment response, or imminent care transition. A residual association would remain descriptive; it would not prove renal hypoperfusion, a physiologic threshold, causality, or that treating duration prevents AKI.

Clinical importance: if H1 survives process, treatment and transportability checks, duration may be a useful risk-summary variable for monitoring and for stratifying future BP trials. If it collapses after those checks, duration should not be treated as a portable renal-risk signal. Both outcomes change the next research decision.

## Population and time boundaries

Use eICU only. Join all tables on patientunitstayid; never join identifiers to HCC or MIMIC. Select the first ICU stay per uniquepid (lowest unitvisitnumber, then earliest unitadmittime24 where needed) to limit recurrent-stay leakage. Adults are age >=18; eICU age strings such as > 89 must be handled by a prespecified documented rule and sensitivity analysis. Index is ICU admission, with longitudinal offsets measured from admission.

Primary exposure window: minutes 0-360. Require at least 12 valid 5-minute bins and at least 240 minutes between first and last covered bin. Do not treat absent measurements as normotension. Use systemicmean from vitalPeriodic, not pamean (the latter is pulmonary artery mean); when systemicmean and noninvasivemean are both available in a bin, preferentially retain systemicmean and record a modality flag, otherwise use noninvasivemean from vitalAperiodic. Accept MAP 20-200 mmHg in the primary analysis; sensitivity 30-180. Do not interpolate across gaps >10 minutes. Compute covered minutes, observation count, median gap, BP modality and missingness.

Exposure variables are covered time below 65, low-time fraction, nadir systemic MAP, low-MAP area below 65, number of low episodes, first-low offset and recovery slope. Threshold sensitivities are 60 and 70 mmHg and common-density resampling.

Primary outcome: new creatinine-defined AKI in minutes 360-2880 (6-48 hours), defined as >=0.3 mg/dL increase from the last valid pre-index creatinine in minutes -24-0. Deduplicate same-clinical-offset revised results by retaining the latest labresultrevisedoffset. Require the lab value to be numeric and audit labname plus labmeasurenamesystem/labmeasurenameinterface and units before accepting it as serum creatinine. A prespecified sensitivity uses a 0-6 hour baseline and is reported as a distinct cohort. Secondary outcome is >=1.5 times baseline within 7 ICU days. Audit urine output before any full KDIGO claim; intakeOutput is not automatically urine and its semantics must be validated.

Death, ICU discharge, transfer and absent follow-up are competing/censoring events, not automatic non-AKI. Report ascertainment and censoring; use competing-risk and IPCW sensitivity analyses. Exclude pre-index AKI or dialysis only for the incident-risk primary analysis, while retaining those stays in descriptive and competing-event sensitivities. carePlanEOL is a sensitivity covariate/exclusion flag, not evidence of clinician intent.

## Verified source bindings

The read-only snapshot is eICU 2.0 with snapshot SHA-256 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476e89543643c08b7df637a15ec and catalog SHA-256 802870bc57f60a7adfb12f5a59267b7cba5e1d61896adb7c6b74a58a1219f14c. Archive members are the uncompressed CSV members named below.

- patient.csv.gz, table patient, SHA-256 2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b: patientunitstayid, patienthealthsystemstayid, uniquepid, age, gender, ethnicity, hospitalid, wardid, hospitaladmitoffset, hospitaladmitsource, unitadmittime24, unitadmitsource, unitvisitnumber, unitstaytype, admissionweight, unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus, unittype. Use unitadmit fields and do not invent a missing unitadmitoffset.
- vitalPeriodic.csv.gz, table vitalPeriodic, SHA-256 329b522f97f7d3d0cb4541e4fc4afc32048eb8fd0f8c9b156907f845a992906c, member vitalPeriodic.csv: patientunitstayid, observationoffset, systemicmean, systemicsystolic, systemicdiastolic, heartrate, respiration, plus pamean. Only systemicmean is the primary systemic MAP field.
- vitalAperiodic.csv.gz, table vitalAperiodic, SHA-256 8b23e5a50f8aabc6cb62fc69e2dcdf755a2e5649b1439a7ca413a7c5b2d5a9a0, member vitalAperiodic.csv: patientunitstayid, observationoffset, noninvasivemean, noninvasivesystolic, noninvasivediastolic.
- lab.csv.gz, table lab, SHA-256 91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a, member lab.csv: patientunitstayid, labresultoffset, labname, labresult, labresulttext, labmeasurenamesystem, labmeasurenameinterface, labresultrevisedoffset.
- infusionDrug.csv.gz, table infusionDrug, SHA-256 f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b, member infusionDrug.csv: patientunitstayid, infusionoffset, drugname, drugrate, infusionrate, drugamount, volumeoffluid, patientweight. Use prespecified pressor names only after name audit; infusion rows represent recorded treatment, not randomized treatment.
- hospital.csv.gz, table hospital, SHA-256 16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6, member hospital.csv: hospitalid, numbedscategory, teachingstatus, region.
- carePlanEOL.csv.gz, table carePlanEOL, SHA-256 8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0, member carePlanEOL.csv: patientunitstayid, cpleolsaveoffset, cpleoldiscussionoffset, activeupondischarge.
- apacheApsVar.csv.gz, table apacheApsVar, SHA-256 4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4, member apacheApsVar.csv: patientunitstayid, intubated, vent, dialysis, urine, heartrate, meanbp, creatinine, bun and other admission-summary fields. It has no time field; use only an adjustment sensitivity, never as a time-aligned exposure/outcome.
- intakeOutput.csv.gz, table intakeOutput, SHA-256 f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121, member intakeOutput.csv: patientunitstayid, intakeoutputoffset, outputtotal, dialysistotal, nettotal, intakeoutputentryoffset, cellpath, celllabel, cellvaluenumeric, cellvaluetext. Use only if cell labels/units/timing validate urine semantics.

All table-specific offsets are minutes from ICU admission, except revised offsets and entry offsets whose meaning must be preserved. There is no permitted cross-dataset patient join.

## Baseline, substantive alternative and estimand

B0 is a prespecified regularized logistic model for the same 6-48 hour AKI target using nadir systemic MAP, initial MAP/HR, pre-index creatinine, age, sex, ethnicity, hospital/ICU type and BP source/missingness/process controls. It excludes duration and all post-index variables.

B1 adds duration below 65, low-time fraction, episode count and recovery features with a restricted spline and fixed-nadir bands. The primary estimand is the held-out incremental log loss, Brier score and calibration of B1 over B0, with hospital-clustered bootstrap intervals and AUROC/AUPRC secondary. Assign whole hospitals 60/20/20 to train/validation/test; if too few hospitals, use repeated grouped-hospital cross-validation and state the limitation. Keep all stays for one uniquepid in one split.

M is a small GRU or temporal convolution over the same 0-6 hour 5-minute sequence: systemic/noninvasive MAP, HR, respiration, modality and time-since-last-observation masks, pressor indicators/rates and pre-index severity. Fluid/output summaries enter only if their semantics pass readiness. Fit only on training hospitals, early-stop on validation hospitals, calibrate on validation data, and evaluate once on held-out hospitals. M can reveal whether persistence, recovery slope, oscillation or BP-treatment coupling carries reproducible information that B0 discards; B0 supplies transparent incremental duration estimates and is harder to overfit. Neither separates causal renal hypoperfusion from unmeasured illness.

The method choice is substantive: if B1’s fixed-duration signal is robust and M adds no reproducible trajectory information, retain the interpretable duration summary; if M adds stable trajectory information beyond B1, revise the clinical summary rather than merely report a tiny predictive gain; if both fail after common-density and process adjustment, defer the direction. GPU is optional. Tabular fits should run on CPU; a bounded one-A100 sequence fit is permitted only if measured parsing/training time justifies it. Future solver planning envelope is 16 CPU, up to 8 GPU, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not execute the full study and does not claim those resources are measured.

Deferred alternatives: latent trajectory classes are deferred because class number/shape would be exploratory; a renal mechanistic state-space model is deferred because these files lack perfusion pressure, congestion imaging, renal biomarkers and clinician-adjudicated tubular injury; a large transformer is deferred because it does not test a distinct uncertainty. Revisit only with new measurements or unstable, reproducible trajectory evidence.

## Falsification and interpretation

Pre-register: within-hospital permutation of trajectory within nadir bands; common-density thinning; systemic versus noninvasive strata; thresholds 60/65/70; a pre-index negative-control creatinine-rise label; treatment-masked, treatment-only and pressor-adjusted ablations; BP/lab coverage controls; strict exclusion of post-index labs, discharge, EOL and outcome-derived fields; and leakage audits for first-stay and hospital splits.

Supportive results require a prespecified improvement in held-out Brier/log loss and calibration for B1 over B0 with uncertainty excluding no improvement, monotonic duration-risk within fixed nadir bands, persistence after common-density/process/treatment adjustment and hospital holdout, and reproducible M trajectory information. This supports only a transportable prognostic summary.

Adverse results include null/non-monotone duration after adjustment, confinement to low-density or one-hospital data, disappearance after treatment adjustment, failure to transport, or apparent gain reproduced by a pre-index negative control. These support R1 and argue against a robust duration signal.

Inconclusive results include wide intervals, insufficient creatinine ascertainment, unstable hospital holdout, exposure-dependent censoring, or unresolved lab/urine semantics. They do not refute H1; they require label adjudication, independent validation or a narrower descriptive BP-process study.

## Deliverable and limits

The solver must newly fit B0, B1 and M and emit cohort flow, field/label audit, held-out predictions, coefficient/spline estimates, calibration and clustered uncertainty tables, fixed-nadir curves, hospital heterogeneity, process/treatment ablations, common-density and negative-control outputs, plus resource logs. Readiness is not a scientific result.

Available data lack clinician-adjudicated AKI, reliable pre-ICU kidney function, complete fluid balance, arterial-line calibration, raw waveforms, renal replacement indication/intent, staffing/bed context and independent external validation. The experiment cannot establish causality, renal mechanism, a treatment threshold, hospital quality, or benefit from changing BP. Those claims require critical-care/nephrology adjudication and a prospective or external validation study.

This is a data-bound adaptation of expert seed eicu-03, not reproduction of a demonstration paper. Other imported seeds remain deferred pending their own binding audits.

# HCC post-TACE trajectory: measurement-validity successor

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no full study or model fit has been executed.

## Question and advance

Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does an assay-indexed laboratory trajectory during days 0–7 add held-out prognostic information beyond baseline for a new post-discharge decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90? The parent established the clinically important opening: early injury may be transient, while coordinated synthetic/renal deterioration could mark later loss of reserve. This successor preserves that question but makes its interpretation falsifiable against the strongest rivals: baseline severity, observation intensity, assay/unit heterogeneity, transient AST/ALT injury, and coding/documentation artifacts.

A supportive result is only an incremental prognostic regularity. It cannot establish TACE causality, a biological latent mechanism, treatment benefit, or a safe action threshold.

## Population, time zero, estimand, and outcomes

Use only HCC. Identify each patient's first procedure row whose 手术 contains TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞, or 动脉化疗栓塞, with parseable 开始时间 and a matching encounter. Require age >=18 and an HCC diagnosis (at minimum 肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤) before/on the index encounter. Exclude prior/index high-specificity decompensation terms: 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎, or 黄疸; report broader cirrhosis-decompensation flags separately. Missing labs do not exclude patients.

Time zero is earliest qualifying 手术.开始时间. Baseline is the closest assay-specific quantitative result in [-14,0] days; [-30,0] is a sensitivity window. Dynamic features use only [0,7] days. The primary event is the first distinct encounter after the index 出院时间 whose admission time is in [8,90] days and whose diagnosis contains a prespecified high-specificity component. Missing discharge is reported, not silently converted to a new admission. Report composite plus ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, and jaundice components; also report any admission and repeat TACE as non-equivalent secondary outcomes.

The primary estimand is the paired chronological-test-set difference between a baseline-only model and a dynamic model in Brier score, calibration, discrimination, and decision-curve net benefit. This is not a treatment-effect estimand.

## Exact read-only bindings

All joins remain within HCC on (患者主索引, 就诊号); duplicate-key rates are audited before aggregation and raw timestamps are retained. These are ordinary CSVs, not archive members.

vitals and transfers are identifier-only; front_page is nominal; pathology is not required and has no timestamp. No unavailable imaging, units, tumor burden, or procedure intensity is inferred.

## Measurement and endpoint validity

Labs have no unit column. Freeze an assay dictionary from 检验 values before outcome analysis. Parse only numeric 定量结果; preserve 定性结果, 标本类型, raw-name variants, duplicate rate, timing and missingness. Use within-assay training-set standardization and within-patient changes/ranks; do not pool raw thresholds across assays or claim valid ALBI/MELD/Child-Pugh without verified units. Candidate assays include bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR, creatinine, sodium, AST/ALT and AFP, but presence and clinical comparability must be demonstrated, not assumed. Aggregate nearest observations to fixed [0,1–2,3–4,5–7] day bins with a deterministic tie rule; retain all timestamps for sensitivity/state-space analysis.

Build pre-index and early observation controls: counts of encounters, admissions, departments, procedures, medications, orders, examinations and labs; number of lab timestamps, assays, encounters with labs, first-lab lag, last observed day, and bin-specific counts. Compare dynamic models without and with these controls and restrict to common support (at least one baseline and one day 3–7 lab). A signal disappearing after controls is utilization-compatible.

The primary endpoint uses transparent diagnosis-name lexical rules. A sensitivity endpoint requires the same component in clinical_documents fields listed above. Report diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant and missing-document strata. Do not infer planned/unplanned status. Produce a blinded clinician adjudication packet to determine true new/worsening decompensation, planned status, competing illness/HCC progression, TACE injury, and text validity.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

B0 is L2-regularized logistic regression using time-zero age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, baseline assay-specific values and missingness. A no-lab B0 is a sensitivity comparator.

B1 adds prespecified [0,7] assay summaries: baseline-to-last delta, robust slope, minimum/maximum, last value, observation count, first-lab lag, missingness, and separate AST/ALT-flare blocks. Fit B0/B1 on the same one-row-per-index-patient data.

The substantive alternative is a two-factor measurement-error state-space model on the same assays and time window: a slowly varying reserve state and a transient post-procedure injury state, with assay-specific loadings/noise, irregular timestamps, missingness and duplicate handling. Predict from the day-7 posterior plus the same baseline covariates; report posterior uncertainty, loadings, reserve-versus-injury contributions, and held-out predictions. It can reveal shared temporal structure and attenuation from measurement error that B1 slopes/extrema lose, but latent states are not mechanisms. A neural sequence model is deferred because it does not directly resolve the assay and utilization rivals; revisit only after stable state-space results and an independent temporal test set.

Use train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03 or an equivalent complete-follow-up cutoff after recomputing source maxima. Keep patients in one split and tune only train/validation. Request CPU (4–8 cores, <32 GB for B0/B1; approximately 16 CPUs and 64–128 GB for state-space/bootstrap, estimated not measured); GPU is not warranted for this low-dimensional tabular likelihood.

## Falsification, uncertainty, and interpretation

Required negative controls are timestamp permutation, a matched pre-index pseudo-window, measurement-only prediction, any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes, and AST/ALT-only versus reserve-panel-only blocks. Support requires a calibrated held-out incremental signal with paired uncertainty excluding a practically negligible gain, persistence after utilization/common-support controls, weak pre-index performance, no timestamp-permutation reproduction, and component/document concordance. Adverse results are disappearance after controls, timestamp permutation or pre-index reproduction, enzyme-only/measurement-density dominance, or specificity only for any admission/repeat TACE. Inconclusive results are sparse coverage, unstable convergence, too few events, endpoint discordance or wide intervals; they defer interpretation rather than refute the hypothesis.

Computationally checkable outputs are cohort flow, joins, timestamp ordering, assay audit, held-out predictions/metrics, calibration, decision curves, uncertainty, component tables and negative-control behavior. Clinical truth, planned status, mechanism, causality, mortality benefit, action thresholds and external validity require adjudication or another study. Missing essentials include verified assay units, imaging/tumor burden, embolized territory/drug/dose, ECOG, portal pressure, death linkage and external validation.

Three inspected key works are retained exactly from the parent: [K1] Sanai et al. anchors decompensation and baseline reserve; [K2] Xu et al. supplies a baseline-only acute dysfunction precedent; [K3] You et al. supports an early post-TACE injury window but not later decompensation prediction. All are abstract-only inspected evidence; no inaccessible full text is claimed.

candidates.public_proposal:
# Cumulative hypotension duration beyond nadir as a predictor of incident creatinine-defined AKI in eICU

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no full study, model fit, or result has been computed. Episode-3 substantive child of candidate-37de9b9932cf160c90bce8f3. Adaptation of expert seed eicu-03, not reproduction of a demonstration paper.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The expert seed asks whether, at the same minimum blood pressure, longer-lasting hypotension precedes more AKI. Inspected evidence supports narrower premises: temporal hypotension patterns based on duration and recurrence can be prognostic in a single-center perioperative cohort [K1]; a clinical AKI guideline bounds endpoint definition [K2]; and a randomized blood-pressure-target trial makes clear why observational hypotension associations must not be presented as treatment effects [K3]. None answers whether a simple duration summary is transportable after accounting for measurement process, current severity and recorded treatment.

H1: among adult first eICU ICU stays with adequate early BP and kidney ascertainment, cumulative covered minutes with systemic MAP below 65 mmHg in ICU minutes 0-360 adds reproducible prognostic information for a new creatinine-defined event in minutes 360-2880 beyond nadir MAP, pre-index severity and observation coverage, including evaluation on hospitals not used for fitting.

The leading explanation is persistent hemodynamic stress. Strong rivals are current severity, care intensity/measurement density, and treatment response: sicker patients may be measured more often, receive pressors, have lower nadirs and have different creatinine ascertainment. A residual association would be descriptive/prognostic only; it would not establish renal hypoperfusion, a physiologic threshold, causality, hospital quality, or benefit from raising MAP. The advance is a data-bound test that can separate a portable duration summary from process rivals and richer temporal information, rather than another association plot or treatment claim.

## Population, boundaries and joins

Use only read-only eICU 2.0 snapshot 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476e89543643c08b7df637a15ec and catalog 802870bc57f60a7adfb12f5a59267b7cba5e1d61896adb7c6b74a58a1219f14c. Direct source directory is [private-path]/eicu数据 库/EICU 2.0数据/; the actual directory contains the stated Unicode name. Source files are the named .csv.gz archives and their ordinary CSV members. Join eICU tables only on patientunitstayid; never join to MIMIC or HCC identifiers. Select the first ICU stay per uniquepid by lowest unitvisitnumber, then earliest unitadmittime24. Keep whole hospitals together in splits.

Adults are numeric age >=18. Preserve > 89 as a category and use 90 only in sensitivity analysis. Index is ICU admission; longitudinal offsets are minutes relative to admission. Require survival/in-ICU presence through minute 360, at least 12 valid 5-minute BP bins and at least 240 minutes between first and last covered bin, plus a valid pre-index creatinine baseline. These are eligibility rules, not imputed negatives. Report a flow table for every exclusion.

## Exact available bindings
