There is no unitadmitoffset.
- vitalPeriodic.csv.gz, table vitalPeriodic, member vitalPeriodic.csv, SHA-256 329b522f97f7d3d0cb4541e4fc4afc32048eb8fd0f8c9b156907f845a992906c: patientunitstayid, observationoffset, systemicmean, systemicsystolic, systemicdiastolic, heartrate, respiration and pamean. Use systemicmean; exclude pamean, which is pulmonary-artery mean.
- vitalAperiodic.csv.gz, table vitalAperiodic, member vitalAperiodic.csv, SHA-256 8b23e5a50f8aabc6cb62fc69e2dcdf755a2e5649b1439a7ca413a7c5b2d5a9a0: patientunitstayid, observationoffset and noninvasivemean. Use noninvasivemean only when systemicmean is absent and retain modality.
- lab.csv.gz, table lab, member lab.csv, SHA-256 91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a: patientunitstayid, labresultoffset, labname, labresult, labresulttext, labmeasurenamesystem, labmeasurenameinterface and labresultrevisedoffset. There is no units column.
- infusionDrug.csv.gz, table infusionDrug, member infusionDrug.csv, SHA-256 f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b: patientunitstayid, infusionoffset, drugname, drugrate, infusionrate, drugamount, volumeoffluid and patientweight.
- hospital.csv.gz, table hospital, member hospital.csv, SHA-256 16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6: hospitalid, numbedscategory, teachingstatus and region.
- carePlanEOL.csv.gz, table carePlanEOL, member carePlanEOL.csv, SHA-256 8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0: patientunitstayid, cpleolsaveoffset, cpleoldiscussionoffset and activeupondischarge.
- apacheApsVar.csv.gz, table apacheApsVar, member apacheApsVar.csv, SHA-256 4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4: admission-summary creatinine, dialysis, urine and meanbp, with no time field. Use only as an adjustment/readiness sensitivity, never as time-aligned outcome or dialysis event.
- intakeOutput.csv.gz, table intakeOutput, member intakeOutput.csv, SHA-256 f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121: intakeoutputoffset, outputtotal, dialysistotal, nettotal, intakeoutputentryoffset, cellpath, celllabel, cellvaluenumeric and cellvaluetext. outputtotal is not automatically urine; use only after label/unit/timing adjudication.

## Exposure and outcome

Construct common 5-minute bins over 0-360. Prefer valid systemicmean, otherwise noninvasivemean; do not interpolate across gaps over 10 minutes or treat absent measurements as normal. Primary exposure is covered minutes with MAP below 65. Preserve low-time fraction, nadir, area below threshold, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, covered count, median gap, modality mix and missingness. Sensitivities use MAP ranges 30-180, thresholds 60/70 and common-density thinning.

Primary target is a creatinine-only incident event in 360-2880. Baseline is the last valid eligible serum-creatinine result in -24-0. Audit normalized labname, labmeasurenamesystem and labmeasurenameinterface; accept only numeric labresult values in a frozen serum-creatinine vocabulary, deduplicating same clinical offsets by latest labresultrevisedoffset. First post-window result at least 0.3 mg/dL above baseline defines the event. Because lab has no units column, there is no unverified conversion; if scale/vocabulary cannot be made reproducible, stop the primary fit and report label-readiness failure. Do not parse labresulttext, substitute BUN, or silently use apacheApsVar.creatinine. A 1.5-times-baseline endpoint over 7 ICU days is a distinct sensitivity. Do not call the primary label full KDIGO because urine semantics are not validated.

A no-event label requires valid baseline, alive/in ICU at 360, and either a valid creatinine at or after 2880 or an observed competing/censoring endpoint. Early discharge/transfer without qualifying lab is right-censored, not negative. Death before 2880 without an event is a competing event. Dialysis is not a primary label; an interpretable intakeOutput dialysis row may be a separate support/competing-event sensitivity, while apacheApsVar.dialysis alone cannot establish timing. EOL fields are process covariates/sensitivity flags, not intent. Fit cause-specific/discrete-time and inverse-probability-of-observation sensitivities, reporting complete-follow-up and competing-event counts.

After freezing the primary analysis, define a pre-index negative control among stays with valid creatinine in -48--24 and a distinct result in -24-0, using the same 0.3 mg/dL rise rule. A stronger pre-index duration association is adverse evidence for baseline severity/measurement process; it is not a causal claim.

## Baseline, alternative and analysis

B0 is regularized logistic/discrete-time cause-specific regression using the same target and split: pre-index creatinine, nadir MAP, initial MAP/HR/respiration, demographics, hospital/ICU type, BP modality/missingness and pre-index lab coverage. B1 adds duration, low-time fraction, episodes and recovery with a restricted spline and fixed-nadir bands. Primary estimands are held-out incremental log loss, Brier score and calibration; AUROC/AUPRC are secondary. Use whole-hospital 60/20/20 train/validation/test, keeping each uniquepid in one split; if hospital count makes this unstable, use repeated grouped-hospital cross-validation and state the limitation. Use hospital-clustered bootstrap intervals.

M is a small GRU or temporal convolution over the same 72 bins, with MAP, HR, respiration, modality, time-since-last-observation, masks, recorded pressor indicators/rates and pre-index severity. Fit only on training hospitals, early-stop/calibrate on validation hospitals and evaluate once on held-out hospitals. M can reveal persistence, oscillation, recovery timing and BP-treatment coupling that a scalar duration/nadir loses; B1 provides the transparent clinical summary. Compare treatment-masked, coverage-only, treatment-inclusive and common-density variants. Treatment-inclusive results remain observational and cannot identify a pressor effect.

Tabular fits use CPU. GPU is optional only if a bounded parsing/sequence-fit measurement justifies it; inside an allocated job use cuda:0 and do not infer GPU absence from ordinary shell. Future planning envelope is 16 CPU, up to 8 GPU, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; these are solver limits, not measured discovery results. The deliverable is newly fitted B0/B1/M plus cohort flow, label audit, held-out predictions, calibration/uncertainty, fixed-nadir curves, hospital heterogeneity, ablations, negative-control output and resource logs.

## Falsification and interpretation

Support requires label readiness, held-out B1 improvement over B0 with uncertainty excluding no improvement, stable calibration, monotone duration-risk within fixed-nadir bands, persistence under process/treatment/common-density checks, no material pre-index negative-control signal, and reproducible M trajectory information across hospital holdout. This supports a transportable prognostic summary only.

Adverse results are null/non-monotone duration, low-density-only gain, a strong mask-only or pre-index-control gain, disappearance after recorded-treatment/process checks, hospital-specific behavior, or label failure. These favor severity, selection or measurement explanations and argue against a robust duration signal.

Inconclusive results are wide intervals, inadequate creatinine coverage, exposure-dependent censoring, too few hospitals, unstable holdout, or unresolved vocabulary/scale semantics. They do not refute H1; they require clinical label adjudication, external validation or a narrower BP-process study. Clinical adjudication is essential for creatinine vocabulary/units, urine/dialysis semantics, EOL interpretation and BP modality; causal and treatment conclusions require another study.

## References and alternatives

The three inspected works are attached as key-references.json with UTF-8 excerpts: [K1] full HTML passages; [K2] and [K3] abstract/metadata only with explicit limits. The natural-history transformer demonstration motivates a bounded structured-sequence adaptation but is not reproduced. The cancer multimodal demonstration cannot be reproduced because configured eICU lacks its images and the main paper/STAR Methods remain unavailable, so it is not used. The Bayesian EHR/genetic work is not selected because genetics are unavailable and a latent model would not test a distinct uncertainty here. Latent trajectory classes and a renal state-space model are deferred because class-shape choices and perfusion/congestion/biomarker data are unavailable; a large transformer adds capacity without a distinct question. Other expert eICU seeds remain deferred pending their own binding audits; eicu-03 is the developed seed.

## Limits

Available data lack clinician-adjudicated AKI, reliable pre-ICU kidney function, verified lab units, complete fluid balance, calibrated raw BP waveforms, renal replacement intent, staffing/bed context and independent external validation. An automatic verifier can check source binding, leakage control, fitting, uncertainty and whether conclusions match outputs; it cannot establish mechanism, causality, clinical benefit or a treatment target.

# HCC post-TACE trajectory: episode-3 transportability and observation-process child

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no full study or model fit has been executed. This is a substantive child of candidate-9bd033dcf9505bdbd56b8b36. It preserves the parent's population, time zero, outcome window, and primary incremental-prognostic estimand, while resolving the remaining uncertainty about who has an observed day-0–7 trajectory and whether an assay/name signal transports across calendar and department regimes.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis, and advance

The established opening is that a short-lived post-TACE aminotransferase injury may differ from a coordinated loss of hepatic synthetic/renal reserve. The parent already made the signal testable with exact HCC bindings, assay-aware transformations, utilization controls, endpoint concordance and a regularized-versus-state-space comparison. The unresolved rival is now explicit: requiring baseline plus a day-3–7 laboratory measurement may select people who remain in care, are readmitted early, or are managed by departments/eras with denser testing. A second rival is transport failure: names, panels and local assay conventions can change over calendar time or department, making a learned trajectory appear portable only inside its source regime.

Primary hypothesis (unchanged): among adult HCC patients with a first observed TACE and no documented pre/index decompensation, a 0–7-day trajectory dominated by worsening synthetic/renal reserve predicts a new post-discharge decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 beyond baseline risk. An isolated AST/ALT flare is the leading substantive rival. The primary estimand remains the paired chronological-test-set incremental prognostic performance of the dynamic model versus the same baseline-only model for that outcome; it is not a treatment effect, causal effect, mechanism, or action threshold.

The new episode asks whether that same incremental signal is transportable and selection-robust. A supportive result would show that the signal is present in the full eligible population through a prespecified missingness-aware model, remains after observation-process adjustment, and has compatible performance/calibration in held-out calendar and department regimes. This would advance the parent from “a potentially useful trajectory in observed patients” toward evidence that the result is not merely a local documentation practice. It would still not establish external validity, causal TACE harm, biological mechanism, or clinical utility without adjudication and prospective validation. An adverse result would localize the claim to an observed-care regime or identify trajectory availability as the dominant explanation; that is a clinically useful boundary, not a failed computation.

## Population, time zero, temporal boundaries, and outcomes

Use only HCC. Identify each patient's first procedure row whose 手术 contains TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞, or 动脉化疗栓塞, with parseable 开始时间 and a matching encounter. Require age >=18 and an HCC diagnosis (at minimum 肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤) before/on the index encounter. Exclude prior/index high-specificity decompensation terms: 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎, or 黄疸; report broader cirrhosis-decompensation flags separately. Missing labs, missing discharge, or absent day-3–7 measurements do not exclude an index patient from the primary analysis.

Time zero is the earliest qualifying 手术.开始时间. Preserve the parent's complete-follow-up rule: include only index dates with a verifiable 90-day source observation horizon, using 2025-10-03 or a recomputed equivalent cutoff after checking source maxima. Baseline is the closest assay-specific quantitative result in [-14,0] days; [-30,0] is a sensitivity window. Dynamic information is restricted to [0,7] days and raw timestamps are retained. The primary event is the first distinct encounter after index 出院时间 whose admission time is in [8,90] days and whose diagnosis contains a prespecified high-specificity component. Missing discharge is reported and separately analyzed; it is never silently changed into an admission or used to redefine time zero.

Report the composite plus ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure and jaundice components; report diagnosis-only, clinical-document-confirmed, discordant and missing-document strata. Any admission and repeat TACE are non-equivalent secondary outcomes. Do not infer planned/unplanned status.

The primary estimand is unchanged: on the chronological test set, compare baseline-only and dynamic predictions for the primary composite using paired differences in Brier score, calibration, discrimination and decision-curve net benefit. The target population is all eligible index patients, not only those with a complete trajectory. The dynamic prediction is therefore defined under observed-data/missingness handling; the complete-trajectory subgroup is a prespecified transportability/selection estimand, not the primary population.

## Exact read-only data bindings and verified source schema

All joins are within HCC on the documented composite key (患者主索引, 就诊号). Audit duplicate-key rates before aggregation and retain raw timestamps. All sources below are ordinary CSVs, not archive members. Their raw hashes are frozen and match the HCC source catalog; target paths are the corresponding /data/HCC paths in a Harbor job.

The source-header audit verified these names. The parent catalog marks vitals and transfers as identifier-only and front_page as nominal; they are not required inputs. Pathology is not required for the predictive model and has no timestamp. No cross-dataset identifier join is permitted. No unavailable imaging, tumor burden, embolized territory, drug/dose, ECOG, portal pressure, mortality linkage or assay units is inferred.

## Measurement and endpoint audit

Labs have no unit column. Before outcome analysis, freeze a training-only assay dictionary from 检验 values, including raw-name variants, qualitative values, specimen type, duplicate rate, timestamps, calendar era and department distribution. Parse only numeric 定量结果. Candidate assay concepts are total/direct bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR or PT ratio, creatinine, sodium, AST, ALT and AFP; presence and comparability must be demonstrated. Within each assay/name regime, use training-set standardization, patient-centered changes or ranks; do not pool raw thresholds or claim valid ALBI/MELD/Child-Pugh without expert unit verification. Map observations to [0,1–2,3–4,5–7] day bins with a deterministic nearest-time tie rule, but retain event-level timestamps and name/regime labels.

Create a data-availability record for every eligible index: baseline availability, any day-0–7 lab, at least one day-3–7 lab, assay-specific bin coverage, number of lab timestamps, distinct assays, first-lab lag, last observed day, encounters with labs, and whether the index admission or a day-8–90 admission generated the observations. The last item is descriptive only: all features must stop at day 7 and later outcome-related observation is never used. Also record encounter, admission, department, procedure, medication, order and examination counts in pre-index and day-0–7 windows. Define availability strata before outcome inspection: A0 no baseline; A1 baseline but no day-3–7 lab; A2 baseline plus day-3–7 lab; and a finer predeclared quartile/low-medium-high observation-density partition within calendar/departments when counts permit. Never condition the primary result on A2 alone.

The primary endpoint is a transparent diagnosis-name lexical rule. The document sensitivity requires the same component in the listed clinical_documents fields. Produce a blinded clinician adjudication packet sampled across availability, calendar and department strata to label true new/worsening decompensation, planned status, competing illness/HCC progression, TACE injury and text validity. Adjudication is essential for clinical truth and cannot be replaced by model performance.

## Baseline comparator and substantive alternative

B0 is the parent's L2-regularized logistic regression using time-zero age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, baseline assay-specific values and missingness. A no-lab B0 is a sensitivity comparator. B1 is the same L2 model plus prespecified [0,7] assay deltas, robust slopes, extrema, last values, observation counts, first-lab lag and separate AST/ALT-flare blocks. B0 and B1 are fit and scored on the same all-eligible index population through the missingness strategy below.

The substantive alternative is a missingness-aware joint outcome/observation model, not a complexity upgrade for its own sake. Let R_{ijb} indicate whether assay j is observed in bin b for patient i, and Y_i the days-8–90 composite. Model the latent standardized reserve and transient-injury factors with the same two-factor irregular-time measurement model as the parent, while jointly modeling the observation intensity R and its bin-level count using pre-index severity, department, calendar era, discharge/encounter context and the latent current state. Include department- and calendar-era random intercepts/slopes for the observation and outcome heads, with partial pooling; assay/name-regime-specific loadings and noise are estimated in training data. The outcome head predicts Y from the day-7 posterior state plus the same baseline covariates. Use a prespecified pattern-mixture sensitivity parameter for nonrandom missingness, varying the association between latent state and unobserved measurement probability over a clinically stated range. Do not use day-8–90 observations.

This alternative adds information B1 loses: it estimates uncertainty about the latent trajectory when measurements are irregular, separates reserve from transient enzyme injury, and estimates how much of apparent performance is explained by who gets measured. Partial pooling can reveal whether loadings and calibration are stable across departments/eras rather than silently averaging incompatible regimes. Risks are stronger assumptions (state evolution, missingness model and exchangeability within department/era), weak identifiability in sparse strata, convergence failure, and sensitivity to unresolved units/name mapping. Latent factors remain representations, not biological mechanisms. A neural sequence model remains deferred because it would add capacity without directly identifying selection or assay transportability.

Alternatives were specified at comparable detail before selection:

1. L2 B0/B1: exact inputs are baseline plus fixed-bin trajectory summaries, missingness and utilization controls; fit target is Y_i; train/validation/test is chronological; paired Brier, calibration, discrimination, net benefit and bootstrap uncertainty are required. It is the transparent primary comparator and may be adequate if the signal is robust.
2. Joint hierarchical observation/outcome state-space model: exact inputs are the same labs/timestamps plus R/count process, department, calendar era and baseline utilization; fit targets are Y_i and the observation process; the same chronological split plus held-out department/era evaluations are required; report predictive metrics, calibration, state/loadings stability, observation-process contribution and sensitivity analysis. It is selected for this episode because the unresolved scientific question is selection and transport, which B1 cannot represent.
3. Neural sequence model: exact inputs would be irregular assay/name/time tokens and utilization context, target Y_i, with temporal and department holdouts; it is deferred because it cannot by itself distinguish missing-not-at-random observation from learned proxy behavior, and its added capacity is not justified before the hierarchical model establishes whether a substantive residual transport problem remains.

## Splits, estimands, fitting, uncertainty, and transport tests

Freeze the split before outcome analysis and keep each patient in one partition: train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, chronological test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03 or an equivalent complete-follow-up cutoff recomputed from the source maximum. Tune penalties, state dimension, random-effect shrinkage and sensitivity-grid presentation on train/validation only. If a department is too sparse for a standalone holdout, retain it in pooled testing and report that transport contrast as inconclusive rather than merging after seeing results.

Primary analysis: all eligible patients, with B0 and the joint model producing a risk for each patient. Missing baseline or trajectory values are represented by the declared observation model and uncertainty; no complete-case primary analysis. Compare paired test-set B0 versus dynamic predictions in Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, ROC-AUC/PR-AUC, decision-curve net benefit and clinically prespecified high-sensitivity operating point. Use patient-cluster bootstrap 2,000 replicates or the maximum permitted bounded equivalent, stratified only as a sensitivity analysis, and report event count, availability strata, effective sample size and 95% intervals. Report model convergence and state/loadings uncertainty.

Selection diagnostics: describe A0/A1/A2 flow and compare baseline covariates, outcome rate, departments, calendar eras, early readmission and observation density across strata. Estimate an inverse-observation-probability weighted complete-trajectory contrast only as a secondary sensitivity analysis, with weights fitted in train/validation from variables available by day 0 (and a prespecified stabilized truncation); do not present it as a cure for unmeasured MNAR. The primary joint model’s observation head is the main missingness-aware estimand. If A2 is rare or positivity fails, report this as a transportability limitation.

Transport diagnostics: (a) temporal test, (b) leave-one-department/regime-out test where feasible, (c) train on earlier eras and score each later era, (d) fit assay/name dictionary on training only then report unmapped and remapped rates by test era/department, (e) pooled versus department/era-specific calibration and random-effect/loadings intervals, and (f) common-support performance restricted to regimes with adequate assay coverage. These are prespecified heterogeneity estimands, not license to select the most favorable subgroup. The primary claim requires the full eligible temporal test; regime contrasts qualify transportability.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted B0, B1 and joint hierarchical observation/outcome models; frozen all-patient test predictions; availability/selection flow; assay/name-regime audit; pooled and held-out department/era metrics; calibration and paired uncertainty; state/loadings and observation-process summaries; component/document endpoint tables; and negative-control results. No model fit or result is claimed in this proposal.

Approximate resource budget is within the configured solver envelope and is an estimate, not a measured result: chunked selected-column parsing and B0/B1 use 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM, likely tens of minutes; the joint state-space/observation fit and 2,000-replicate bootstrap request 16 CPUs, 64–128 GB RAM, no GPU, and up to 4–8 hours (28,800 s). A smaller diagnostic/optimization pilot may use 4 CPUs and 16 GB to test convergence on train data only; it cannot be used as a scientific result. GPU is deferred because this is low-dimensional likelihood fitting and the uncertainty is observational-process modeling, not representation capacity.

## Falsification and interpretation

Mandatory negative controls are: within-patient timestamp permutation preserving values and counts; a matched pre-index pseudo-window; measurement-only prediction from counts/lag/department/era without lab values; AST/ALT-only versus reserve-panel-only blocks; any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes; and a “future observation” audit that proves no post-day-7 feature is present. Add a regime-shuffle control that permutes department/era labels within the training design: if apparent transport heterogeneity disappears under the shuffle, it may be a regime-label artifact; if the primary signal survives timestamp permutation or is reproduced in the pre-index window, ordering/timing or utilization is the stronger explanation.

Support requires: (i) a non-negligible paired dynamic improvement on the untouched chronological test in the all-eligible analysis; (ii) calibrated performance and uncertainty that are not confined to A2 complete-trajectory patients; (iii) persistence after observation controls and the MNAR sensitivity range; (iv) no material timestamp-permutation or pre-index reproduction; (v) assay/name mappings and loadings that are stable enough across held-out eras/departments, with no severe calibration drift; and (vi) at least directionally concordant document/component results. This supports transportable incremental prognostic value, not mechanism or causality.

Adverse evidence is a dynamic gain that disappears after observation-process adjustment; large A2-versus-non-A2 selection differences with no positivity; a gain confined to one department/era or to one unmapped/local assay; calibration failure in held-out regimes; timestamp-permutation or pre-index reproduction; count-only dominance; AST/ALT-only dominance; or endpoint/document discordance. These results would revise the claim to “local observed-care association,” prioritize standardized assay capture or adjudication, or abandon the trajectory direction if no regime has adequate support.

Inconclusive evidence includes too few events in availability/department/era cells, non-identifiable observation parameters, unstable state-space convergence, wide paired intervals, unresolved units, high unmapped assay names, missing discharge, or insufficient common support. Do not interpret an imprecise null as refutation. Continue only if the primary computation and enough regime support are complete; revise to a narrower regime if only a prespecified regime is estimable; defer if adjudication or assay verification is missing; abandon only if a well-powered, adequately observed test repeatedly fails after the negative controls.

Computationally checkable outputs are source hashes/headers, join and duplicate audits, cohort flow, timestamp bounds, assay dictionary and unmapped rates, availability/selection tables, split integrity, predictions, metrics, calibration, paired intervals, regime contrasts, convergence, negative-control behavior and absence of post-day-7 leakage. Clinical adjudication is required for true/worsening decompensation, planned status, competing illness and text validity. Expert assay/unit review, imaging/tumor burden, procedural intensity, death linkage, external validation and prospective surveillance are required for stronger clinical or causal conclusions.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Sanai et al. supports the clinical consequence of post-locoregional-therapy decompensation and the role of baseline reserve; it does not test this HCC routine-lab 0–7-day incremental trajectory or transportability. Abstract-only inspection; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

[K2] Xu et al. supports a baseline-only acute post-intervention dysfunction prediction precedent with internal validation; it does not establish a missingness-aware longitudinal trajectory or external transport. Abstract-only inspection; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

[K3] You et al. supports an early post-TACE liver-injury observation window and the need to distinguish enzyme injury from reserve loss; it does not establish days-8–90 decompensation prediction or cross-regime transport. Abstract-only inspection; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

The attached excerpts and key-references.json preserve these limits. These works are evidence for the opening and boundaries, not evidence that the primary hypothesis is true.

# Repair child: observed discordant renal recovery at the ICU-discharge landmark

Status: planned design only. No MIMIC rows were read into this branch, no model was fitted, and no clinical conclusion is claimed. Parent: candidate-2ff2435c231c6e0d39a42a6e. This is a substantive child focused on ascertainment and interpretation, not a topic or estimand change.

## Scientific question and advance

The parent asks whether a fall in serum creatinine without concurrent urine-output recovery in the last 24 hours before ICU discharge identifies short-horizon risk beyond measured severity. The strongest available evidence supports two narrower premises: creatinine and urine output are complementary clinical observations ([K1]), and creatinine can misrepresent filtration when muscle production and ICU physiology change ([K2]). Dynamic renal assessment can be prognostic while extra biomarkers add inconsistent incremental value ([K3]). None of those observations establishes that an EHR-defined discordance at ICU discharge is a reproducible risk marker, nor that a repeated longitudinal pattern is different from a brief or poorly documented episode.

The unresolved, falsifiable claim is:

> In adults surviving a first ICU stay of at least 48 hours, among patients with adequate and sufficiently dense urine-output observation, creatinine improvement without urine-output recovery during [t0-24 h,t0) is associated with higher 48-hour post-ICU-discharge risk of readmission or in-hospital death after adjustment for pre-landmark severity and discharge-selection proxies; the association is stronger and more reproducible when the same discordance recurs across earlier 6-hour bins than when it appears only in the final bin.

This is a non-causal prognostic claim. It does not say that delaying discharge, changing diuretics, or restoring urine output would improve outcomes. The substantive advance is a boundary test: it separates a clinically interpretable observed phenotype from three alternatives that the parent did not yet operationalize tightly enough—missing urine measurement, residual illness/discharge selection, and transient threshold/charting noise.

The result that would change the next decision is the contrast between (a) a dense-observation, severity-adjusted landmark association and (b) a repeated-versus-transient contrast in a held-out sample. If the association disappears with observation coverage and discharge proxies, the useful conclusion is that the phenotype is largely ascertainment/selection, not that renal recovery is biologically irrelevant.

## Population, landmark, and outcome

Use the frozen MIMIC-IV 3.1 snapshot and first ICU stay per subject:

- Source archive: [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip, 10,551,747,784 bytes, SHA-256 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09.
- Join hosp/patients to hosp/admissions by subject_id, then icu/icustays by subject_id,hadm_id. No cross-dataset join is permitted.
- Include age >=18, valid intime < outtime, ICU LOS >=2 days, outtime <= dischtime, first ICU stay for each subject, and alive at t0 = outtime.
- All predictors are strictly before t0: the landmark feature window is [t0-24 hours,t0), and longitudinal bins are the non-overlapping 6-hour intervals from ICU admission through t0. No post-t0 variable is a predictor.
- Primary outcome: the first event in (t0,t0+48 hours] consisting of admissions.deathtime or a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id,hadm_id; censor at admissions.dischtime. Report the two components separately, 7-day event risk, and in-hospital death as secondary outcomes.

The primary estimand remains the standardized observational risk difference (and risk ratio) for the discordant group versus improved/high-output concordance, conditional on measured pre-t0 covariates. The repeated-versus-transient analysis is an explicitly prognostic decomposition, not a causal mediation analysis.

## Ascertainment repair: urine observation is a measured variable

The parent’s requirement of “at least one urine record” is insufficient: one record can be a missed chart, a zero, a partial interval, or a late retrospective total. The experiment must preserve coverage information rather than treating all unobserved volume as zero.

Required urine records are icu/outputevents rows restricted to d_items item IDs 226559 (Foley), 226560 (Void), and 226561 (Condom Cath), joined within the selected stay. Use charttime, numeric nonnegative value, and valueuom; reject incompatible units rather than silently converting. The readiness manifest must prove these item labels are unique and present in icu/d_items.

For each 6-hour bin and the final 24-hour window, construct:

1. urine_volume_observed: sum of valid nonnegative volumes, with no imputation of unobserved volume.
2. urine_n_records: number of valid output rows.
3. urine_active_hours: hours between the earliest and latest valid urine chart time, clipped to the bin/window; this is a documentation-span measure, not a claim of continuous collection.
4. urine_bin_coverage: urine_active_hours / bin_hours, capped at 1.
5. urine_any: an indicator that at least one valid row exists.
6. urine_zero_fraction: fraction of valid rows whose volume is zero.
7. item-source indicators for Foley, Void, and Condom Cath, plus the count of distinct source types.

Coverage is a documentation/measurement proxy, not a validated completeness measure. A record timestamp does not prove that all urine was collected or charted. Define the primary ascertainable cohort as final-window urine_bin_coverage >= 0.75, at least two valid records in each of the four 6-hour bins, and at least one source-type indicator. Preserve the full eligible cohort as a pre-specified observation-sensitivity cohort with coverage features and missingness indicators; do not silently replace it with the dense subset. Also report a complete-case ladder: any record, >=2 records, >=0.75 coverage, and the strict four-bin rule, with cohort flow and outcome counts.

The low-output rule is retained as an operational threshold: total valid volume <400 mL in 24 hours. It is intentionally unweighted because MIMIC binding does not guarantee a valid weight field in this proposal. A weight-indexed analysis is deferred unless a verified weight field and compatible timing are added in a new approved design. Sensitivity checks use continuous volume and the zero/low/high categories, never negative values or unit-mixed sums. Urine data from other item IDs are not used as if they were measured equivalents.

Creatinine remains item 50912 in hosp/labevents, linked to hosp/d_labitems. Require at least two valid creatinine observations at least six hours apart, with the final observation in [t0-24h,t0). Define C_peak as the maximum valid value in that window, C_last as the final value, and improvement as C_peak-C_last >=0.3 mg/dL. Record creatinine count, span, and time since the peak. This makes a two-point improvement distinguishable from a long, repeatedly observed trajectory.

## Residual severity and discharge-selection repair

The study cannot observe the clinical decision to transfer out of ICU, the clinician’s rationale, baseline CKD, complete diuretic exposure, or true fluid balance. Therefore “adjusted beyond severity” is limited to measured proxies and must not be phrased as eliminating confounding or selection.

Use the parent’s exact available fields and add only pre-t0 variables available from the same bound tables:

- age, sex, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-landmark time, and calendar-year/site-independent ICU care-unit category from patients, admissions, and icustays;
- creatinine level/trajectory and observation counts;
- urine volume, coverage, record count, source-type indicators, and missingness;
- last-six-hour and preceding-six-hour MAP summaries from icu/chartevents item 220052, with count and time-since-last measurement;
- available lactate and platelet values from chartevents after a frozen item-manifest lookup, with their measurement indicators and time-since-last values;
- vasopressor exposure indicators and duration/last-active status from icu/inputevents items 221906, 221289, 221749, and 222315, using starttime,endtime,statusdescription;
- invasive ventilation indicator from icu/procedureevents item 225792;
- renal replacement therapy indicators after resolving the procedure/item labels in the frozen readiness manifest.

The discharge-selection sensitivity set is defined before outcome inspection and includes current support (vasopressor/ventilation/RRT), last and preceding MAP, lactate/platelet availability and values, ICU LOS, admission type, care unit, recent measurement intensity, and the interval from admission to t0. Fit the primary model with these measured proxies and a second model restricted to no vasopressor, no invasive ventilation, and no RRT before t0. Compare standardized risks, not only odds ratios. In a descriptive negative-control-style check, ask whether discordance predicts a same-window pre-landmark event or an earlier pseudo-landmark outcome; this is a diagnostic for severity/timing and cannot validate a causal interpretation.

Because conditioning on ICU survival and discharge is part of the design, report the eligible-to-landmark flow and compare excluded patients by observed baseline fields. Do not call the survivor restriction “confounding control.” If discordance is associated with outcome only in sparsely observed or highly supported patients, that supports documentation or discharge-selection explanations. If it remains in the dense, support-restricted set with similar direction and calibration, it is a stronger prognostic regularity but still not a mechanism.

## Baseline versus the longitudinal latent alternative

The method comparison is scientific, not a contest for a small AUROC gain.

B0 is a penalized logistic regression for the primary 48-hour outcome. Exact inputs are age, sex, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 time, C_peak, C_last, creatinine improvement, time since creatinine peak, final 24-hour urine volume, low-output indicator, urine coverage, urine record count/source indicators, last and preceding MAP, available lactate and platelets, vasopressor/ventilation/RRT indicators, and all corresponding measurement/missingness indicators. B1 adds the four-level final-window group: improved/high, improved/low (discordant), not-improved/high, and not-improved/low. Continuous creatinine and urine quantities are retained alongside the group so B1 does not confuse a threshold with information already represented by its components. Use standardization fixed from training data and a prespecified penalty selected on the tuning split.

The bounded alternative is a three-state multivariate HMM/state-space model, fit only if the readiness gate passes, on 6-hour bins from ICU admission to t0. Its emissions use the same measured channels: creatinine level and change, urine volume, urine coverage/record count/source indicators, MAP, available lactate/platelet channels, support indicators, and missingness indicators. Do not interpolate unobserved urine as zero. Use an explicit observation mask and coverage channel; bins with no valid output are missing emissions, not low output. Fit the model on training subjects only; select the number/regularization of states and emission family on the 15% tuning set, with fixed subject-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test membership made before fitting. The test set is untouched until final held-out evaluation. Use 200 patient bootstrap resamples for intervals, with a reproducible seed and patient-level resampling.

The latent model’s scientific target is not “better prediction.” It estimates:

- posterior probability of a renal-observation state at each bin;
- occupancy and number of transitions;
- time since the last transition;
- posterior probability that the final discordance is persistent across at least two prior bins versus isolated to the last bin;
- held-out outcome risk conditional on those summaries.

The specific discriminating comparison is repeated discordance versus transient discordance at matched final-window observed discordance and matched B0 risk. The rival charting-noise explanation predicts that the pattern will be concentrated in low-coverage bins, have unstable state assignments, show little persistence, and lose its association after coverage/support adjustment. A repeated-physiology explanation predicts higher posterior persistence, consistent transitions across bins, and a held-out risk contrast that survives coverage and support-restricted analyses. Neither pattern establishes renal mechanism or causality.

A simpler mechanistic alternative was considered: a deterministic two-compartment filtration/urine-balance model using creatinine change, urine volume, and support/coverage. It is deferred because MIMIC lacks measured GFR, cystatin C in the bound design, fluid composition, reliable body weight, complete diuretic exposure, and a trustworthy creatinine-generation parameter. Fitting such a model would create untestable assumptions rather than reveal filtration. A transformer/LSTM is also deferred because it would add opaque sequence capacity without a separable scientific observable. The HMM is retained only because persistence, transition timing, and observation masking are direct outputs that answer the repeated-versus-transient uncertainty.

Selection rule: if the test set has fewer than 200 subjects or 30 primary events, or if the observation-mask/coverage channels cannot be represented without imputation, do not fit or interpret the HMM; report B0/B1 feasibility and defer the latent question. If state separation is poor (pre-specified emission overlap and transition instability across bootstrap fits), treat the HMM as inconclusive, not as evidence for noise or physiology.

## Analysis, uncertainty, and falsification

Primary analysis:

1. Freeze the item manifest, unit checks, cohort flow, coverage thresholds, outcome construction, and split before fitting.
2. Fit B0 and B1 on training data, tune penalty on tuning data, and report held-out standardized group risks, risk differences/ratios, Brier score, log loss, AUROC/AUPRC as descriptive discrimination, calibration slope/intercept, and calibration plots.
3. Estimate uncertainty with 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of the held-out test predictions for performance and standardized contrasts; for the HMM, repeat posterior summaries within each bootstrap using fixed fitted parameters unless a convergence/fit instability rule requires refitting, which must be stated.
4. Report missingness, coverage, support, and exclusions for each cohort and outcome. Never turn a confidence interval crossing zero into proof of no association.

Prespecified falsification and robustness checks are: permutation of discordance within baseline-risk/ICU-LOS/admission strata; 12-hour versus 48-hour windows; continuous creatinine slope; final-window coverage strata; complete-case ladder; measurement-density and ICU-care-unit strata; no-support restriction; RRT exclusion; creatinine-only, urine-only, and interaction models; and a pseudo-landmark 24 hours before t0. The pseudo-landmark cannot share future data with the primary feature window. A stable result should have directionally similar estimates in the dense and full cohorts, while a documentation artifact should attenuate as coverage and measurement proxies are controlled. These are diagnostic patterns, not causal proof.

Supportive result: in the dense cohort, B1’s discordant contrast is directionally stable with calibrated held-out risk above concordance after measured severity/support adjustment, and the HMM shows reproducible persistence with a held-out risk contrast for repeated versus transient discordance. This supports an observable prognostic phenotype and justifies external validation or adjudicated urine completeness; it does not support delaying discharge or a renal mechanism.

Adverse result: the contrast is absent after coverage adjustment, reverses in the support-restricted cohort, tracks low measurement density, or is explained by B0 severity/support variables; the HMM finds isolated low-coverage transitions. This supports ascertainment, residual severity, or discharge-selection explanations and should end the direction unless a better measurement source is obtained.

Inconclusive result: sparse dense-cohort membership, fewer than 30 events, wide intervals, missing/invalid units, unstable item labels, poor state separation, calibration failure, or a readiness failure. Then report feasibility and the exact missing evidence; do not select a favorable subgroup or claim a null.

## Exact source bindings

The archive and all required members/fields remain exactly those verified in the parent:

- hosp/patients, member mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz: subject_id,gender,anchor_age; schema hash cb80bb36137e4dd90fc7beac4be87a44751132357c82f054143ea0b9c97443bf.
- hosp/admissions, member mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,hospital_expire_flag; hash 2178417fbbbf78db42ee5e121bcfa42d01f00f7b2542227def83a87151e2904b.
- icu/icustays, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,intime,outtime,los,care units; hash fee9b12a2f13dc8570332e11b36e021570cd487e28ae6f9fc2d18cf95da118de.
- hosp/labevents, member mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/labevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,itemid,charttime,valuenum,valueuom,flag; hash 08b8d6d27183895edd3ffdb6399c8427005ed23821a4e8d88a78a2e8dd05bb65.
- hosp/d_labitems, member mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/d_labitems.csv.gz: itemid,label,fluid,category, creatinine item 50912; hash 3cd809536045e8fc3cc2557f11549939c1b4495295ffdd43fddd10e57a483bdf.
- icu/outputevents, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/outputevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,itemid,charttime,value,valueuom; hash 86beb9fcb0f719aca31d808dd3664604a997bb01870b0def9cb2c44641c2401b. Use only urine items 226559, 226560, 226561.
- icu/d_items, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz: itemid,label,linksto,category,unitname,param_type; hash daa6639c4ab9a469d2889c729d37673c08627ce668cfd808e8a45db4069c4c2e.
- icu/chartevents, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,charttime,itemid,valuenum,value,valueuom; hash 7b739dc2f38c6d791f2cffb46f9b96e57d08b581777a03af0da56b6ae6007d76; MAP item 220052 and frozen manifest-resolved lactate/platelet items.
- icu/inputevents, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/inputevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,starttime,endtime,itemid,amount,amountuom,rate,rateuom,statusdescription; hash 10a879ef5731ed8c2ee8a7cdca3f168b0307ceab91e4e9a31de74739370d1c13; vasopressors 221906, 221289, 221749, 222315.
- icu/procedureevents, member mimic-iv-3.1/icu/procedureevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,starttime,endtime,itemid,value,valueuom,statusdescription; hash 0cbde2f8800a06ba4b2c5057ae6f640fddfc06099929d29aa1fc11ae4f83efe2; ventilation item 225792 and readiness-resolved RRT labels.

The readiness check must fail on missing archive members, any hash mismatch, duplicate item labels, incompatible units, unresolved RRT mapping, invalid time ordering, or empty required item sets. The full archive and source tables remain read-only; only derived manifests, cohort-flow tables, model outputs, and logs may be written.

## Three inspected works

The child reuses the parent’s three frozen, abstract-only inspected works and their byte-matched receipts; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

- [K1] Kellum/KDIGO acute-kidney-injury guideline: supports complementary creatinine and urine-output criteria; it does not establish this ICU-discharge discordance phenotype or its short-horizon prognosis.
- [K2] Haines creatinine-versus-cystatin-C/clearance work: bounds interpretation by showing that creatinine-based renal estimates can be misleading in ICU muscle-loss physiology; it does not provide MIMIC urine ascertainment or test this landmark.
- [K3] Neumann dynamic-eGFR renal-assessment work: supports dynamic assessment as a risk-stratification idea while limiting claims about incremental biomarkers; it does not distinguish persistent EHR discordance from transient charting noise in MIMIC.

A new study would add a fixed landmark, explicit observation-coverage ladder, measured discharge-selection proxies, and a held-out repeated-versus-transient latent comparison. The attached parent receipts remain the source of the exact bibliographic records and hashes; this proposal does not claim to have inspected more than those abstract-only materials.

## Actual deliverable and deferred claims

Completion requires newly generated, frozen outputs: item/label/unit manifest; cohort and exclusion flow; coverage-ladder table; outcome/event table; fixed split; B0/B1 coefficients and held-out predictions; calibrated standardized contrasts with 200-bootstrap intervals; HMM emissions/transitions, masks, persistence summaries, convergence/state-separation diagnostics, and held-out comparisons; and every falsification result with interpretation labels.

The study cannot establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD or renal reserve, tubular injury, fluid balance, complete diuretic exposure, discharge rationale, a renal mechanism, treatment benefit, causality, or transportability beyond this MIMIC snapshot. Those claims require clinical adjudication, richer medication/weight/biomarker data, measured clearance, an external cohort, or an interventional study.

- Source archive: [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip, 10,551,747,784 bytes, SHA-256 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09.
- Join hosp/patients to hosp/admissions by subject_id, then icu/icustays by subject_id,hadm_id. No cross-dataset join is permitted.
- Include age >=18, valid intime < outtime, ICU LOS >=2 days, outtime <= dischtime, first ICU stay for each subject, and alive at t0 = outtime.
- All predictors are strictly before t0: the landmark feature window is [t0-24 hours,t0), and longitudinal bins are the non-overlapping 6-hour intervals from ICU admission through t0. No post-t0 variable is a predictor.
- Primary outcome: the first event in (t0,t0+48 hours] consisting of admissions.deathtime or a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id,hadm_id; censor at admissions.dischtime. Report the two components separately, 7-day event risk, and in-hospital death as secondary outcomes.

The primary estimand remains the standardized observational risk difference (and risk ratio) for the discordant group versus improved/high-output concordance, conditional on measured pre-t0 covariates. The repeated-versus-transient analysis is an explicitly prognostic decomposition, not a causal mediation analysis.

## Ascertainment repair: urine observation is a measured variable

The parent’s requirement of “at least one urine record” is insufficient: one record can be a missed chart, a zero, a partial interval, or a late retrospective total. The experiment must preserve coverage information rather than treating all unobserved volume as zero.

Required urine records are icu/outputevents rows restricted to d_items item IDs 226559 (Foley), 226560 (Void), and 226561 (Condom Cath), joined within the selected stay. Use charttime, numeric nonnegative value, and valueuom; reject incompatible units rather than silently converting. The readiness manifest must prove these item labels are unique and present in icu/d_items.

For each 6-hour bin and the final 24-hour window, construct:

1. urine_volume_observed: sum of valid nonnegative volumes, with no imputation of unobserved volume.
2. urine_n_records: number of valid output rows.
3. urine_active_hours: hours between the earliest and latest valid urine chart time, clipped to the bin/window; this is a documentation-span measure, not a claim of continuous collection.
4. urine_bin_coverage: urine_active_hours / bin_hours, capped at 1.
5. urine_any: an indicator that at least one valid row exists.
6. urine_zero_fraction: fraction of valid rows whose volume is zero.
7. item-source indicators for Foley, Void, and Condom Cath, plus the count of distinct source types.

Coverage is a documentation/measurement proxy, not a validated completeness measure. A record timestamp does not prove that all urine was collected or charted. Define the primary ascertainable cohort as final-window urine_bin_coverage >= 0.75, at least two valid records in each of the four 6-hour bins, and at least one source-type indicator. Preserve the full eligible cohort as a pre-specified observation-sensitivity cohort with coverage features and missingness indicators; do not silently replace it with the dense subset. Also report a complete-case ladder: any record, >=2 records, >=0.75 coverage, and the strict four-bin rule, with cohort flow and outcome counts.

The low-output rule is retained as an operational threshold: total valid volume <400 mL in 24 hours. It is intentionally unweighted because MIMIC binding does not guarantee a valid weight field in this proposal. A weight-indexed analysis is deferred unless a verified weight field and compatible timing are added in a new approved design. Sensitivity checks use continuous volume and the zero/low/high categories, never negative values or unit-mixed sums. Urine data from other item IDs are not used as if they were measured equivalents.

Creatinine remains item 50912 in hosp/labevents, linked to hosp/d_labitems. Require at least two valid creatinine observations at least six hours apart, with the final observation in [t0-24h,t0). Define C_peak as the maximum valid value in that window, C_last as the final value, and improvement as C_peak-C_last >=0.3 mg/dL. Record creatinine count, span, and time since the peak. This makes a two-point improvement distinguishable from a long, repeatedly observed trajectory.

## Residual severity and discharge-selection repair

The study cannot observe the clinical decision to transfer out of ICU, the clinician’s rationale, baseline CKD, complete diuretic exposure, or true fluid balance. Therefore “adjusted beyond severity” is limited to measured proxies and must not be phrased as eliminating confounding or selection.

Use the parent’s exact available fields and add only pre-t0 variables available from the same bound tables:

- age, sex, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-landmark time, and calendar-year/site-independent ICU care-unit category from patients, admissions, and icustays;
- creatinine level/trajectory and observation counts;
- urine volume, coverage, record count, source-type indicators, and missingness;
- last-six-hour and preceding-six-hour MAP summaries from icu/chartevents item 220052, with count and time-since-last measurement;
- available lactate and platelet values from chartevents after a frozen item-manifest lookup, with their measurement indicators and time-since-last values;
- vasopressor exposure indicators and duration/last-active status from icu/inputevents items 221906, 221289, 221749, and 222315, using starttime,endtime,statusdescription;
- invasive ventilation indicator from icu/procedureevents item 225792;
- renal replacement therapy indicators after resolving the procedure/item labels in the frozen readiness manifest.

The discharge-selection sensitivity set is defined before outcome inspection and includes current support (vasopressor/ventilation/RRT), last and preceding MAP, lactate/platelet availability and values, ICU LOS, admission type, care unit, recent measurement intensity, and the interval from admission to t0. Fit the primary model with these measured proxies and a second model restricted to no vasopressor, no invasive ventilation, and no RRT before t0. Compare standardized risks, not only odds ratios. In a descriptive negative-control-style check, ask whether discordance predicts a same-window pre-landmark event or an earlier pseudo-landmark outcome; this is a diagnostic for severity/timing and cannot validate a causal interpretation.

Because conditioning on ICU survival and discharge is part of the design, report the eligible-to-landmark flow and compare excluded patients by observed baseline fields. Do not call the survivor restriction “confounding control.” If discordance is associated with outcome only in sparsely observed or highly supported patients, that supports documentation or discharge-selection explanations. If it remains in the dense, support-restricted set with similar direction and calibration, it is a stronger prognostic regularity but still not a mechanism.

## Baseline versus the longitudinal latent alternative

The method comparison is scientific, not a contest for a small AUROC gain.

B0 is a penalized logistic regression for the primary 48-hour outcome. Exact inputs are age, sex, admission type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 time, C_peak, C_last, creatinine improvement, time since creatinine peak, final 24-hour urine volume, low-output indicator, urine coverage, urine record count/source indicators, last and preceding MAP, available lactate and platelets, vasopressor/ventilation/RRT indicators, and all corresponding measurement/missingness indicators. B1 adds the four-level final-window group: improved/high, improved/low (discordant), not-improved/high, and not-improved/low. Continuous creatinine and urine quantities are retained alongside the group so B1 does not confuse a threshold with information already represented by its components. Use standardization fixed from training data and a prespecified penalty selected on the tuning split.

The bounded alternative is a three-state multivariate HMM/state-space model, fit only if the readiness gate passes, on 6-hour bins from ICU admission to t0. Its emissions use the same measured channels: creatinine level and change, urine volume, urine coverage/record count/source indicators, MAP, available lactate/platelet channels, support indicators, and missingness indicators. Do not interpolate unobserved urine as zero. Use an explicit observation mask and coverage channel; bins with no valid output are missing emissions, not low output. Fit the model on training subjects only; select the number/regularization of states and emission family on the 15% tuning set, with fixed subject-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test membership made before fitting. The test set is untouched until final held-out evaluation. Use 200 patient bootstrap resamples for intervals, with a reproducible seed and patient-level resampling.

The latent model’s scientific target is not “better prediction.” It estimates:

- posterior probability of a renal-observation state at each bin;
- occupancy and number of transitions;
- time since the last transition;
- posterior probability that the final discordance is persistent across at least two prior bins versus isolated to the last bin;
- held-out outcome risk conditional on those summaries.

The specific discriminating comparison is repeated discordance versus transient discordance at matched final-window observed discordance and matched B0 risk. The rival charting-noise explanation predicts that the pattern will be concentrated in low-coverage bins, have unstable state assignments, show little persistence, and lose its association after coverage/support adjustment. A repeated-physiology explanation predicts higher posterior persistence, consistent transitions across bins, and a held-out risk contrast that survives coverage and support-restricted analyses. Neither pattern establishes renal mechanism or causality.

A simpler mechanistic alternative was considered: a deterministic two-compartment filtration/urine-balance model using creatinine change, urine volume, and support/coverage. It is deferred because MIMIC lacks measured GFR, cystatin C in the bound design, fluid composition, reliable body weight, complete diuretic exposure, and a trustworthy creatinine-generation parameter. Fitting such a model would create untestable assumptions rather than reveal filtration. A transformer/LSTM is also deferred because it would add opaque sequence capacity without a separable scientific observable. The HMM is retained only because persistence, transition timing, and observation masking are direct outputs that answer the repeated-versus-transient uncertainty.

Selection rule: if the test set has fewer than 200 subjects or 30 primary events, or if the observation-mask/coverage channels cannot be represented without imputation, do not fit or interpret the HMM; report B0/B1 feasibility and defer the latent question. If state separation is poor (pre-specified emission overlap and transition instability across bootstrap fits), treat the HMM as inconclusive, not as evidence for noise or physiology.

## Analysis, uncertainty, and falsification

Primary analysis:

1. Freeze the item manifest, unit checks, cohort flow, coverage thresholds, outcome construction, and split before fitting.
2. Fit B0 and B1 on training data, tune penalty on tuning data, and report held-out standardized group risks, risk differences/ratios, Brier score, log loss, AUROC/AUPRC as descriptive discrimination, calibration slope/intercept, and calibration plots.
3. Estimate uncertainty with 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of the held-out test predictions for performance and standardized contrasts; for the HMM, repeat posterior summaries within each bootstrap using fixed fitted parameters unless a convergence/fit instability rule requires refitting, which must be stated.
4. Report missingness, coverage, support, and exclusions for each cohort and outcome. Never turn a confidence interval crossing zero into proof of no association.

Prespecified falsification and robustness checks are: permutation of discordance within baseline-risk/ICU-LOS/admission strata; 12-hour versus 48-hour windows; continuous creatinine slope; final-window coverage strata; complete-case ladder; measurement-density and ICU-care-unit strata; no-support restriction; RRT exclusion; creatinine-only, urine-only, and interaction models; and a pseudo-landmark 24 hours before t0. The pseudo-landmark cannot share future data with the primary feature window. A stable result should have directionally similar estimates in the dense and full cohorts, while a documentation artifact should attenuate as coverage and measurement proxies are controlled. These are diagnostic patterns, not causal proof.

Supportive result: in the dense cohort, B1’s discordant contrast is directionally stable with calibrated held-out risk above concordance after measured severity/support adjustment, and the HMM shows reproducible persistence with a held-out risk contrast for repeated versus transient discordance. This supports an observable prognostic phenotype and justifies external validation or adjudicated urine completeness; it does not support delaying discharge or a renal mechanism.

Adverse result: the contrast is absent after coverage adjustment, reverses in the support-restricted cohort, tracks low measurement density, or is explained by B0 severity/support variables; the HMM finds isolated low-coverage transitions. This supports ascertainment, residual severity, or discharge-selection explanations and should end the direction unless a better measurement source is obtained.

Inconclusive result: sparse dense-cohort membership, fewer than 30 events, wide intervals, missing/invalid units, unstable item labels, poor state separation, calibration failure, or a readiness failure. Then report feasibility and the exact missing evidence; do not select a favorable subgroup or claim a null.

The readiness check must fail on missing archive members, any hash mismatch, duplicate item labels, incompatible units, unresolved RRT mapping, invalid time ordering, or empty required item sets. The full archive and source tables remain read-only; only derived manifests, cohort-flow tables, model outputs, and logs may be written.

## Three inspected works

The child reuses the parent’s three frozen, abstract-only inspected works and their byte-matched receipts; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed.

- [K1] Kellum/KDIGO acute-kidney-injury guideline: supports complementary creatinine and urine-output criteria; it does not establish this ICU-discharge discordance phenotype or its short-horizon prognosis.
- [K2] Dejaco iohexol-clearance measurement work: bounds interpretation by showing that creatinine-based renal estimates can be misleading in ICU muscle-loss physiology; it does not provide MIMIC urine ascertainment or test this landmark.
- [K3] Neumann dynamic-eGFR renal-assessment work: supports dynamic assessment as a risk-stratification idea while limiting claims about incremental biomarkers; it does not distinguish persistent EHR discordance from transient charting noise in MIMIC.

A new study would add a fixed landmark, explicit observation-coverage ladder, measured discharge-selection proxies, and a held-out repeated-versus-transient latent comparison. The attached parent receipts remain the source of the exact bibliographic records and hashes; this proposal does not claim to have inspected more than those abstract-only materials.

## Actual deliverable and deferred claims

Completion requires newly generated, frozen outputs: item/label/unit manifest; cohort and exclusion flow; coverage-ladder table; outcome/event table; fixed split; B0/B1 coefficients and held-out predictions; calibrated standardized contrasts with 200-bootstrap intervals; HMM emissions/transitions, masks, persistence summaries, convergence/state-separation diagnostics, and held-out comparisons; and every falsification result with interpretation labels.

The study cannot establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD or renal reserve, tubular injury, fluid balance, complete diuretic exposure, discharge rationale, a renal mechanism, treatment benefit, causality, or transportability beyond this MIMIC snapshot. Those claims require clinical adjudication, richer medication/weight/biomarker data, measured clearance, an external cohort, or an interventional study.

# Episode 4 branch: temporal hypotension signal versus care-process artifacts

Status: proposed substantive child of candidate-5e34d7c66f47264a743e91eb. No cohort scan, label fit, model fit, or result has been computed. This branch preserves the selected eICU question and adds a discriminating temporal/process design; it is not a reproduction of any cited paper.

## Scientific opening, claim, and clinical importance

The unresolved question is whether cumulative systemic hypotension duration carries prognostic information for subsequent creatinine-defined AKI beyond minimum MAP. A residual duration association could still be an artifact of when clinicians measure, how they respond, or how sick patients are at ICU entry. Conversely, a duration signal that is temporally ordered, fixed-nadir, density-robust, and transportable would be useful as a prognostic summary for monitoring and for stratifying a future BP-management study.

H1: in adult first ICU stays that pass BP and creatinine ascertainment gates, covered minutes with systemic MAP <65 during ICU minutes 0–360 add held-out prognostic information for a first creatinine rise during minutes 360–2880 beyond nadir MAP, early physiologic severity, baseline creatinine, and observation-process features; the information has a forward-lag pattern and is not explained by recorded infusion response or hospital-specific practice.

This is not a claim that MAP <65 causes renal injury, that 65 mmHg is a treatment target, that vasopressors help or harm, or that the variable identifies a renal mechanism. The strongest inspected evidence supports narrower premises: hypotension duration/trajectory summaries can be associated with complications in a selected perioperative cohort [K1]; creatinine changes are relevant to AKI definitions [K2]; and randomized BP-target evidence cautions against converting an observational MAP association into a treatment claim [K3]. The unresolved claim is incremental, temporally ordered, transportable prognostic information in eICU after explicit process and treatment diagnostics.

The leading explanation is cumulative hemodynamic stress. The strongest rivals are (1) severity/selection, where duration summarizes unmeasured shock or baseline kidney vulnerability; (2) observation density, where sicker patients are measured more often and both exposure and outcome become easier to observe; (3) treatment response, where low MAP prompts recorded pressor starts; and (4) measurement/timing artifacts from five-minute monitor summaries, modality substitution, lab ordering, and discharge processes. The design can separate these as prognostic/process explanations only. It cannot establish renal hypoperfusion or a causal treatment effect.

## Scientific deliverable

The solver must newly produce a frozen cohort flow and label-readiness audit; held-out predictions and calibrated estimates for B0, B1, and M; a lagged duration table; hospital-cluster uncertainty; fixed-nadir curves; process, treatment, density, modality, threshold, and negative-control outputs; and a decision table classifying results as supportive, adverse, or inconclusive. Readiness or an observed association is not completion. Completion requires all three fits and their falsification outputs, or an explicit label/process stop report that prevents fitting.

## Population, boundaries, joins, and censoring

Use only the read-only eICU 2.0 snapshot 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476e89543643c08b7df637a15ec and catalog 802870bc57f60a7adfb12f5a59267b7cba5e1d61896adb7c6b74a58a1219f14c. The catalog is datasets/eicu/README.md, with full metadata in datasets/eicu/metadata.json and relevant schemas in datasets/eicu/table-*.json. The source directory is [private-path]/eicu数据 库/EICU 2.0数据/. Source archives are gzip files with ordinary CSV members.

Join only on patientunitstayid; use uniquepid only to select the first ICU stay and keep all stays for one uniquepid in one split. Select lowest unitvisitnumber, then earliest unitadmittime24 as tie-break. Adults are numeric age >=18; preserve the >89 category and run a documented age-90 sensitivity. ICU admission is time zero; offsets are minutes relative to admission. There is no unitadmitoffset field.

Eligibility at minute 360 is survival/in-ICU observation through 360, at least 12 valid five-minute BP bins, at least 240 minutes between first and last covered bin, and a valid pre-index serum-creatinine baseline in -24–0. These are exclusions, not imputed negatives.

The primary grid is 72 five-minute bins. Prefer valid vitalPeriodic.systemicmean; if absent use vitalAperiodic.noninvasivemean and retain modality. Do not average modalities and do not use vitalPeriodic.pamean, which is pulmonary-artery mean. Reject MAP outside 30–180 mmHg (20–200 sensitivity), do not interpolate gaps over 10 minutes, and treat absence as missing. Exposure is covered minutes with MAP <65, retaining low-time fraction, nadir, area below 65, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, covered count, median gap, modality mix, and missingness. Threshold sensitivities are 60 and 70.

Primary outcome is the first accepted numeric serum-creatinine result in 360–2880 at least 0.3 mg/dL above the last accepted baseline result in -24–0. Deduplicate same clinical labresultoffset by latest labresultrevisedoffset. Accept only after a frozen audit of labname, labmeasurenamesystem, and labmeasurenameinterface. lab.csv has no units column: never silently convert. If vocabulary or scale is not reproducible, stop the primary fit and report label-readiness failure. Do not parse labresulttext, substitute BUN, or use apacheApsVar.creatinine as a timed outcome. A 1.5-times-baseline/7-day endpoint is a distinct sensitivity, not automatically full KDIGO AKI.

Death before 2880 after eligibility is a competing event. ICU discharge/transfer before 2880 without AKI is censoring, not a negative. A negative requires adequate ascertainment, including an accepted creatinine at or after 2880; otherwise censor. Use patient.unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus, and unitdischargelocation for follow-up status. Fit cause-specific discrete-time and inverse-probability-of-censoring/observation sensitivities, and report event, competing, censoring, and unclassified counts. carePlanEOL is a process flag, not evidence of intent.
