|---|---|---|---|
| `patient` | `patient.csv.gz`, `2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b` | `patientunitstayid`, `uniquepid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, age, gender, ethnicity, hospitalid, unitadmittime24, unitvisitnumber, unitstaytype, unitdischargeoffset, unitdischargestatus | first-stay selection, index, censoring |
| `vitalPeriodic` | `vitalPeriodic.csv.gz`, `329b522f97f7d3d0cb4541e4fc4afc32048eb8fd0f8c9b156907f845a992906c` | `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `systemicmean`, heart rate, respiration | primary BP sequence |
| `vitalAperiodic` | `vitalAperiodic.csv.gz`, `8b23e5a50f8aabc6cb62fc69e2dcdf755a2e5649b1439a7ca413a7c5b2d5a9a0` | `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `noninvasivemean` | fallback BP modality |
| `lab` | `lab.csv.gz`, `91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a` | `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, name fields, numeric result, revision offset | label/ascertainment |
| `infusionDrug` | `infusionDrug.csv.gz`, `f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b` | `patientunitstayid`, `infusionoffset`, `drugname`, drugrate, infusionrate, drugamount, volumeoffluid, patientweight | conservative treatment/process proxy |
| `hospital` | `hospital.csv.gz`, `16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6` | hospitalid, numbedscategory, teachingstatus, region | hospital grouping/context |
| `apacheApsVar` | `apacheApsVar.csv.gz`, `4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4` | patientunitstayid, admission creatinine/dialysis/urine/meanbp; no time | baseline sensitivity only |
| `carePlanEOL` | `carePlanEOL.csv.gz`, `8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0` | patientunitstayid, cpleolsaveoffset, cpleoldiscussionoffset, activeupondischarge | index process markers only if offset <=360 |
| `intakeOutput` | `intakeOutput.csv.gz`, `f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121` | offsets, output/dialysis totals, cell label/value fields | descriptive/adjudication sensitivity only |

The source schemas were inspected from the complete eICU catalog and table JSONs: `lab` has no units column; `vitalPeriodic` contains `systemicmean` and a distinct pulmonary-artery `pamean`; `vitalAperiodic` contains `noninvasivemean`; `infusionDrug` has an offset but no explicit stop time or verified unit/indication; and `carePlanEOL` has offset fields but `activeupondischarge` is an end-of-stay field. Use `systemicmean`, never `pamean`, and join tables only on `patientunitstayid`.

Select one ICU stay per `uniquepid`: lowest `unitvisitnumber), then earliest `unitadmittime24`. Include age >=18, preserve >89 as a category, and keep each `hospitalid` intact for splitting. Index is ICU admission because there is no unit-admit offset. Require at least 12 valid 5-minute BP bins and at least 240 minutes between first and last covered bin in 0–360. Report a flow table with every exclusion.

## Exposure representations

Create 72 fixed bins `[5k,5(k+1))), k=0,...,71. Within a bin, use the median valid `systemicmean`; if no valid systemic value exists, use the median valid `noninvasivemean` and mark modality=noninvasive. Do not interpolate across gaps >10 minutes or turn missingness into normal physiology. Retain value mask, modality, time since last observation, covered-bin count, median gap, and early BP missingness. Exposure summaries are covered minutes with MAP<65 (primary), low-time fraction, area below 65, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, and nadir; use 60/70 thresholds and 30–180 minutes only as frozen sensitivities.

## Matched scalar baseline versus temporal alternative

All models target the same three-interval competing-risk prediction task and use identical hospital splits, censoring weights, and feature normalization rules. The baseline comparison is:

- **B0 (severity/process baseline):** regularized discrete-time cause-specific regression with age, gender, ethnicity, hospital/ICU type, baseline creatinine, admission APS meanbp/creatinine where available, initial MAP/heart rate/respiration, pre-index creatinine/BP counts, BP coverage/missingness/modality/gaps, and prespecified <=360-minute EOL/process markers. It contains no early MAP duration, nadir, or trajectory shape.
- **B1 (scalar estimand model):** B0 plus covered minutes MAP<65, low-time fraction, area, episode count, first-low offset, recovery slope, and restricted spline of duration, with fixed-nadir bands and common-support restrictions. The primary contrast B1-B0 estimates incremental prognostic value of the early duration/nadir summary, not a causal effect.
- **M (temporal alternative):** a one-layer GRU with hidden width 32 and dropout 0.1, with one sigmoid/softmax head for the same three follow-up intervals. It receives the same 72-bin sequence of MAP, heart rate, respiration, modality, observation mask, time-since-last-observation, and early recorded-pressor indicators only in a treatment-inclusive ablation; the primary M masks treatment inputs. It receives B0 baseline covariates through the head. It is trained only in training hospitals, early-stopped/calibrated in validation hospitals, and evaluated once in held-out hospitals.

M is scientifically substantive because two stays can have the same duration and nadir but differ in repeated isolated lows versus one persistent episode, order of recovery, oscillation, and whether a low precedes renewed observation. B1 discards that order; M can test whether the distinction changes later risk after matching scalar burden. To prevent a small predictive gain from becoming the scientific claim, report an order-destroying sensitivity that permutes complete observed bin tuples (value, mask, modality, time-since-last-observation, treatment proxy) within each stay while retaining the scalar summaries. If original and permuted M perform similarly, any gain is not evidence for temporal ordering.

Training target: discrete-time three-state prediction for each interval (creatinine event, death/competing endpoint, no event), with inverse-probability-of-censoring/observation weights fitted in training hospitals only. Fit B0, B1, and M with the same weighted proper loss; use the same risk-set definition. M is not fit if the label gate or minimum event/hospital-support criteria fail.

Use deterministic whole-hospital splits: hash `episode5|hospitalid` with SHA-256, assign sorted hashes 60% train, 20% validation, 20% test; every `uniquepid` and all its stays remain in one split. If the prespecified minimum hospital/event counts make one split infeasible, use five-fold grouped-hospital cross-validation with one untouched fold for final evaluation and report that deviation before viewing test performance. Fit scalers, vocabulary, model selection, calibration, nuisance models, and censoring/observation weights on training data only.

Primary uncertainty and scores: hospital-cluster bootstrap (at least 1,000 resamples) of held-out differences in Brier score and log loss at 720, 1440, and 2880 minutes, calibration intercept/slope, calibration curves, and cumulative-incidence risk curves. AUROC/AUPRC are secondary. Report hospital, stay, event, competing-event, censoring, and label-readiness counts. No threshold is selected from test results.

## Process/treatment rivals and falsification

Fit a separate observation-process model for any valid post-360 creatinine measurement and time to first measurement, using the same frozen vocabulary without the rise requirement. Strong duration-to-testing association is evidence compatible with ascertainment/clinical-concern coupling; it is not proof of bias. Apply observation weights only when their positivity/support diagnostics pass.

Use a pre-index negative-control event: among stays with valid creatinine in -48 to -24 and a distinct result in -24 to 0, apply the same +0.3 rule before the exposure window. A comparable or stronger association is adverse evidence for baseline severity/measurement process, not causal proof. Use common-support strata fixed before test evaluation: nadir band, covered count, baseline creatinine band, initial vitals, BP modality/missingness, and S/O/T propensity overlap. Refit all nuisance models in each training fold; never residualize or select strata with test information.

The infusion table supports only conservative recorded-pressor indicators/timing and possibly raw-field summaries after a name/field audit; it has no verified stop time, dose unit, or treatment indication. Compare treatment-masked primary models with treatment-inclusive ablations. Loss after treatment inclusion is compatible with treatment-response/recorded-severity coupling; persistence does not identify a causal effect.

Use `carePlanEOL.cpleolsaveoffset` and `cpleoldiscussionoffset` only when <=360 for index predictors. Never use post-index EOL rows or `activeupondischarge` as predictors; post-index EOL may be descriptive censoring context only. A broken-linkage negative control may permute complete early BP trajectories within hospital x nadir band x coverage stratum while keeping outcomes/B0 fixed; the incremental temporal signal should disappear.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive scalar result: label gate passes; B1 improves held-out Brier/log loss over B0 with hospital-cluster uncertainty excluding no improvement; duration-risk is coherent within fixed-nadir/common-support strata; the gain survives density thinning, modality and threshold sensitivities, process weighting, and hospital holdout; and no comparable pre-index negative-control association is present. This supports an independently useful prognostic scalar summary only.

Supportive trajectory result: M improves the same held-out scores over B1, is calibrated across hospitals, and original-versus-order-permuted M shows a prespecified loss of temporal information. This supports useful ordering/recovery information beyond duration/nadir. If M adds no stable information while B1 is stable, the scalar summary is adequate for this question. If M adds information but B1 does not, the duration estimand is insufficient and the next study should focus on trajectory descriptors. Neither outcome establishes renal hypoperfusion, causality, a MAP target, or treatment benefit.

Adverse result: label readiness fails; B1's gain is matched by the observation-process model or pre-index control; gain disappears after observation weighting, density thinning, common-support restriction, hospital holdout, or recorded-treatment adjustment; M learns only masks/treatment; or original and order-permuted M are equivalent. These favor ascertainment, selection, treatment-response, severity, or non-temporal explanations.

Inconclusive result: missing units leave scale unresolved, eligible events are too few, hospital support is inadequate, censoring/observation positivity fails, intervals are wide, or model rankings reverse across prespecified splits. Do not call an imprecise null a refutation. Obtain clinical laboratory/nephrology adjudication, validated treatment and urine/dialysis semantics, and independent external data before stronger claims.

The verifier can check snapshot/source hashes, joins, exact windows, first-stay selection, binning, no future EOL leakage, split integrity, training-only preprocessing, held-out predictions, uncertainty, and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot adjudicate laboratory units/analyte identity, BP modality validity, clinical intent, residual unmeasured severity, mechanism, or causal benefit. Those require expert review or another study.

## Alternatives, resource budget, and deliverable

A simple scalar regression is retained because it directly estimates the parent’s duration-versus-nadir question and is auditable. The GRU is retained because it can test a distinct ordering/recovery hypothesis on the exact same inputs and target, not because it is more complex. A temporal convolution of two width-3 layers with 32 channels is the preregistered implementation substitute if GRU library/runtime support fails; it receives the identical sequence and loss. A latent state-space model is deferred because perfusion/congestion/renal biomarkers and validated state labels are unavailable. A transformer is deferred because it adds capacity without a distinct scientific uncertainty. A causal vasopressor model is deferred because dose units, stops, indications, and assignment are unavailable. Revisit these choices only with validated units/intent, adjudicated labels, richer physiologic data, or external validation.

Task-specific deliverable: newly fit B0, B1, residualized/common-support contrasts, observation-process model, and M when the label/support gate passes; held-out predictions, calibration, hospital-cluster uncertainty, flow/label audit, fixed-nadir and temporal-order checks, process/treatment/negative-control outputs, and resource logs. Discovery inspected schemas and ran a bounded full streaming vocabulary/scale diagnostic; it did not fit the proposed clinical models. Future solver planning envelope is 16 CPU, up to 8 GPU, 262144 MiB, 28800 seconds. Use CPU for B0/B1; request one allocated GPU for M only if a measured bounded probe shows a material runtime benefit, and use `cuda:0` inside the allocation. # MIMIC-IV renal-discordance: longitudinal discriminator repair

Status: planned design only. No patient rows were read, no cohort was fitted, and no clinical result is claimed.

Parent: candidate-9bd7a428ee4ae729076c3694. This child preserves the parent population, first-ICU-discharge landmark, non-causal 48-hour estimand, exact verified MIMIC bindings, and the inherited three-work evidence package. The substantive repair is to replace “matched as closely as feasible on B0 risk” with a nested, leakage-safe comparison that separates a transparent repeated-pattern summary from the masked HMM.

## Scientific opening and claim boundary

Creatinine and urine output are complementary renal observations, but the parent question remains unresolved: does a fall in creatinine without adequately observed urine recovery immediately before ICU discharge identify a reproducible short-horizon prognostic phenotype, and does recurrence across an earlier period distinguish persistent observed physiology from a transient threshold or documentation episode?

[K1] supports the complementary creatinine/urine assessment premise but does not test this landmark phenotype. [K2] bounds interpretation by reporting measured-clearance evidence that creatinine-based estimates can be misleading during critical illness and muscle loss; it does not establish MIMIC urine ascertainment or prognosis. [K3] supports dynamic renal assessment as a risk-stratification idea while limiting claims about incremental biomarkers; it does not distinguish persistent EHR discordance from transient charting noise. These works do not establish the unresolved MIMIC claim.

The falsifiable claim is:

> Among adults surviving a first ICU stay of at least 48 hours, with dense and valid urine observation, creatinine improvement without observed urine-output recovery in [t0-24 hours,t0) is associated with higher first-48-hour post-discharge risk of ICU readmission or in-hospital death beyond measured pre-t0 severity and discharge-selection proxies; recurrence in the immediately preceding non-overlapping 24-hour window supplies additional held-out prognostic information beyond the final-window phenotype, and a masked HMM supplies further information only if its transition/persistence summaries outperform that transparent recurrence comparator.

This is a standardized observational prognostic comparison, not an intervention effect. It cannot establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD, renal reserve, fluid balance, tubular injury, a renal mechanism, causality, a discharge decision effect, or transportability.

The clinical advance is a boundary test. A positive final-window association that disappears with coverage or support adjustment is evidence for ascertainment or selection. A stable repeated-versus-transient contrast would show that the observed temporal pattern has prognostic information beyond a single discharge snapshot. If the HMM adds nothing beyond a simple prior-window indicator and coverage summaries, the clinically useful conclusion is that latent-state complexity is unnecessary for this question.

## Population, landmark and outcome

Use only the frozen MIMIC-IV 3.1 source. Include adults with patients.anchor_age >= 18; a valid first ICU stay per subject_id with intime < outtime and los >= 2 days; a linked admission; outtime <= admissions.dischtime; and survival to t0 = icustays.outtime. A death time earlier than t0 is an exclusion/data-quality failure, not a post hoc outcome assignment.

The primary outcome is the first event in (t0, t0 + 48 hours] and before or at admissions.dischtime:

1. admissions.deathtime, or
2. a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id and hadm_id with intime > t0.

Keep ICU readmission and death separate. Secondary outcomes are the component events, 7-day in-hospital composite, and time to the primary component. Do not infer an event time from hospital_expire_flag when deathtime is unusable; report that exception and apply the frozen time-to-event rule.

All predictors precede t0. The primary final window is [t0-24 hours,t0). Longitudinal bins are non-overlapping 6-hour bins from icustays.intime through t0, with partial first-bin duration retained. MIMIC timestamps are subject-shifted; no cross-subject calendar alignment is used.

## Exact measurements and discordance definition

Creatinine is restricted to hosp/labevents itemid=50912, linked to hosp/d_labitems. Retain finite, positive valuenum values with verified compatible valueuom (canonical mg/dL); exclude and report incompatible or unitless values rather than silently converting. In a 24-hour window, require at least two observations at least 6 hours apart, with the final valid observation inside the window. Let C_peak be the maximum and C_last the final valid value; creatinine improvement is C_peak-C_last >= 0.3 mg/dL. Retain count, observation span and time since peak.

Urine is restricted to icu/outputevents itemid 226559 (Foley), 226560 (Void), or 226561 (Condom Cath), with finite nonnegative value, valueuom=mL, and charttime inside the selected stay/window. Sum valid values; absent rows are not zero. Retain row count, source indicators, zero fraction, earliest/latest charttime and observed-span. Span is documentation timing, not proof of complete collection.

The dense primary ascertainment rule is at least two valid urine rows in each of the four final 6-hour bins and at least one verified source type. The full eligible cohort and a frozen ladder (any valid row; at least two final-window rows; at least one row in every final bin; strict two rows per final bin) are reported separately. Low output is total observed urine <400 mL/24 hours, deliberately unweighted because a validated, time-aligned weight field is not bound. Continuous volume and documentation measures are retained.

Final-window groups remain improved/high-output, improved/low-output (discordant), not-improved/high-output, and not-improved/low-output. These are descriptive observed groups, not diagnoses.

## The repaired method comparison

### B0/B1 final-window baseline

B0 is penalized logistic regression for the primary composite. Its verified inputs are age, gender, admission_type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 duration, first_careunit and last_careunit, creatinine level/trajectory and observation intensity, final-window urine volume/low-output/row count/observed span/source/zero fraction, MAP summaries and measurement indicators, vasopressor exposure and duration/last-active status, invasive-ventilation exposure and duration/status, and explicit missingness indicators.

MAP is icu/chartevents itemid 220052. Vasopressors are icu/inputevents itemids 221906, 221289, 221749 and 222315, using starttime, endtime and statusdescription. Ventilation is icu/procedureevents itemid 225792, using starttime, endtime and statusdescription. Transfer context from hosp/transfers is a pre-t0 selection diagnostic.

B1 adds the four-level final-window group while retaining continuous component measurements and documentation fields. B1 versus B0 asks whether the thresholded discordance grouping adds information beyond its measured ingredients. B0/B1 do not contain any post-t0 value.

### B2: transparent longitudinal baseline

B2 adds one pre-specified longitudinal comparison to B1. Define the immediately preceding, non-overlapping window P=[t0-48 hours,t0-24 hours) using exactly the same creatinine, urine, units, and coverage rules as the final window. Define prior discordance D_P=1 only when P has the required creatinine improvement and observed urine <400 mL with strict four-bin urine coverage. The final discordance D_F is defined identically in [t0-24,t0).

B2 includes D_P, a prior-window-valid indicator, prior urine row count/span/source/zero-fraction, prior creatinine count/span/time-since-peak, and prior continuous urine volume and creatinine change. Its focal descriptive contrast is:
- repeated: D_F=1 and D_P=1;
- transient: D_F=1 and D_P=0 with prior-window validity;
- not-final-discordant: D_F=0.

No missing prior window is called transient. B2 is the simple baseline because it makes recurrence explicit, uses a non-overlapping historical window, and preserves documentation information. It is fitted with the same penalized logistic family and same outcome as B0/B1. Thus B1-to-B2 measures the information in a transparent recurrence summary.

### L1: masked HMM, tested beyond B2

L1 is a three-state masked HMM over the 6-hour sequence from ICU intime to t0. Per-bin channels are creatinine last value and adjacent observed change, urine volume, urine row count, observed span, source indicators, zero fraction, MAP, vasopressor/ventilation support, and explicit masks. Unobserved urine is a missing emission, never zero. A partial first bin retains duration. Only verified item IDs and fields listed above enter the primary model; unresolved lactate, platelet and renal-replacement mappings are deferred and cannot appear by assumption.

Fit the HMM on training subjects only. Tune emission family/regularization on the tuning subjects using unsupervised sequence likelihood and state-stability criteria; the test outcomes remain untouched. State labels are not biological labels. For each subject, export only pre-specified, label-invariant summaries: expected adjacent transition count; posterior probability that adjacent latent states remain equal through the final four bins; posterior probability of remaining in the same latent state across the boundary between P and the final window; occupancy/observation-mask summaries; and time since the last inferred transition. These are trajectory descriptors, not claims about renal mechanisms.

The outcome model for the HMM comparison is B2 plus the limited HMM summaries, with penalty selected on the tuning split. This nested comparison is essential: L1 must beat B2 to demonstrate information beyond final-window measurements, transparent recurrence, and documentation. An HMM improvement over B1 alone is not sufficient.

The charting-noise/discharge-selection rival predicts that B2 and L1 recurrence is concentrated in low-coverage or high-support records, that latent transitions are unstable, and that held-out risk separation attenuates after documentation and support adjustment. A persistent-observed-pattern explanation predicts stable recurrence and a transition/persistence contrast that remains in dense and support-restricted analyses. Neither explanation proves biological renal recovery.

A deterministic filtration/fluid-balance model is deferred because the bound data do not provide measured GFR, complete urine collection, fluid composition, validated creatinine-generation parameters, reliable time-aligned weight, or complete diuretic exposure. A transformer/LSTM is deferred because added opaque capacity would not supply a more direct observable than B2/HMM transition summaries. These are question-specific decisions, not blanket exclusions of neural networks or GPU use.

## Split, fitting, evaluation and uncertainty

Create one patient-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test split before fitting, using the first-ICU subject population and a recorded fixed seed/hash rule. Reuse this membership for B0, B1, B2 and L1. Fit all preprocessing on train only, select logistic penalties and any HMM hyperparameters on tune only, and inspect test outcomes once.

Report held-out standardized risks and risk difference/risk ratio for final discordance versus improved/high-output, and for repeated versus transient among D_F=1 with valid P. Standardize comparisons over fixed B1-risk strata whose cutpoints are learned from training predictions, plus the pre-specified dense/full and no-support restrictions. Report Brier score, log loss, calibration slope/intercept and calibration plots; AUROC/AUPRC are descriptive only. Report paired held-out deltas B1-B0, B2-B1 and L1-B2, not a leaderboard.

Use 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of held-out predictions for uncertainty in all risks, contrasts and proper-score deltas. Report test size, event count, and repeated/transient group sizes. For HMM state stability, use label-invariant summaries in bounded train-resampling diagnostics; failure to converge or unstable summaries is inconclusive, not evidence for either rival.

The HMM must not be fit or interpreted if the test set has fewer than 200 subjects or 30 primary events, if masks require imputation, if either repeated or transient focal group has fewer than 20 test subjects, or if required train/tune support is absent. A fit is inconclusive if a state occupies <5% of training bins, median maximum posterior state probability is <0.60, convergence fails, or label-invariant persistence/transition summaries are directionally stable in fewer than 80% of the pre-specified stability refits.

L1 is scientifically retained only when it shows a reproducible transition/persistence pattern, an incremental held-out proper-score result over B2 whose paired bootstrap interval excludes zero, and a repeated-versus-transient risk contrast that remains directionally consistent across dense/full and support-restricted checks. A small score improvement without a distinct stable temporal contrast is prediction complexity, not a clinical advance; defer the HMM and retain B0-B2. No clinical utility or treatment threshold is claimed.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze before test-outcome review: archive/member/schema/item checks; cohort flow; coverage ladder; 12-hour and 48-hour follow-up; continuous creatinine change; measurement-density and ICU-care-unit strata; no-support restriction; permutation of final discordance within ICU-LOS/admission/B1-risk strata; creatinine-only and urine-only models; and a pseudo-landmark 24 hours before t0 constructed only from data before that pseudo-landmark. A pseudo-landmark is a timing diagnostic, not a second causal analysis.

Supportive evidence is a calibrated dense-cohort final-window contrast after measured severity/support adjustment, a stable repeated-versus-transient contrast in B2, and an additional stable, held-out L1 transition/persistence contrast beyond B2. This supports an observable prognostic regularity and justifies external validation or clinical adjudication of urine completeness.

Adverse evidence is attenuation/reversal after coverage or support restriction, concentration in sparse documentation, a permutation contrast comparable to the observed contrast, or L1 transitions dominated by low-density bins with no incremental evidence over B2. This supports ascertainment, residual severity or discharge selection and argues against paying the complexity cost of HMM.

Inconclusive evidence includes invalid units or times, hash/schema/item mismatch, unresolved outcome timestamps, too few events/groups, calibration failure, HMM instability, or wide uncertainty. Report the exact limitation without converting it to a null or favorable subgroup.

Computationally checkable claims are source/member/schema availability, leakage-free cohort/split construction, model fitting, held-out predictions, uncertainty, transition summaries and whether interpretations match those outputs. Complete urine collection, true filtration, CKD/renal reserve, mechanism, discharge rationale, causality, clinical utility and transportability require clinical adjudication, richer measurements, external validation or another study.

# Context-specific MerTK target prioritization in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial coculture

Status: Lead design, planned experiment; no scientific screening result has been executed. Episode 1, crossover of D2-T1 and D2-T2.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The available evidence supports two facts but leaves an actionable boundary unresolved. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response; the inspected source also reports that MerTK inhibition increases FLS IL6 and MMP1/3/14 [K1]. Separately, HBEGF-positive macrophages can drive an invasive FLS program [K2], and fibroblast pathology is heterogeneous across immune-interacting and vascular-interacting states [K3]. These findings do not establish that MerTK perturbation has the same consequence in every macrophage context, nor that a MerTK-directed intervention should be selected without stratifying protective versus inflammatory macrophage states.

Falsifiable hypothesis: in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial FLS coculture, MerTK inhibition produces a larger inflammatory FLS response when the macrophage context is MerTK/CD206-positive (resolution-like) than when it is MerTK/CD206-negative, after accounting for contributing FLS/macrophage donors and generic LPS stimulation. The clinically consequential extension is that a MerTK-preservation or activation strategy should be considered state-stratified: patients or cocultures enriched for the MerTK-positive/CD206-positive resolution context should show the greatest avoidable fibroblast harm from MerTK loss. This is a hypothesis about a perturbation-by-context interaction, not a claim that MerTK activation is already an effective treatment.

The strongest available claim is a broad protective association/perturbational effect, not clinical efficacy or direct target causality. The strongest rival is that the observed FLS changes are generic inflammatory or stress responses, cell-composition/sorting proxies, donor/reuse artifacts, or assay timing effects; under that rival, inhibitor effects should not show a reproducible CD206-context interaction after donor-aware adjustment. [K2] makes the macrophage-state alternative consequential, while [K3] motivates separating FLS state readouts from mere bulk expression changes. The proposed advance over [K1] is a state-by-perturbation safety/selection test, not another broad MerTK expression association.

## Population, boundaries, and exact data bindings

Primary population: all 33 recorded pseudobulk FLS samples in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 matrix, restricted to samples whose design row has cell_type=type B synovial cell, tissue=synovial membrane, and a documented co-culture condition. Primary contrasts are macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor versus no treatment within condition=co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages and, as the context comparator, the corresponding CD206neg condition. No raw cell is treated as an independent donor.

Required primary inputs and keys:

- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz (catalog SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f): table with feature row key and 33 sample-ID columns. Verified measured feature columns include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.

Estimate the inhibitor-by-context interaction jointly with crossed FLS and macrophage donor effects, allowing feature-specific residual covariance. The model's target is not a predictive label; it is the posterior distribution of the context-specific perturbation effect and the probability that the interaction exceeds a prespecified scientifically meaningful direction. Fit by CPU using a reproducible Bayesian or penalized-likelihood implementation; no GPU is needed for this small table. If the donor design is too sparse to identify the latent model, defer it and report the baseline only.
5. Compare the baseline and mechanistic alternative on scientific information: sign and uncertainty of the same interaction estimand, leave-one-donor-cluster-out stability, posterior/cluster-bootstrap predictive checks, and whether the alternative changes interpretation by separating a correlated macrophage state from the FLS harm outcome. Do not rank by small predictive improvement. No random train/test split is appropriate for this finite hypothesis test; the held-out unit is a donor cluster. The future solver must report coefficient/effect tables, donor membership and exclusions, uncertainty intervals or posterior intervals, feature-level and score-level outputs, sensitivity analyses, and diagnostic plots/data.
6. Compute a bounded negative control: the LPS-treated versus untreated contrast within the same macrophage context where present. # Donor-aware identifiability of context-selective MerTK harm in RA synovial coculture

Status: substantive child of candidate-8d4724c711ef0520a9b2f872; planned Harbor experiment only. No molecular screening or result has been executed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports a broad claim: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair, and MerTK inhibition has been reported with increased FLS inflammatory transcripts [K1]. It does not establish that the perturbation is more harmful in the MerTK/CD206-positive context than in the CD206-negative context. That unresolved boundary matters for target prioritization: a MerTK-preservation or activation strategy could be selectively attractive only if loss of the resolution-like macrophage context produces a materially larger fibroblast harm program, rather than a generic response to perturbation or assay stress.

The falsifiable hypothesis is unchanged: in RA type-B synovial FLS coculture, macrophage MerTK inhibition produces a larger FLS inflammatory harm response in the MerTK/CD206-positive context than in the CD206-negative context, after accounting for contributing FLS and macrophage memberships. The clinical-research implication is a context-stratified next-step decision, not a claim of clinical efficacy or that MerTK activation is already a treatment.

The strongest rival explanations are generic LPS/stress signaling, altered cell composition or capture, donor and assay-round confounding, and timing or preparation-label artifacts. They predict either a similar effect under LPS, a signal in FLS-only samples, instability after donor-aware mapping, or no coherent marker-level interaction. [K2] makes an inflammatory macrophage-state explanation consequential; [K3] cautions that FLS inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked. [K1] supports the starting perturbational observation, but does not identify this state-by-perturbation interaction. The substantive advance is an explicit identifiability and decision-usefulness test under the actual sparse design.

## Population and exact data bindings

The primary population is the 33 recorded pseudobulk columns in:

- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f. It is a feature-row table with the sample IDs in the header and 445 measured features. Required measured transcript columns are MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. It has one row per matrix column and the fields sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Join only on design.sample_id = counts header sample ID. The comma-separated donor_id memberships are dependence annotations, not a single donor identifier.
- [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab1bd1a31c77b7f70f. This records 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors, and prohibits ordinary donor t-tests.
- E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt, SHA-256 4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719, plus the registered R1, R2 and R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz archive members listed in datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json. These are lineage/source members, not extra observations; the prepared pseudobulk table is the analysis table.

Eligible rows must have tissue=synovial membrane, cell_type=type B synovial cell and a documented co-culture condition. The primary context variables are MerTK/CD206pos versus MerTK/CD206neg. The mixed rows R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg and R5_SA263R_FLS_SA278R_1Mpos_SA277A_3Mneg are context-ambiguous and are excluded from the primary interaction, retained as descriptive composition controls. The not-co-cultured rows, including R1_SA256A_FLS_Inhibitor, are not primary coculture observations; the six FLS-only rows are a control stratum.

The exact treated rows are R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor. R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor are a separate preInhibitor tier. The parent’s count of five treated rows is retained, but the tiers are never silently merged: exact inhibitor is primary; preInhibitor is secondary only if protocol metadata establishes equivalence. The untreated counterpart R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos has conflicting donor_id metadata, including SA256A versus SA256A, SA260R and a recorded metadata conflict, so it is sensitivity-only. No donor label is repaired by inference. All measured samples are assay conditions, not clinical time points; no longitudinal boundary or clinical treatment transition exists.

Secondary sources remain accessible and read-only but are not pooled or joined by matching IDs:

- E-MTAB-8316 counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81. Its six verified within-other_donor_id none versus UNC106238 pairs are nested in four verified donors (SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049); use only as a paired exploratory state/perturbation context after reconciling labels and protocol. It has no time field.
- E-MTAB-8322 counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json, SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da. It has 27 macrophage pseudobulk columns across healthy, treatment-naive RA, remission, resistant RA and undifferentiated arthritis. Its Ensembl feature IDs lack a configured feature map, so target-module scoring is blocked pending a named frozen annotation release; use state metadata descriptively only and exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from independent-donor inference.
- GSE95588 source and prepared tables remain bound for provenance/rival context: GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz, GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz, series.soft, samples.soft, and their registered prepared matrices/designs/feature maps. Donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved and the coculture branch includes earlier GSE57723 material; no donor-aware inferential claim or independent validation uses it.

## Estimand and identifiability gate

Normalize the measured feature rows per sample to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserving transcript identifiers and without imputing unmeasured genes. Before modeling, emit a manifest with every included row, exposure tier, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, context, cells, exclusions and mapping scenario.

The primary outcome is a prespecified FLS harm score H: the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen from the eligible untreated coculture reference rows; if a required feature is absent from the exact header, the score is unavailable rather than repaired. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12, MMP13 and each primary component. The context panel is MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1; it is descriptive of the state and cannot prove direct target engagement.

The primary estimand is

  Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)]
          - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]

with donor membership treated as crossed dependence, not as independent observations. Because the prepared design contains only one exact-inhibitor Mneg row and two unambiguous exact-inhibitor Mpos rows, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-FLS/macrophage-pair context comparison. Therefore the interaction is not automatically identifiable as a population-level causal effect. The solver must first report a rank/overlap gate: treatment-context cells, exact matched counterpart availability, donor membership overlap, and whether Delta can be estimated without using the ambiguous row or the preInhibitor tier. A rank-deficient or overlap-failing primary model returns inconclusive, not a zero effect.

The primary baseline is a transparent paired-score/interaction analysis. Construct within-round matched differences wherever the design explicitly supports the same FLS/macrophage membership, then estimate exact-exposure context contrasts with a small fixed-effects model including context, exposure, their interaction and assay round only when estimable. Represent every contributing FLS and macrophage donor with a membership incidence matrix; use a cross-classified random-intercept or penalized fixed-effect formulation only if its rank is documented. Do not include age or sex as if independently varying when age is round-confounded and all rows are female. Report feature-level effects, H effects, donor-cluster bootstrap intervals, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out sensitivity, and exact mapping scenarios. Ordinary donor t-tests, cell-level replication and random row splits are prohibited.

The LPS rows are a bounded generic-inflammatory control: compare preLPS with untreated within context where available and ask whether the marker pattern and context contrast are reproduced. FLS-only rows test whether a response appears without macrophages. Neither control establishes MerTK specificity; both can falsify a selective interpretation. Mixed-composition rows test whether changing Mpos:Mneg mixture alone tracks H and are not used as clean context labels.

## Substantive alternative on the same inputs

The alternative is a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model, not a different question. On the same log-CPM outcome matrix and the same frozen manifest, model the primary and secondary FLS features jointly with feature-specific intercepts, exposure-tier effect, context effect, exposure-by-context effect, assay-round effect, and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads on IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14; a separate macrophage-context factor uses MERTK, MRC1 and TREM2, with SPP1 and IL1B retained as an inflammatory contrast rather than forced into the resolution factor. Feature-specific residual covariance allows correlated markers to contribute uncertainty jointly.

Its fitting target is the posterior or penalized-likelihood distribution of the same Delta, the two context-specific exposure effects, the shared-harm loading coherence and the probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold. It is not trained to predict a label. Fit only after design-rank checks; if the one-Mneg treated cluster or the ambiguous memberships make the latent model non-identifiable, record the attempted model and defer it rather than replacing it with a simpler unannounced fit. Compare the alternative with the baseline by sign, interval width, donor/mapping stability and marker coherence. The information gained is whether a seemingly single-marker interaction is a correlated FLS program and whether partial pooling makes uncertainty widen or shrink appropriately; the score baseline loses that structure but is more transparent under sparsity.

The held-out unit is an assay round or donor-membership cluster for leave-one-cluster-out sensitivity. With only R1, R2 and R5 and unbalanced treatment, this is a stability diagnostic, not external validation. Use posterior predictive or residual checks for the fitted model, not predictive accuracy as the scientific criterion. The estimated future solver cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB memory and minutes for this 33-by-11 feature table; full runtime is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the matrix is small and the scientific uncertainty is design/identifiability, not computational scale.

Deferred alternatives are: a neural expression predictor, because predictive improvement cannot answer whether the interaction is causal or decision-useful; a pooled analysis that merges exact inhibitor and preInhibitor, because protocol equivalence is unavailable; ordinary differential expression t-tests, because donor dependence is explicitly unresolved; E-MTAB-8322 target scoring, because the feature namespace lacks a configured map; and GSE95588 validation, because donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved. These alternatives can be revisited only after the named missing dependency is supplied or the question changes.

## Supportive, adverse and inconclusive rule

Define a material harm threshold delta = 0.5 SD of H, fixed before fitting. A result is supportive only if the exact-exposure Delta is positive and its uncertainty supports Delta > delta (or the equivalent prespecified posterior probability is at least 0.90), the sign is unchanged across admissible donor mappings and round/membership holdouts, the primary marker components are directionally coherent, and neither LPS nor FLS-only controls reproduces the same selective pattern. This supports a balanced orthogonal follow-up to test state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation; it does not justify a clinical treatment or patient-selection claim.

A result is adverse if Delta is nonpositive or Mneg harm is at least as large, or if generic LPS/stress or FLS-only controls reproduce the apparent response. This weakens or refutes the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing explanations; do not advance the state-selective MerTK direction on this evidence.

A result is inconclusive if the rank/overlap gate fails, the mapping scenario changes the sign, uncertainty spans zero or delta, only one donor cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol resolution, or the partial-pooling alternative is non-identifiable. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos and Mneg perturbations across FLS/macrophage donor pairs, with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, estimand computation, uncertainty outputs and whether the conclusion obeys these rules. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, cell viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window or independent biological validity. Those require expert adjudication, orthogonal perturbation such as agonism or genetic loss-of-function, and an independent cohort.

## Completion deliverable and evidence boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty from E-MTAB-8873, plus an explicit identifiability report, exposure-tier comparison, LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, and a fit-or-defer record for the partial-pooling model. Completion requires effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json and a results.json conclusion linked to those outputs. Readiness or a planned method is not a scientific result.

[K1] establishes the broad MerTK-positive resolution/repair and inhibitor-associated FLS-response evidence; this child adds the state-by-perturbation estimand, exposure-tier separation and donor-identifiability gate.
[K2] supplies the strongest macrophage-state rival, in which inflammatory macrophage programs can drive fibroblast pathology without the proposed selective MerTK explanation; this child uses LPS, composition and state controls to separate it where possible.
[K3] bounds interpretation of the FLS harm endpoint by showing inflammatory FLS heterogeneity and niche-linked states; this child therefore requires a multi-marker outcome and does not call a single transcript mechanism.

The exact key-references.json and the three inspected UTF-8 evidence excerpts are reused unchanged from the valid parent, with their frozen receipts and byte hashes. No unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed. The configured evidence does not provide clinical outcomes, donor medication response, MerTK protein/phosphorylation, efferocytosis, viability, dose-response, time-course, spatial localization or an independent validation cohort.

[K2] makes an inflammatory macrophage-state explanation consequential; [K3] cautions that FLS inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked. [K1] supports the starting perturbational observation, but does not identify this state-by-perturbation interaction. The substantive advance is an explicit identifiability and decision-usefulness test under the actual sparse design.

Donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved and the coculture branch includes earlier GSE57723 material; no donor-aware inferential claim or independent validation uses it.

## Estimand and identifiability gate

Normalize the measured feature rows per sample to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserving transcript identifiers and without imputing unmeasured genes. Before modeling, emit a manifest with every included row, exposure tier, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, context, cells, exclusions and mapping scenario.

The primary outcome is a prespecified FLS harm score H: the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen from the eligible untreated coculture reference rows; if a required feature is absent from the exact header, the score is unavailable rather than repaired. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12, MMP13 and each primary component. The context panel is MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1; it is descriptive of the state and cannot prove direct target engagement.

The primary estimand is

  Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)]
          - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]

with donor membership treated as crossed dependence, not as independent observations. Because the prepared design contains only one exact-inhibitor Mneg row and two unambiguous exact-inhibitor Mpos rows, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-FLS/macrophage-pair context comparison. Therefore the interaction is not automatically identifiable as a population-level causal effect. The solver must first report a rank/overlap gate: treatment-context cells, exact matched counterpart availability, donor membership overlap, and whether Delta can be estimated without using the ambiguous row or the preInhibitor tier. A rank-deficient or overlap-failing primary model returns inconclusive, not a zero effect.

The primary baseline is a transparent paired-score/interaction analysis. Construct within-round matched differences wherever the design explicitly supports the same FLS/macrophage membership, then estimate exact-exposure context contrasts with a small fixed-effects model including context, exposure, their interaction and assay round only when estimable. Represent every contributing FLS and macrophage donor with a membership incidence matrix; use a cross-classified random-intercept or penalized fixed-effect formulation only if its rank is documented. Do not include age or sex as if independently varying when age is round-confounded and all rows are female. Report feature-level effects, H effects, donor-cluster bootstrap intervals, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out sensitivity, and exact mapping scenarios. Ordinary donor t-tests, cell-level replication and random row splits are prohibited.

The LPS rows are a bounded generic-inflammatory control: compare preLPS with untreated within context where available and ask whether the marker pattern and context contrast are reproduced. FLS-only rows test whether a response appears without macrophages. Neither control establishes MerTK specificity; both can falsify a selective interpretation. Mixed-composition rows test whether changing Mpos:Mneg mixture alone tracks H and are not used as clean context labels.

## Substantive alternative on the same inputs

The alternative is a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model, not a different question. On the same log-CPM outcome matrix and the same frozen manifest, model the primary and secondary FLS features jointly with feature-specific intercepts, exposure-tier effect, context effect, exposure-by-context effect, assay-round effect, and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads on IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14; a separate macrophage-context factor uses MERTK, MRC1 and TREM2, with SPP1 and IL1B retained as an inflammatory contrast rather than forced into the resolution factor. Feature-specific residual covariance allows correlated markers to contribute uncertainty jointly.

Its fitting target is the posterior or penalized-likelihood distribution of the same Delta, the two context-specific exposure effects, the shared-harm loading coherence and the probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold. It is not trained to predict a label. Fit only after design-rank checks; if the one-Mneg treated cluster or the ambiguous memberships make the latent model non-identifiable, record the attempted model and defer it rather than replacing it with a simpler unannounced fit. Compare the alternative with the baseline by sign, interval width, donor/mapping stability and marker coherence. The information gained is whether a seemingly single-marker interaction is a correlated FLS program and whether partial pooling makes uncertainty widen or shrink appropriately; the score baseline loses that structure but is more transparent under sparsity.

The held-out unit is an assay round or donor-membership cluster for leave-one-cluster-out sensitivity. With only R1, R2 and R5 and unbalanced treatment, this is a stability diagnostic, not external validation. Use posterior predictive or residual checks for the fitted model, not predictive accuracy as the scientific criterion. The estimated future solver cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB memory and minutes for this 33-by-11 feature table; full runtime is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the matrix is small and the scientific uncertainty is design/identifiability, not computational scale.

Deferred alternatives are: a neural expression predictor, because predictive improvement cannot answer whether the interaction is causal or decision-useful; a pooled analysis that merges exact inhibitor and preInhibitor, because protocol equivalence is unavailable; ordinary differential expression t-tests, because donor dependence is explicitly unresolved; E-MTAB-8322 target scoring, because the feature namespace lacks a configured map; and GSE95588 validation, because donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved. These alternatives can be revisited only after the named missing dependency is supplied or the question changes.

## Supportive, adverse and inconclusive rule

Define a material harm threshold delta = 0.5 SD of H, fixed before fitting. A result is supportive only if the exact-exposure Delta is positive and its uncertainty supports Delta > delta (or the equivalent prespecified posterior probability is at least 0.90), the sign is unchanged across admissible donor mappings and round/membership holdouts, the primary marker components are directionally coherent, and neither LPS nor FLS-only controls reproduces the same selective pattern. This supports a balanced orthogonal follow-up to test state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation; it does not justify a clinical treatment or patient-selection claim.

A result is adverse if Delta is nonpositive or Mneg harm is at least as large, or if generic LPS/stress or FLS-only controls reproduce the apparent response. This weakens or refutes the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing explanations; do not advance the state-selective MerTK direction on this evidence.

A result is inconclusive if the rank/overlap gate fails, the mapping scenario changes the sign, uncertainty spans zero or delta, only one donor cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol resolution, or the partial-pooling alternative is non-identifiable. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos and Mneg perturbations across FLS/macrophage donor pairs, with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, estimand computation, uncertainty outputs and whether the conclusion obeys these rules. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, cell viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window or independent biological validity. Those require expert adjudication, orthogonal perturbation such as agonism or genetic loss-of-function, and an independent cohort.

## Completion deliverable and evidence boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty from E-MTAB-8873, plus an explicit identifiability report, exposure-tier comparison, LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, and a fit-or-defer record for the partial-pooling model. Completion requires effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json and a results.json conclusion linked to those outputs. Readiness or a planned method is not a scientific result.

[K1] establishes the broad MerTK-positive resolution/repair and inhibitor-associated FLS-response evidence; this child adds the state-by-perturbation estimand, exposure-tier separation and donor-identifiability gate.
[K2] supplies the strongest macrophage-state rival, in which inflammatory macrophage programs can drive fibroblast pathology without the proposed selective MerTK explanation; this child uses LPS, composition and state controls to separate it where possible.
[K3] bounds interpretation of the FLS harm endpoint by showing inflammatory FLS heterogeneity and niche-linked states; this child therefore requires a multi-marker outcome and does not call a single transcript mechanism.

The exact key-references.json and the three inspected UTF-8 evidence excerpts are reused unchanged from the valid parent, with their frozen receipts and byte hashes. No unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed. The configured evidence does not provide clinical outcomes, donor medication response, MerTK protein/phosphorylation, efferocytosis, viability, dose-response, time-course, spatial localization or an independent validation cohort.

# Independent transferability of context-selective MerTK perturbation

Status: substantive evolution of candidate-e2c88fac21f4420df13909b9; planned Harbor experiment only. No scientific screening result has been executed.

## Question, hypothesis and clinical importance

The inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce fibroblast repair [K1]. A different inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. None establishes the parent’s unresolved claim: that MerTK inhibition causes a larger FLS inflammatory harm response in a MerTK/CD206-positive context than in a MerTK/CD206-negative context, and that this interaction transfers to an independently verified perturbation assay.

The falsifiable hypothesis is therefore:

> In the primary E-MTAB-8873 RA type-B synovial FLS coculture, exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure has a larger FLS harm effect in the unambiguous Mpos context than in Mneg; an independent E-MTAB-8316 paired perturbation will show directionally coherent, target-relevant response only if its compound label, feature identity and paired biological unit are independently verified.

The clinically consequential decision is whether to prioritize state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation experiments. A supportive result justifies balanced orthogonal perturbation and functional testing; it does not establish a treatment, patient-selection rule, direct target engagement or clinical benefit. The substantive advance over the parent is a transportability gate: it distinguishes a valid primary FLS interaction from a source-specific monocyte perturbation response and prevents a false “external validation” created by matching donor-like strings.

## Verified data bindings and population

The full source catalog is `[private-path]/catalog.json`, catalog SHA-256 `162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f`; the therapeutic-targets snapshot is `core-molecular-20261003`. The catalog and `datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json` define the source lineage. The prepared tables are analysis tables, not extra observations.

Primary E-MTAB-8873:

It is feature rows by 33 sample-ID columns and 445 measured transcript rows. Required transcript columns are `MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end`, `MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end`, `TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end`, `SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end`, `IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end`, `IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end`, `MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end`, `MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end`, `MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end`, `MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end`, and `MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end`. The header field is `feature`; sample IDs are the remaining headers.
- Design table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json`, SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`. Required fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata), and `cells). Join only `design.sample_id = counts header sample ID). `donor_id` may contain multiple contributors and is not a single independent donor.
- Registry: `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, verified local SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. Its E-MTAB-8873 entry records 33 samples, 445 features, no verified single donors, targeted-assay limits, and a prohibition on ordinary donor t-tests.
- Source lineage members include `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719`) and the registered RSEC members used by the primary rows: `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `ef435ca4a16bb535f74ad077297861f2f9672827c2d2a4e7f9e65171bea2b0d7`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`1dafc0a646fc9cdc1101803cf9d36802a1775844a85877930341ebe6edcf2176`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`144b62d01db3f4635bdd19ecc599ce7670770ddf79b7e72e846c46a3cf732e9e`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`e3d6554a4e6c262fca98ce8263fb3c1d86d2c47c5f7e3e1fe5aa516367b3f599`), and the R2/R5 `Mpos_preInhibitor` members (`e14006cefdb3b642c3f280d3e888b3e16767e2b36288bb7029ce2e52d36c6a85` and `09bb1e81c247f251930c10ea8bfc25e651c01a8746a2fbe630d27dce4cb064a8`). The exact exposure rows are R1 `SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor`, R1 `SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor), and R1 `SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor). R2 and R5 `Mpos_preInhibitor` are a separate secondary tier; protocol equivalence must be established before any sensitivity use. - Design table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json`, SHA-256 `ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81`. Required fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `donor_status`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `tissue), `cell_type`, `age), and `sex), plus `unit_definition`. The six exact same-unit pairs are MK11/MK12, MK15/MK16, MK19/MK20, MK23/MK24, MK3/MK4, and MK7/MK8: within each pair `condition/treatment=none` versus `UNC106238`. They are nested in four verified FLS donor clusters `SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049`; `other_donor_id` identifies six nested monocyte donors `1533,1534,1601,1602,1462,1463`. - Source lineage members are `[private-path]/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228`) and `E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74`). The registry records four verified single donor IDs, six nested monocyte donors, 12 samples, and no 12-independent-donor claim.

No identifier is joined across assays. In particular, SA114/SA049/SA104/SA051 in 8316 are not matched to SA256A, SA259A, SA266A or any other 8873 label. A source comparison may use only separately estimated, explicitly standardized effect summaries after compatibility checks; it may not pool rows, donors, feature IDs or raw counts.

## Estimands and identifiability gates

Normalize each source separately to log2(CPM + 1), preserving original feature IDs and never imputing absent genes.

Primary E-MTAB-8873 outcome:
`H_s` is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen using eligible untreated, unambiguous co-culture reference rows. The primary estimand is

`Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]`.

The solver must emit a pre-fit gate with treatment/context cell counts, exact counterpart availability, donor-membership incidence rank, and estimability of the interaction. The gate fails if the model requires the ambiguous mixed rows, the preInhibitor tier, the metadata-conflicted untreated row, a random row split, or independent-donor assumptions. Given the verified design, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-membership exact-inhibitor Mpos/Mneg contrast; therefore a population-level causal interaction is not automatically identified. A failed or rank-deficient gate returns inconclusive, never a zero estimate.

The baseline is a transparent paired score/interaction analysis: calculate within-membership matched differences wherever explicitly supported, fit context, exposure and interaction with assay round only when rank permits, and represent FLS/macrophage memberships by an incidence matrix. Use cluster bootstrap or a bounded sign/permutation sensitivity over contributing membership clusters, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out analyses. Report H, each component, exact versus preInhibitor tiers, mapping scenarios, and controls. Ordinary donor t-tests and cell-level replication are prohibited.

The E-MTAB-8316 secondary estimand is source-specific:
`d_{f,m,g}=logCPM(UNC106238)_{f,m,g}-logCPM(none)_{f,m,g}`, for each of the six exact pairs, summarized within the four FLS donor clusters with monocyte donor nested dependence. It is not H, not Delta, and not an FLS outcome. A six-pair response can be reported only as exploratory paired evidence; it is not six independent donors.

The 8316 compatibility gate requires: (1) protocol/registry confirmation that UNC106238 is the intended perturbation and that the none/UNC106238 rows are paired units; (2) a named frozen Ensembl-to-gene annotation map if gene-level MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 or inflammatory-marker claims are attempted; (3) verified correspondence of cell type and readout to the intended secondary question; and (4) no cross-source donor join. The currently inspected prepared files pass the pairing and donor-nesting checks but fail the configured feature-map requirement for gene-level target claims and do not expose an Mpos/Mneg context. The correct current plan is therefore bounded source-specific triangulation with an explicit non-pooling status, not a hierarchical cross-cohort Delta.

A shared hierarchical cross-cohort effect is scientifically identifiable only if both sources share a measured endpoint, intervention definition, context contrast, feature namespace/annotation and biological unit. They currently do not: 8873 measures targeted FLS coculture harm with transcript labels, while 8316 measures Ensembl-indexed monocyte samples under none/UNC106238 and has no context field. A model with source-specific intercepts cannot repair a missing common estimand. If a future named annotation and protocol adjudication make a common secondary signature defensible, fit source-specific effects with a hierarchical shrinkage sensitivity, never a forced pooled primary coefficient. Otherwise report non-pooling.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both methods use the same source-specific normalized matrices, design fields, paired units and frozen manifests.

The baseline estimates the primary Delta transparently and the 8316 paired d contrasts without a learned prediction target. Its strength is auditable behavior under sparsity; it loses correlated marker structure and can be noisy when one membership drives a contrast.

The alternative is a source-stratified cross-classified multivariate model. For 8873, jointly model IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 with feature-specific exposure, context and interaction effects, crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects, and a shared harm factor; retain IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 and MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 as contrasts. For 8316, fit a multivariate paired response only after the feature-map and protocol gates pass, with FLS-cluster and nested monocyte effects. The target is the same Delta (8873) and source-specific d-vector (8316), not a disease label. Compare signs, uncertainty, marker coherence and leave-cluster-out stability, not predictive accuracy. The alternative can reveal whether a response is a correlated program and whether partial pooling appropriately widens or shrinks uncertainty; the baseline loses that structure.

Do not fit the alternative if the 8873 rank gate fails or the 8316 feature map/units remain unresolved. This is a scientific deferral, not a mechanical simplification. Expected solver resources are 4–8 CPU cores, <16 GiB memory and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary feature table plus 12-by-feature paired secondary table; the estimate is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is identifiability and biological-unit compatibility, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected: a predictive gain cannot distinguish context selectivity from donor/assay confounding and has no clinically meaningful target estimand here.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze material harm at 0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive requires a positive exact-exposure Delta above that threshold with uncertainty supporting Delta > 0.5 SD, stable admissible donor/mapping/round sensitivities, coherent primary components, no matching selective pattern in LPS or FLS-only controls, and a gated 8316 secondary response that is directionally compatible without asserting a shared effect. It supports balanced agonism/genetic-loss-of-function, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis and fibroblast invasion or matrix-degradation follow-up.

Adverse means Delta is nonpositive, Mneg harm is at least as large, generic controls reproduce the apparent selectivity, or a validly gated 8316 perturbation response is discordant. This weakens the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition, timing or assay-specific explanations.

Inconclusive means the primary rank/overlap gate fails, an admissible mapping changes sign, uncertainty spans zero or the material threshold, one membership cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol equivalence, or 8316 annotation/protocol compatibility remains blocked. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos/Mneg FLS–macrophage donor pairs with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS functional readouts.

Harbor can verify source-local joins, feature presence, paired contrasts, rank calculations, uncertainty outputs, compatibility status and rule-consistent conclusions. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window, or independent biological validity; those require expert adjudication, orthogonal perturbation and another study.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted 8873 `Delta`, context-specific effects and component effects with uncertainty; a primary identifiability report; LPS/FLS-only/composition controls; donor/mapping/tier sensitivity; a source-local 8316 paired-response and compatibility report (or an explicit blocked status); and a fit-or-defer record for the multivariate alternative. Readiness and the planned design are not a scientific result.

Unavailable evidence remains explicit: no clinical outcomes, dose-response, exposure-time field, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation, or independent balanced FLS validation cohort is configured. The 8316 source cannot fill those gaps and is not an external validation of 8873.

## Key references

[K1] establishes the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage and fibroblast-repair prior; it does not establish the interaction tested here.
[K2] supplies the strongest inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; it does not establish MerTK specificity.
[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; it does not validate this panel or assay transfer.

Attached branch files preserve exactly these three inspected works and bounded source excerpts: `key-references.json`, `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt`, and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`.
