# Independent, source-specific triangulation of context-selective MerTK harm

Status: substantive successor of candidate-e2c88fac21f4420df13909b9. Planned Harbor experiment only; no screening or scientific result has been executed.

## Opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports a broad starting claim: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair and MerTK perturbation has been associated with increased FLS inflammatory transcripts [K1]. It does not establish that inhibitor harm is larger in MerTK/CD206-positive than MerTK/CD206-negative context, or that the observation transfers to an independently designed paired perturbation assay.

Primary hypothesis: in E-MTAB-8873 type-B synovial-cell cocultures, exact macrophage MerTK-inhibitor exposure produces a larger FLS harm response in MerTK/CD206pos than MerTK/CD206neg coculture after accounting for contributing FLS and macrophage memberships. Secondary triangulation hypothesis: within E-MTAB-8316, paired UNC106238 response in synovial monocyte preparations is directionally compatible with the primary perturbation response when summarized with a frozen verified gene map and nested donor-aware units. The secondary is not a claim that E-MTAB-8316 contains Mpos/Mneg contexts or FLS coculture harm.

The strongest rivals are generic inflammatory/stress signaling or composition, and timing/protocol mismatch. They predict similar perturbation direction in LPS controls, FLS-only samples, or all macrophage contexts; and they predict that any E-MTAB-8316 disagreement could reflect its different compound, monocyte label and absent time field. [K2] makes the macrophage-state rival consequential; [K3] shows why heterogeneous, niche-linked FLS programs must not be reduced to one transcript. The advance over [K1] is a prespecified identifiability gate plus a directional source-specific transfer check, not pooled external validation.

## Data bindings and population

All source files are read-only. Prepared matrices and designs are analysis tables; archive members are provenance, not extra observations.

Primary E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f. Verified header has 33 sample columns and 445 feature rows. Measured rows include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- Design: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. Fields are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Join only design.sample_id to counts header. Comma-separated donor memberships are dependence annotations, not independent donors.
- Registry: [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab1bd1a31c77b7f70f. It records 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors and disables ordinary donor t-tests.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt and registered R1, R2 and R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz members listed in configured metadata.

Eligible rows have tissue=synovial membrane, cell_type=type B synovial cell and documented coculture. Context is the design label co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages versus co-cultured with MerTK/CD206neg macrophages. Exact primary treatment is macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor. Exact treated rows are R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor. The last has no unambiguous untreated counterpart. R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor remain a separate tier and are not silently pooled. R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos has conflicting donor metadata and is sensitivity-only. Mixed-composition, not-cocultured and six FLS-only rows are controls or descriptive strata. Secondary E-MTAB-8316 is source-specific and is never joined to E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645. It has 12 sample columns and 58,302 Ensembl-indexed feature rows; header IDs are MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7 and MK8.

Labels are verified none versus UNC106238; no time field and no Mpos/Mneg label. Unit definition is FLS donor cluster; monocyte donors nested and balanced across compound conditions.
- Registry: same assay-registry path; it records 12 samples, 58,302 features, independent donors not assumed, verified single donors SA049, SA051, SA104 and SA114, four FLS donor clusters and six nested monocyte donors.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8316/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz and E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt, source hashes 510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228 and 3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74.

The six verified within-source pairs are MK11/MK12 (SA114, other_donor_id 1533), MK15/MK16 (SA114, 1534), MK19/MK20 (SA051, 1601), MK23/MK24 (SA104, 1602), MK3/MK4 (SA049, 1462), and MK7/MK8 (SA049, 1463), first none and second UNC106238. No identifier, donor, specimen or row may be joined across assays. E-MTAB-8316 cells are monocyte; FLS donor cluster is a nesting unit, not evidence that its readout is FLS harm.

The feature-header inspection found no rows named MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, MMP12, MMP13, MMP14, TNF or CXCL8 in E-MTAB-8316. It is Ensembl-only. A target-module claim is gated on a named frozen Ensembl-to-transcript map and protocol reconciliation. If absent, secondary status is mapping_blocked, not zero.

## Estimands, baseline and identifiability

Normalize each prepared matrix independently to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserve identifiers and do not impute absent genes. Emit a manifest with source, sample ID, treatment tier, context, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, nested donor unit, mapping status and exclusions.

Primary harm score H is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14, standardized using eligible untreated coculture references only. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12 and MMP13 plus each component. MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1 are a descriptive context panel, not proof of target engagement.

Primary estimand:
Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)].

First report the rank/overlap gate: exposure-by-context cells, matched counterpart availability, FLS/macrophage membership incidence overlap, and whether Delta is estimable without the ambiguous untreated row or preInhibitor tier. Only the R1 SA256A/SA259A Mneg and Mpos pairs provide complete same-membership exact comparisons; one Mneg treated cluster and conflicting Mpos metadata mean a population-level interaction may be non-identifiable. Failure returns inconclusive, not zero.

Transparent baseline: construct within matched same-membership H differences, then fit a small fixed-effects model with context, exact exposure and interaction, adding assay round only when rank permits. Represent every FLS and macrophage donor as a membership incidence matrix. Use crossed random effects or penalized membership effects only after documenting rank. Report effects, intervals, component effects, donor-membership bootstrap, leave-one-round-out, leave-one-membership-out and admissible mapping sensitivities. Donor t-tests, cell counts as replication, random row splits, confounded age/sex adjustment and pooling exact/preInhibitor are prohibited.

Secondary estimand is not pooled with Delta. Conditional on the annotation gate, compute within-source log-expression differences for the six none/UNC106238 pairs, average repeated context measurements within each verified donor/condition as the registry directs, retain four FLS-cluster and six nested-monocyte strata, and fit a paired donor-aware response summary with no twelve-independent-donor claim. Compare direction and module coherence only. Without the map, output secondary_mapping_blocked.json with the missing dependency and stop that branch.

## Same-input alternative and compute

The substantive alternative uses the same E-MTAB-8873 matrix, manifest, rows and outcomes: a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model with feature-specific intercepts, exposure, context, exposure-by-context, round and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14; MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 form a descriptive context factor; SPP1 and IL1B remain an inflammatory contrast. Its target is the distribution of the same Delta, context effects, loading coherence and probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold, not predictive accuracy. Compare sign, uncertainty width, marker coherence and membership/mapping stability. The baseline loses correlated-program information; the alternative can reveal a coherent multi-marker program or appropriately widen uncertainty.

Fit only after the primary rank gate; otherwise record alternative_deferred. A conditional E-MTAB-8316 alternative, only after an Ensembl map, is a low-dimensional paired latent perturbation score within source, not a pooled meta-analysis. Held-out unit is assay round or donor-membership cluster for stability diagnostics, not external validation. Planned future cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB RAM and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary target table plus a 12-sample secondary check; this is an estimate, not a measured runtime. GPU is deferred because design identifiability, not scale, limits the study. Neural prediction, ordinary t-tests, pooling the two compounds, E-MTAB-8322 scoring without its missing map and GSE95588 validation with unresolved mapping are deferred.

## Falsification and interpretation

Fix material threshold delta=0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive primary evidence requires positive Delta with uncertainty supporting Delta > delta (or posterior probability at least 0.90), coherent components, stable sign across mapping and membership/round holdouts, and no selective mimicry in LPS or FLS-only controls. A gated E-MTAB-8316 result is directionally concordant only if its mapped target/module response has the prespecified compatible sign across donor strata; it cannot rescue a failed primary rank gate.

Adverse evidence is nonpositive Delta, Mneg harm at least as large, generic LPS/FLS-only mimicry, or clearly discordant gated secondary direction. This weakens context-selective prioritization and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing.

Inconclusive evidence includes rank/overlap failure, missing Ensembl map, unreconciled secondary protocol/labels, uncertainty spanning zero or delta, sign changes across mappings, one cluster driving the effect, exact/preInhibitor disagreement or a non-identifiable alternative. Next test: balanced matched Mpos/Mneg perturbation across multiple FLS/macrophage donor pairs with dose, time, viability, MerTK protein/phosphorylation, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, paired units, estimand arithmetic, rank reports, mapping gates, uncertainty and conclusion compliance. It cannot establish direct mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window, patient selection, clinical benefit or independent biological validity. Those require expert review, orthogonal agonism/genetic loss-of-function, protein/functional assays and an independent cohort. Clinical outcomes, medication response, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, viability, dose-response and longitudinal time course are unavailable.

## Completion deliverable and references

The deliverable is newly fitted primary Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty, rank/overlap report, exposure-tier and LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, fitted-or-deferred alternative, and separate E-MTAB-8316 status concordant, discordant or mapping_blocked. Required outputs are effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json, results.json and, when needed, secondary_mapping_blocked.json. Readiness and a planned analysis are not a result.

[K1] supports MerTK-positive resolution/repair and inhibitor-associated FLS-response evidence; this proposal adds the state-by-perturbation estimand and transferability gate. [K2] supplies the inflammatory macrophage/HBEGF rival; this proposal uses generic controls and refuses to call a generic response MerTK-selective. [K3] bounds the FLS endpoint by showing heterogeneity and niche-linked states; this proposal requires a multi-marker score and does not infer mechanism from one gene.

The exact parent key-reference receipts and three inherited work excerpts are preserved in the support package. Local files are concise UTF-8 evidence notes; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed.

# MerTK-conditioned macrophage–fibroblast communication in rheumatoid arthritis

Episode 1; evolved as a targeted repair of expert seed D3-M2. This is a planned Harbor experiment, not an executed biological result.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

Rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) synovium contains macrophage and fibroblast states associated with either destructive inflammation or remission. The strongest inspected evidence supports three separate observations: HBEGF+ macrophages can induce an EGFR-linked inflammatory/invasive fibroblast response in human RA tissue [K1]; MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response [K2]; and MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states are co-enriched in clinically distinct RA synovial tissue contexts [K3]. None of those observations establishes that a MerTK-conditioned macrophage state is the directional driver of a fibroblast transcriptional response, and co-enrichment can reflect shared tissue context or composition.

Hypothesis: among human RA FLS samples cocultured with MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages, macrophage pre-treatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor will reduce a prespecified coherent inflammatory-FLS program relative to the matched untreated coculture. The reduction should be larger and more coherent than the available MerTK/CD206-negative control, should not be reproduced simply by LPS pre-treatment, and should remain after modeling the contributing FLS/macrophage donors. This is a directional perturbation hypothesis about an in-vitro molecular state, not a claim that MerTK blockade will improve RA clinically.

The key unresolved comparison is:

- MerTK-conditioned communication: Mpos macrophage pre-treatment changes the FLS program in a reproducible direction, with coherent reversal of an inflammatory score.
- Strong rival: generic macrophage activation, donor mixture, FLS composition, batch/cell-number effects, or inhibitor off-target pharmacology explains the same pattern. Those rivals predict no Mpos-specific, donor-consistent reversal or a comparable effect in Mneg/LPS controls.

What would change practice or research is not a small predictive gain. A positive result would justify target-engagement and functional coculture studies aimed at preserving or restoring a pro-resolving macrophage–stromal circuit in difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA. An adverse result would prevent MerTK state association from being promoted to a MerTK-directed fibroblast mechanism.

## Closest inspected work and substantive advance

[K1] established a human RA macrophage–fibroblast communication axis and an EGFR-dependent fibroblast consequence, but it did not test the configured MerTK-pretreated macrophage mixtures. The present experiment adds a matched perturbation boundary and explicitly acknowledges that HBEGF and EGFR are absent from the targeted E-MTAB-8873 panel.

[K2] associated MerTK-positive macrophage subsets with remission and fibroblast repair. The present experiment asks whether a recorded perturbation of the macrophage input changes a prespecified inflammatory FLS output, rather than treating a remission association as a directional mechanism.

[K3] defined clinically meaningful co-enriched MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states and candidate communication structure. The present experiment is a small, donor-aware perturbational test designed to distinguish communication from shared tissue context, selection and composition. It does not reproduce K3’s clinical cohort or spatial evidence.

The advance is therefore boundary testing: state association and inferred communication become a falsifiable, bounded perturbation hypothesis, with explicit failure criteria and a direct next experiment.

## Population, temporal boundary, and exact data binding

Primary population: the FLS sample columns in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 targeted matrix. The matrix is a gzipped TSV whose first column is feature and whose remaining 33 columns are the sample_id values in E-MTAB-8873.design.json. It has 445 measured feature rows (446 lines including the header). The design identifies human type-B synovial cells from RA synovial membrane, with condition, treatment, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, and cells.

Primary matched Mpos inhibitor comparison uses only these design-matrix pairs, because both untreated and pre-inhibitor samples are present for the same recorded contributing-donor mixture:

- R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos vs R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor; donor string SA256A, SA259A; untreated versus macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor.
- R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos vs R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA257A, SA266A.
- R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos vs R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA266A, SA277A.

The R1 SA256A/SA260R Mpos samples have a conflicting donor representation in the prepared design (SA256A versus SA256A | SA256A, SA260R) and are excluded from the primary matched estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves the contributing donor. The three mixed Mpos/Mneg samples (R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg, and the R5 analogue) are secondary composition controls, not pure Mpos observations. All E-MTAB-8873 records have donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model; the FLS cells are not independent donors. No claim will call the 33 columns 33 independent biological replicates.

The matrix’s primary prespecified FLS outcome panel is restricted to measured, uniquely identified targeted rows:

- MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end
- MMP9|NM_004994.2|Reference_end
- IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end
- IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end
- CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end

MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end, ADAM17|NM_003183.5|Reference_end, and the two COL1A1 transcript rows are retained as exploratory context/QC only. The targeted panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; their absence is a measurement limitation, not a negative finding.

Exact primary source and prepared paths:

- GSE95588: raw [private-path]/GSE95588; prepared coculture table [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5, with design GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json and unresolved donor IDs; prepared d1–d4 table [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0, with design GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json. Its duplicate/date-like gene labels require the registered feature-map JSONs before naming targets, and its donor-column mapping is unresolved; coculture r1/r2 includes earlier GSE57723 lineage and is not independent validation. These files are an exploratory context branch only, not part of the primary inferential package.

## Sampling, preprocessing, analysis, and uncertainty

The solver must first emit a binding audit: each matrix header must join one-to-one to a design sample_id; each primary pair must have exactly one untreated and one pre-inhibitor Mpos sample; all excluded/conflicting and mixed-ratio records must be listed. Source files are read-only and derived matrices/results go to the workspace.

For E-MTAB-8873, apply the documented targeted-matrix convention, preserve the full transcript identifiers, remove no features merely because they are unmeasured, and filter only samples failing the explicit header/design or numeric-value audit. Normalize within matrix using a predeclared library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for score modeling, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. Do not merge duplicate identifiers. Report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count, library size, and all filtering decisions.

Primary outcome is the sample-level inflammatory FLS score: the standardized mean of the eight prespecified row values after normalization, with each gene’s direction fixed before fitting. The primary pairwise effect is delta_k = score(Mpos + MerTK-inhibitor)_k - score(Mpos untreated)_k for the three usable matched mixtures. A supportive direction is negative attenuation in all or nearly all pairs, with a coherent panel-level estimate and uncertainty. Secondary contrasts compare untreated Mpos with untreated Mneg where the FLS donor contribution is recorded; the one available R1 Mneg inhibitor/no-inhibitor pair is a negative-control check, not a stable estimate. LPS-treated Mpos/Mneg records are a generic activation control and are never relabeled as MerTK perturbations.

Fit the simple baseline as a prespecified per-feature donor-aware model (negative-binomial count model or limma-voom equivalent, with size factor, experiment/run and FLS/macrophage contributing-donor terms when identifiable) plus the eight-gene score model. Do not use an ordinary donor t-test on the 33 E-MTAB-8873 columns. With only three usable matched mixtures, report paired estimates, donor/mixture bootstrap or Bayesian posterior intervals, and effect directions; do not manufacture asymptotic p-values or call the result independently replicated.

Fit the substantive alternative on the same inputs: a small hierarchical multivariate latent-factor model in which the eight-gene inflammatory score is a prespecified loading block and the remaining measured 445-feature matrix can contribute only through regularized factors, with random effects for FLS donor, macrophage donor/contributing mixture, and run. The target is coherent FLS-state reversal under inhibitor, not prediction of a clinical label. Fit the alternative only on the training donor clusters and report a leave-one-cluster-out stress test across R1/R2/R5; with three clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare the baseline and alternative on signed paired effect, uncertainty coverage by donor/mixture resampling, coherence of gene-level reversal, and sensitivity to the conflicting donor record. The latent model is scientifically useful because the baseline can hide a distributed, partially correlated state behind noisy per-gene tests; it can also reveal that apparent reversal is driven by one technical module or donor. It is deferred if the sample-level design cannot support partial pooling without unstable factors.

E-MTAB-8316 is analyzed separately as a donor-paired compound-response context: average repeated other_donor_id contexts within each of the four verified donor_id clusters before any exploratory comparison, as required by the dataset guide. Use it to ask whether the compound produces a coherent monocyte transcriptional shift consistent with the proposed macrophage-state perturbation, not to confirm FLS direction or target specificity. E-MTAB-8322 and GSE95588 may be used only for source-specific descriptive context after their own feature/lineage limitations are honored.

No GPU is needed for the planned discovery or solver: the matrices are small enough for CPU linear/multivariate models, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GB RAM allocation should be sufficient; this estimate is reasoned from the 33×445 targeted matrix and is not a measured fit benchmark. The configured planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; it is a future solver envelope, not an instruction to use GPUs. A bounded CPU fit should be under minutes, but convergence and model-library availability remain unverified. No full scientific screen was executed in this episode; only schema/header/design and source-literature inspection were performed.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive result: the three usable Mpos matched pairs show a negative inhibitor effect on the inflammatory score, the direction is coherent across the prespecified genes, the effect is not as large in the available Mneg control, donor-aware sensitivity does not erase it, and the multivariate alternative agrees without being driven by an unmeasured feature. This supports a MerTK-conditioned FLS communication hypothesis and justifies independent factorial coculture with target engagement and functional outcomes. It does not prove direct ligand–receptor binding, MerTK target specificity, clinical efficacy, remission causality, or a mechanism involving HBEGF/EGFR.

Adverse result: the score is unchanged or increases under Mpos inhibitor, the sign is inconsistent across matched mixtures, a comparable effect occurs in Mneg or LPS controls, the effect vanishes after donor/run adjustment, or the latent alternative localizes it to a technical/composition factor. This falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific directional interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, or assay validity. It does not prove that MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive result: the three matched mixtures cannot be reconciled, the donor contribution is not identifiable, counts are too sparse, the panel is not measured reliably, or UNC106238/“MerTK inhibitor” identity and exposure cannot be verified. The correct action is to obtain protocol/target-engagement information and run a new balanced factorial coculture, not to interpret a null as biological refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are the header/design joins, measured-feature availability, normalization/model execution, paired estimates, uncertainty, sensitivity results, and whether the conclusion matches the prespecified outcome. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for direct target engagement, secreted cytokines, fibroblast invasion/matrix damage, tissue localization, treatment response, flare risk, and patient benefit. The verifier must reject both incorrect computation and unsupported claims that a QA result proves mechanism or clinical efficacy.

## Method alternatives and selection record

The simple donor-aware score/feature model was selected as the primary baseline because it is transparent, aligned to the limited matched design, and gives an interpretable falsification test. The hierarchical multivariate factor alternative is retained because it can reveal distributed state coherence and donor heterogeneity that separate gene tests lose; it is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos pairs and the targeted panel do not support an unconstrained latent model. A mechanistic ligand–receptor mediation model is deferred: the primary targeted matrix is FLS-focused and lacks HBEGF/EGFR, direct ligand abundance, protein secretion, target engagement and a balanced factorial design. Evidence that would justify revisiting it is a verified ligand-containing assay, independent FLS/macrophage donors, vehicle/washout details, direct MerTK engagement, and a functional FLS endpoint.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, donor-aware estimates of the Mpos inhibitor effect on the prespecified FLS score and feature panel, plus a fitted/assessed multivariate alternative and the binding/QC audit. Completion requires those outputs, uncertainty and the supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification; a readiness package alone is not a biological result.

## Demonstration and seed dispositions

The three clinical demonstrations were treated as ambition references, not topic requirements. Delphi’s learned dated-disease-history method is not pursued because these are molecular endpoint assays without longitudinal EHR histories; its lesson is to compare a substantive learned alternative against a simple baseline, which is applied here with a multivariate FLS-state model. Oncoformer is not pursued because the configured domain has no routine EHR or chest-X-ray modality; its lab-only adaptation would answer a different predictive question, not this mechanism question. ALADYNOULLI is not reproduced because genetic inputs and longitudinal patient trajectories are unavailable; a latent-factor adaptation is retained only as a compact descriptive alternative for the current perturbation question.

D3-M1 is deferred: E-MTAB-8322 is macrophage-only and E-MTAB-8873 is targeted FLS/coculture, so whole-tissue composition versus within-cell regulation cannot be identified without tissue composition or matched whole-tissue data. D3-M3 is deferred as a longitudinal persistence claim: E-MTAB-8322 has cross-sectional treatment-naive, resistant and remission groups and no transition times; it can later support a bounded state comparison, not persistence/remission transition inference. D3-M2 is developed because its MerTK-labeled pre-treatment contrasts provide the clearest bounded perturbation test, while the unresolved target-specific and functional evidence is explicitly retained.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Sci Transl Med. 2019. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nat Med. 2020. DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k2-remission-excerpt.txt.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature. 2023. DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt.

# MerTK specificity repair: a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS interaction test

Episode 4 child of candidate-5282fd53c9408f02e8752f4b. This is a planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit or wet-lab experiment was executed here.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important question is unchanged: can a MerTK-associated macrophage state condition rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior in a way that could motivate resolution-restoring therapy for difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA? The strongest inspected evidence is not yet target-specific. [K1] reports an HBEGF+ macrophage–FLS axis with EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness, but it is a different macrophage program. [K2] reports MerTKpos synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an in-vitro FLS repair response. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states are structured within clinically distinct synovial contexts. These observations support a plausible macrophage–FLS mechanism and its clinical importance; they do not establish that a compound-labeled MerTK perturbation changes FLS communication through MerTK.

Hypothesis: in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 endpoint matrix, the recorded inhibitor effect on a prespecified inflammatory FLS program is larger for MerTK/CD206-positive (Mpos) macrophage cocultures than for the matched MerTK/CD206-negative (Mneg) coculture. Formally, for a matched donor/run block k, let delta_g(k) = normalized FLS outcome under macrophage pretreatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor minus the untreated outcome. The specificity observable is the interaction I_g = delta_g(Mpos) - delta_g(Mneg), with the same construction for the eight-gene inflammatory score. A MerTK-conditioned interpretation predicts negative I and coherent negative Mpos deltas; generic activation, compound-wide off-target effects, donor mixture, cell-composition differences or assay artifacts predict a comparable Mneg response, a response that tracks LPS rather than Mpos status, or loss of the effect after donor/QC adjustment.

This is a falsifiable molecular-state hypothesis, not a claim that MerTK blockade improves RA, that MerTK is a direct ligand–receptor mediator, or that the recorded compound is selective. The repair matters clinically because falsely treating an association or off-target drug response as MerTK causality could misdirect a resolution-restoring program, whereas a reproducible state-specific interaction would justify a target-engagement and functional coculture study.

## What is already supported versus unresolved

Supported by the inspected evidence:

- RA synovial macrophage programs can affect fibroblast behavior, including destructive invasiveness [K1].
- MerTK-positive macrophage subsets are associated with remission biology and can induce a fibroblast repair response in a separate in-vitro context [K2].
- Macrophage and fibroblast states can be co-structured by clinically meaningful synovial tissue context [K3].

Unresolved and tested here:

- Whether the E-MTAB-8873 inhibitor contrast is Mpos-specific rather than a generic compound effect.
- Whether the FLS response survives a matched Mneg comparison and donor/contributing-mixture sensitivity.
- Whether the inhibitor response is compatible with generic macrophage activation, as indexed by available LPS-pretreated samples.

Still not established by this experiment:

- MerTK target engagement, compound selectivity, direct binding, ligand identity, intracellular signaling, secreted mediator changes, FLS invasion or matrix damage, tissue localization, flare prediction, treatment response or clinical benefit.
- A temporal transition or persistence mechanism. The design JSONs have no numeric sampling-time field or culture-duration/washout table; the temporal boundary is the recorded terminal endpoint for each sample only.

## Exact data binding and population

Primary source:

- Matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`. It contains the `feature` column and 33 sample columns, with 445 measured feature rows.
- Design: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json`, SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`. It has 33 records and the required keys `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `condition`, `treatment`, `cells`, `donor_status`, `source_metadata`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, and `cell_type`.
- Join key: matrix header sample ID must match design `sample_id) exactly one-to-one. The source audit found `donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model` for all 33 records; these are recorded pseudobulk/coculture samples, not 33 independent donors.
- Raw repository and MAGE-TAB: `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8873/repository.json` and `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt`; SDRF SHA-256 `4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719`. Raw selected archive members include `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, the corresponding R2 and R5 Mpos pairs, all recorded preLPS members, and `E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt). The prepared matrix/design are the bound analysis inputs.

Primary Mpos inhibitor pairs, retained only where the same recorded contributing-donor mixture has one untreated and one pre-inhibitor sample:

- R1: `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos` versus `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor`; donor string `SA256A, SA259A).
- R2: `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos` versus `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor`; donor string `SA257A, SA266A).
- R5: `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos` versus `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor`; donor string `SA266A, SA277A`.

The R1 `SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos` record has a conflicting donor representation (`SA256A` versus `SA256A | SA256A, SA260R`) and is excluded from the primary estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves it. The R1 Mneg negative-control pair is `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg` versus `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor`; it is one specificity block, not a replicated Mneg estimate. There are no matched Mneg inhibitor pairs in R2 or R5.

The three mixed-composition controls are `R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg`, `R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg`, and `R5_SA263R_FLS_SA278R_1Mpos_SA277A_3Mneg`. They are secondary composition stress tests, not pure Mpos or Mneg observations. LPS controls include the recorded `*_Mpos_preLPS` and `*_Mneg_preLPS` samples in R1, R2 and R5. LPS is a generic-activation control, not a MerTK perturbation or a substitute for an inactive analog.

The prespecified primary FLS outcome is the standardized mean of these exactly measured targeted rows after normalization, with the direction fixed before fitting:

- `MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end`
- `MMP9|NM_004994.2|Reference_end`
- `IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end`
- `IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end`
- `CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end`
- `CCL2|NM_002982.3|Reference_end`
- `ICAM1|NM_000201.2|Reference_end`
- `TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|Reference_end`

`MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end`, `CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1`, `MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end`, `APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end`, `ADAM17|NM_003183.5|Reference_end`, and both `COL1A1` rows are exploratory context/QC only. The panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; absence from the panel is not a negative result.

Orthogonal source-separated context:

- E-MTAB-8316 matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645`; design `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json`, SHA-256 `ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81`. The matrix sample columns are `MK11,MK12,MK15,MK16,MK19,MK20,MK23,MK24,MK3,MK4,MK7,MK8`; its design join key is `sample_id), with required `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `condition`, `treatment`, `age`, `sex), `donor_status), `source_metadata), and `cell_type`. Raw members are `MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz`, `E-MTAB-8316.idf.txt`, and `E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt` under `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8316/`. The registry records four verified donor clusters `SA049, SA051, SA104, SA114`, six none/UNC106238 pairs and UNC106238 at 250 micromolar. Average repeated `other_donor_id) contexts within `donor_id) before any exploratory paired comparison. The prepared feature rows are Ensembl identifiers; no assay-specific feature-map is bound, so do not claim gene-symbol or MerTK expression from E-MTAB-8316 without a separately documented annotation join. This source can test whether a compound shift is coherent across donor clusters, but cannot establish MerTK specificity or be joined to E-MTAB-8873 by matching donor strings.

- E-MTAB-8322 remains accessible but is not pooled: prepared `E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) and `E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`). Raw archive members under `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8322/` are per-sample `*.matrix.mtx`, `*.genes.tsv`, `*.barcodes.tsv), plus `E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt). It is macrophage-only, cross-sectional context with 27 samples and 33,694 features; SA149/SA149P relatedness remains unresolved. It can contextualize macrophage states, not estimate FLS communication or provide participant-level validation.

- GSE95588 is source-separated into prepared `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5`) with `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json` (SHA-256 `b324aeb435525132ba231663fd863faae6b676b8301d8ded18f4301a1ee45981`), and prepared `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0`) with `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json` (SHA-256 `54fb86625bd5982310e14feddb17247ea2daca6ffae2e4c67c7528a1776b6bdc`). Required feature maps are `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json` (bound registry spelling: `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json`, SHA-256 `9c3af22472f6bea36ab2e66ab998ca83c944cb0e96f26a811ce5cf5739b80087`) and `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json` (SHA-256 `745f4fb65a6fb643b3edc1a0c6e2d237be38c029e8ade99415061f068a49859a`). Raw archive members are `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz`, `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz`, `samples.soft`, and `series.soft`. Duplicate/date-like feature labels and unresolved donor-to-GSM mappings prohibit target naming or independent validation until the feature map and design are resolved. No E-MTAB or GSE donor ID is a cross-source join key.

The full catalog/registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. All source files are read-only; derived audit, matrices and results belong in this branch.

## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.

# MerTK specificity repair: a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS interaction test

Episode 4 child of candidate-5282fd53c9408f02e8752f4b. This is a planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit or wet-lab experiment was executed here.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important question is unchanged: can a MerTK-associated macrophage state condition rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior in a way that could motivate resolution-restoring therapy for difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA? The strongest inspected evidence is not yet target-specific. [K1] reports an HBEGF+ macrophage–FLS axis with EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness, but it is a different macrophage program. [K2] reports MerTKpos synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an in-vitro FLS repair response. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states are structured within clinically distinct synovial contexts. These observations support a plausible macrophage–FLS mechanism and its clinical importance; they do not establish that a compound-labeled MerTK perturbation changes FLS communication through MerTK.

Hypothesis: in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 endpoint matrix, the recorded inhibitor effect on a prespecified inflammatory FLS program is larger for MerTK/CD206-positive (Mpos) macrophage cocultures than for the matched MerTK/CD206-negative (Mneg) coculture. Formally, for a matched donor/run block k, let delta_g(k) = normalized FLS outcome under macrophage pretreatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor minus the untreated outcome. The specificity observable is the interaction I_g = delta_g(Mpos) - delta_g(Mneg), with the same construction for the eight-gene inflammatory score. A MerTK-conditioned interpretation predicts negative I and coherent negative Mpos deltas; generic activation, compound-wide off-target effects, donor mixture, cell-composition differences or assay artifacts predict a comparable Mneg response, a response that tracks LPS rather than Mpos status, or loss of the effect after donor/QC adjustment.

This is a falsifiable molecular-state hypothesis, not a claim that MerTK blockade improves RA, that MerTK is a direct ligand–receptor mediator, or that the recorded compound is selective. The repair matters clinically because falsely treating an association or off-target drug response as MerTK causality could misdirect a resolution-restoring program, whereas a reproducible state-specific interaction would justify a target-engagement and functional coculture study.

## What is already supported versus unresolved

Supported by the inspected evidence:

- RA synovial macrophage programs can affect fibroblast behavior, including destructive invasiveness [K1].
- MerTK-positive macrophage subsets are associated with remission biology and can induce a fibroblast repair response in a separate in-vitro context [K2].
- Macrophage and fibroblast states can be co-structured by clinically meaningful synovial tissue context [K3].

Unresolved and tested here:

- Whether the E-MTAB-8873 inhibitor contrast is Mpos-specific rather than a generic compound effect.
- Whether the FLS response survives a matched Mneg comparison and donor/contributing-mixture sensitivity.
- Whether the inhibitor response is compatible with generic macrophage activation, as indexed by available LPS-pretreated samples.

Still not established by this experiment:

- MerTK target engagement, compound selectivity, direct binding, ligand identity, intracellular signaling, secreted mediator changes, FLS invasion or matrix damage, tissue localization, flare prediction, treatment response or clinical benefit.
- A temporal transition or persistence mechanism. The design JSONs have no numeric sampling-time field or culture-duration/washout table; the temporal boundary is the recorded terminal endpoint for each sample only.

## Exact data binding and population

Primary source:

- Matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`. It contains the `feature` column and 33 sample columns, with 445 measured feature rows.
- Design: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json`, SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`. It has 33 records and the required keys `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `condition`, `treatment`, `cells`, `donor_status`, `source_metadata`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, and `cell_type`.
- Join key: matrix header sample ID must match design `sample_id) exactly one-to-one. The source audit found `donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model` for all 33 records; these are recorded pseudobulk/coculture samples, not 33 independent donors.
- Raw repository and MAGE-TAB: `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8873/repository.json` and `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt`; SDRF SHA-256 `4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719`. Raw selected archive members include `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz`, the corresponding R2 and R5 Mpos pairs, all recorded preLPS members, and `E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt). The prepared matrix/design are the bound analysis inputs.

Primary Mpos inhibitor pairs, retained only where the same recorded contributing-donor mixture has one untreated and one pre-inhibitor sample:

- R1: `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos` versus `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor`; donor string `SA256A, SA259A).
- R2: `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos` versus `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor`; donor string `SA257A, SA266A).
- R5: `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos` versus `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor`; donor string `SA266A, SA277A`.

The R1 `SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos` record has a conflicting donor representation (`SA256A` versus `SA256A | SA256A, SA260R`) and is excluded from the primary estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves it. The R1 Mneg negative-control pair is `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg` versus `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor`; it is one specificity block, not a replicated Mneg estimate. There are no matched Mneg inhibitor pairs in R2 or R5.

The three mixed-composition controls are `R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg`, `R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg`, and `R5_SA263R_FLS_SA278R_1Mpos_SA277A_3Mneg`. They are secondary composition stress tests, not pure Mpos or Mneg observations. LPS controls include the recorded `*_Mpos_preLPS` and `*_Mneg_preLPS` samples in R1, R2 and R5. LPS is a generic-activation control, not a MerTK perturbation or a substitute for an inactive analog.

The prespecified primary FLS outcome is the standardized mean of these exactly measured targeted rows after normalization, with the direction fixed before fitting:

- `MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end`
- `MMP9|NM_004994.2|Reference_end`
- `IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end`
- `IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end`
- `CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end`
- `CCL2|NM_002982.3|Reference_end`
- `ICAM1|NM_000201.2|Reference_end`
- `TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|Reference_end`

`MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end`, `CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1`, `MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end`, `APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end`, `ADAM17|NM_003183.5|Reference_end`, and both `COL1A1` rows are exploratory context/QC only. The panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; absence from the panel is not a negative result.

Orthogonal source-separated context:

- E-MTAB-8316 matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645`; design `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json`, SHA-256 `ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81`. Raw members are `MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz`, `E-MTAB-8316.idf.txt`, and `E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt` under `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8316/`. The registry records four verified donor clusters `SA049, SA051, SA104, SA114`, six none/UNC106238 pairs and UNC106238 at 250 micromolar. Average repeated `other_donor_id) contexts within `donor_id) before any exploratory paired comparison. The prepared feature rows are Ensembl identifiers; no assay-specific feature-map is bound, so do not claim gene-symbol or MerTK expression from E-MTAB-8316 without a separately documented annotation join. This source can test whether a compound shift is coherent across donor clusters, but cannot establish MerTK specificity or be joined to E-MTAB-8873 by matching donor strings.

- E-MTAB-8322 remains accessible but is not pooled: prepared `E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) and `E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`). Raw archive members under `.../private/data/E-MTAB-8322/` are per-sample `*.matrix.mtx`, `*.genes.tsv`, `*.barcodes.tsv), plus `E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt). It is macrophage-only, cross-sectional context with 27 samples and 33,694 features; SA149/SA149P relatedness remains unresolved. It can contextualize macrophage states, not estimate FLS communication or provide participant-level validation.

- GSE95588 is source-separated into prepared `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5`) with `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json` (SHA-256 `b324aeb435525132ba231663fd863faae6b676b8301d8ded18f4301a1ee45981`), and prepared `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0`) with `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json` (SHA-256 `54fb86625bd5982310e14feddb17247ea2daca6ffae2e4c67c7528a1776b6bdc`). Required feature maps are `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json` (bound registry spelling: `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json`, SHA-256 `9c3af22472f6bea36ab2e66ab998ca83c944cb0e96f26a811ce5cf5739b80087`) and `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json` (SHA-256 `745f4fb65a6fb643b3edc1a0c6e2d237be38c029e8ade99415061f068a49859a`). Raw archive members are `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz`, `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz`, `samples.soft`, and `series.soft`. Duplicate/date-like feature labels and unresolved donor-to-GSM mappings prohibit target naming or independent validation until the feature map and design are resolved. No E-MTAB or GSE donor ID is a cross-source join key.

The full catalog/registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. All source files are read-only; derived audit, matrices and results belong in this branch.

## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.

# UKB-36 repaired proposal: prediagnostic host reserve and competing mortality after colorectal-cancer diagnosis

Status: proposed, not executed. Parent repaired: candidate-d86aa409eb930af6b534886f. Dataset snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`; catalog SHA-256 `6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32`.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The closest inspected CRC prognostic work [K1] reports that functional status and frailty add most for overall and nondisease-specific survival, whereas a model containing tumor stage/location already performs well for CRC-specific outcomes. A prospective multi-cancer cohort [K2] associates prediagnostic frailty with mortality after cancer diagnosis. The unresolved clinical question is narrower and consequential: among people with incident CRC, does objectively measured host reserve before diagnosis identify a specifically larger risk of non-CRC death than CRC death, and does that signal persist when the measurement is separated from diagnosis far enough to reduce occult-cancer reverse causation?

Primary falsifiable hypothesis: in incident CRC, lower prediagnostic reserve, measured at least two years before the CRC diagnosis, is associated with a larger five-year cumulative incidence of non-CRC death than CRC death after diagnosis, after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, smoking, and baseline calendar time. Formally, for a one-standard-deviation lower reserve score R, the primary contrast is
`log(HR_nonCRC) - log(HR_CRC) > 0`
in cause-specific hazard models, with the corresponding non-CRC CIF contrast exceeding the CRC CIF contrast at five years. This is an association/description estimand, not a causal effect of changing grip strength or renal biomarkers.

The strongest evidence already supports only an association between prediagnostic frailty/reserve and later mortality [K2], and the parent’s bounded diagnostic reported 4,732 C18 diagnoses plus 108,481 rows with baseline handgrip, creatinine and cancer-diagnosis fields. No complete cohort fit or effect estimate has been computed here. The proposed experiment tests the unresolved differential endpoint and temporal-boundary claim. It does not test treatment tolerance, stage, recurrence, or a biological mechanism.

The principal rival is cancer-associated decline before diagnosis: [K3] shows that >10% prediagnostic weight loss predicts worse CRC survival and attenuates an apparent obesity-survival association. If the UKB reserve signal is confined to assessments within two years of diagnosis and disappears with a five-year lag, occult disease/timing is more plausible than durable host reserve. Other rivals are age/comorbidity selection, measurement error, and differential CRC stage or treatment. UKB does not contain the required stage/treatment variables, so these rivals can be bounded but not fully separated.

Clinical value: a reproducible prediagnostic signal that is stronger for non-CRC mortality could justify prospective validation of a reserve screen at CRC diagnosis and different survivorship/supportive-care pathways. A null or proximity-only result would prevent overinterpreting grip or laboratory values as a durable reserve phenotype.

## Population, temporal anchors and outcomes

Unit: one participant with one `eid` in the `ukb672073` namespace.

Baseline `b_i`: the date in `53-0.0` (Date of attending assessment centre), using only the initial assessment instance. Participants missing `53-0.0` or with non-parsable dates are excluded. The primary exposure is therefore prediagnostic and cannot use any measurement after the baseline assessment.

CRC diagnosis date `t_i`: among paired columns `40005-k.0` (date of cancer diagnosis) and `40006-k.0` (type of cancer: ICD10), k=0,...,21, select the earliest date after `b_i` whose paired ICD-10 code matches the prespecified colorectal definition `^C(18|19|20)` after trimming and upper-casing. This includes colon (C18), rectosigmoid junction (C19), and rectum (C20); it excludes C00-C17, C21 and non-ICD10 values. Do not treat an unpaired date or a missing code as CRC. Exclude anyone with a CRC code/date on or before baseline. The primary cohort requires `730 <= t_i-b_i < 3653` days (approximately 2 to <10 years); the five-year-lag sensitivity cohort requires `t_i-b_i >= 1826` days. A prespecified timing analysis retains eligible CRC cases with `t_i>b_i` and reports strata 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years; it is not used to redefine the primary cohort.

Cancer-diagnosis dates and codes are registry-derived fields in the frozen source. They are not an adjudicated pathology record. If more than one paired CRC record has the same earliest date, retain one participant and record the tie.

Post-diagnosis time origin: `t_i), not assessment date. Death dates on or before `t_i` are data-quality exclusions, not events.

Competing outcomes, using the underlying primary cause paired by death record in `40001-0.0`/`40001-1.0`:

1. CRC death: cause code matches `^C(18|19|20)`.
2. Non-CRC death: a valid nonmissing ICD-10 cause code that does not match `^C(18|19|20)`.
3. Unknown-cause death: a death date exists but the cause is missing or cannot be parsed.

No death by the administrative boundary is censored. Unknown-cause death remains a third competing event in the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis classifies it as non-CRC and a second sensitivity censors it at death.
